I called the hotel, spoke to the front desk manager. After explaining this all to him he tells me the cpu shows my room was ready, keys were made & I was called all at 445?! I never received a call or VM. Not even the email, that I requested on the kiosk, telling me my room was clean. I was constantly checking 430-630, even spam.He claimed there was nothing that could be done at this point because there weren’t notes made about the resort fee. Didn’t matter if the young lady recalled telling me all this or not (I felt she would). I feel the young lady forgot to call me at 445. When I returned at 630 her face lit up, I figured she just recognized my face from earlier. Now I believe it was because she remembered she NEVER called me. Which is why she agreed to the FREE late check AND waiving the resort fee. NONE of this mattered to the manager tho. He was adamant that I was notified at 445 and returned to check in at 630 just by choice, something they wouldn’t waive resort fee for. I had already planned to spend the money so it’s not about that. I just really don’t appreciate being told by TWO people I’d get a refund, when obviously it hadn’t even been initiated. Then the manager being absolutely no help, just repeated off procedure as if mistakes don’t happen. Especially knowing they were busy w/ ONE agent. Annoyed but not surprised she forgot but I did MY part by verifying with the second agent that the charge would fall off.

allReviews.title: Not a good pool experience - Woman Drill Sargent
allReviews.text: My friend and I were enjoying the Palms Place pool yesterday, when this security woman came over to us and advised we couldn't move the lounge chairs to face the sun. Then she went over to a gentleman who was on his computer with headphones likely taking a meeting temporarily sitting in one of the cabanas and yells at him to get out then when he motioned just a minute she turned on the tv in the cabana and threw the remote at his computer. Someone is taking their job way too seriously! We were uncomfortable being at the pool after that and went over to the Palms pool.

allReviews.title: The pool bar is just a great place for relaxing after work
allReviews.text: The private dining room was awesome for our business meeting.  Excellent service and very quite. I was very pleased with the staff and the attention they paid to our group.The food was very good and the drinks were made to order.

allReviews.title: Main palms casino
allReviews.text: Nice, clean,  and cool designs. Didn't smell like cigarettes and had some great food places. Only issue that i had was the musky smell of the room when we went in. Since it was still early it wasn't to packed

allReviews.title: Great facility and staff
allReviews.text: The facility is pristine. The staff was even better. Donna in housekeeping kept our room immaculate and she was incredibly hospitable. Valet was incredible helpful and friendly. We will definitely come and stay again. Security initiated and quickly got my wife a wheelchair since she is disabled and helped her to the restaurant. Must stay!

allReviews.title: Affordable luxury
allReviews.text: All stainless steel appliances , had a rain shower and jacuzzi soaking tub!  We started on the 35th floor amazing view, especially at night. The skywalk leads you right to the casino and restaurants. Fully equipped gym and amazing pool

allReviews.title: Breathtaking
allReviews.text: I loved every second of my stay. The hotel was so luxurious I have literally never felt like I got so much bang for my back ever. The rooms were amazing the restroom was breathtaking and the view was incredible. Definitely staying again next year as long as the price stays somewhat reasonable.

allReviews.title: The place is a dump. Overpriced and they charge for TOWELS!!!
allReviews.text: I used to stay here all the time when they first opened. The rooms were nice and new and I never had issues. Now I check into a room that's clearly been abused, the lamp is broken, chairs are raggedy, and we called down to get additional towels. They CHARGED US 12 dollars! For 2 extra towels?!?! Are you kidding? Then what is the resort fee they add onto your room for? What am I paying for if I get charged for extra towels! This will be the last time I ever stay here.

allReviews.title: Fabulous
allReviews.text: Hotel is connected to the Palms casino. Be sure to request the Palm Place or the taxi will take you to the Palms casino. We made that mistake and had to drag our luggage a long way to get to the right place. I will say the desk clerk should have called someone to help us old folk. The suite was fabulous. Full kitchen, sitting area and wonderful bathroom. Would stay there again. Since we were only there one night we didn’t get a player card which was a mistake on our part. Off the strip.

allReviews.title: Extremely sub par
allReviews.text: Stayed for a 3 day biz trip. Was majorly disappointed with this location. Service, cleanliness etc... all well below Vegas standards. First off, the decor is just plain bizarre, even for Vegas standards. Room was dusty and dirty. Went to lobby around 7 am one morning. Was told to go to 6th floor. Nothing opened, lady could not have been more rude about it. Room was not even cleaned the second day, despite the room clean light being on literally all day. Would never stay at this dump again.

allReviews.title: Not worth being so far from the strip
allReviews.text: The room was very nice and clean and modern but noisy. We switched our room because the first one had tons of noise from the road. ( it was pretty bad)Second room better- you can still hear traffic but it muffled so it is fine. Each time we went somewhere it was 16$ - 19& cab ride.  Not worth being off the strip since we like to go back to room in between shopping and or gambling to take a break. Not many shops in the hotel and  restaurants  were just ok. Price was pretty good but overall I think we will stay somewhere closer because we dropped $40 on cabs each day but maybe it suits your needs

allReviews.title: Great Anniversary Trip!
allReviews.text: (Booked this stay on Airbnb)This unit was exactly as pictured. The view was spectacular especially at night.Things like paper towels, coffee maker and dishes are all in the cupboards (FYI)The Palms Place is located about 5 minutes from the strip and is a good change of pace after a day of walking up and down the strip. The building is very cozy and with easy access to the Palms Casino with a sky-walk.The front desk staff was welcoming with truly superb customer service.The host, Jacob, was very easy to communicate with and very accommodating.  We would definitely stay at this unit again if we had the opportunity to do so.

allReviews.title: The Palms Place
allReviews.text: This accommodation is so nice and relax with reasonable prices. This is a really good and convienince place (close to down town and shops) for families who wish to visit and spend their holiday in Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: Expensive and bad service
allReviews.text: I visited this place last month when my friend and I decided to eat at the coffee shop. There was a loud, intoxicated person yelling and nobody did anything about it. When the food finally arrived, it was cold and the server seemed to not care. It is amazing how Station Casinos acquired this property and constantly bragged how it was going to be a better place with all the new renovations, however, it seems the only change is the attitudes in this place.

allReviews.title: Excellent off strip option
allReviews.text: First off it’s important to note that this building is mixed use hotel/condos and my wife and I rented from an owner through Airbnb so YMMV in terms of upkeep of the unit and responsiveness of the host to any issues.  Having said that we had an excellent time here and Palms Place has a lot going for it with a few minor drawbacks.The property – Palms Place is part of the Palms complex and is about a mile west of the strip.  It’s not really walking distance, especially since you have to cross the freeway, but an Uber/Lyft is about $10 and will have you to the strip in about 10 minutes.  If you’re renting a car there is ample free parking at Palms Place.  This used to be the case on the strip too but no longer.  We stayed here as a way to avoid the nickel and diming that all the strip hotels now engage in.  Along those lines another major bonus is no obscene resort fee here which can easily add $30-50/night to your stay on the strip.  From the lobby of Palms Place it’s an easy 5 minute walk to the Palms casino which has a variety of great restaurants, a food court, movie theater, show theater, etc.  Palms Place has a little sundries shop in the lobby but of course everything has a high mark up.  There are gas stations and convenience stores within walking distance and Target, Walmart, and grocery stores you could get to via car or rideshare.  There are 2 dispensaries directly across the street from the hotel if you want to partake in some legal (in NV at least) weed or edibles.  I’m not a pool person so I can’t comment on the pool but they do have one.The room – We rented a 1 bedroom suite which has a separate bedroom area that can be closed off by a sliding door.  The bed was comfortable enough but nothing to write home about.  The kitchenette is nice so you can make coffee and eat a simple breakfast in the room without having to trek to the Palms to go to a restaurant.  There’s a fireplace (we didn’t use it) and a deep, jetted tub located by the window which is a great way to relax after a long day and take in the lights of the strip.  The open balcony faced the strip and being a bit to the west it’s cool to be able to see the entire stretch from Mandalay Bay at the south end to Stratosphere and all the way to downtown.  There are 2 bathrooms, great for 2 people to get ready for the night at the same time.  Our unit was starting to show its age a little, some scuffs on the furniture, worn carpet, etc but it was very clean so this was certainly no deal breaker.  The only real annoyance was the lack of outlets near the bed for charging your phone at night.  I ended up pulling the night stands away from the wall a bit and unplugging the alarm clock to have access to an outlet.Service – Check in was quick and easy at the front desk.  Overall we didn’t have much interaction with staff but those we did were friendly.  Since we went through Airbnb the host was upfront that daily housekeeping was optional upon request and we would be charged a fee by the property.  I’m perfectly capable of making my own bed so we never requested this.  We did want to come clean towels to use during a 5 night say but there is a washer dryer in the unit so we just bought a travel size laundry detergent and did a load of towels during our down time in the room.Miscellaneous – If you like BBQ you should go to Mabel’s in the Palms.  The meats and sides were fantastic.  Palms has also been through a major makeover in recent years and the whole property just looks brighter and more inviting than the garish look it had previously.  There are a lot of cool art pieces around the property as well.  As previously mentioned the view at night from the balcony is awesome but the day time view is cool too as we had a great view of the new NFL stadium that the Raiders will move into next season going up.All in all we had a great time here and it will be strong contender to stay at again on our next trip to Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: Loved It Here!
allReviews.text: We rented via Airbnb. Loved this place away from the madness of downtown or the strip. Check in was quick and easy and the staff very pleasant. Stayed on 27th floor in a studio. Great space and had everything we needed. Good balcony space. The bathroom had a huge tub and dual shower heads. We had no issues with noise. Walkway to the Palms Hotel & Casino which allowed us access to bars, restaurants and the food court. Walked to the strip in the morning. A pleasant stroll took 20 minutes. Lyft / Uber was around $8 to $10 depending on where we were going. Highly recommend this place.

allReviews.title: Viva las vegas
allReviews.text: Check in was delayed first due to lateness with cleaning then a maintenance issue in the room we were assigned however the staff was gracious and fixed it for us. The property and rooms are top notch, a quick 25 min walk to the strip or a 8 minute drive, free parking on site, pool still open in November. 24 hr room service, connected to a casino cineplex and performance theatre. Most king units have a balcony but some do not, make sure to clarify with staff if you want one, strip view rooms highly recommended

allReviews.title: Good renovation
allReviews.text: I had not been at the hotel since the change in ownership and I think they have done a good job. They have added many very good new restaurants such as a Bobby Flay and Michael Simon locations. The rooms are simple but nicely done. If you want to go to the Strip it is easy and not expensive especially if you use Lyft or Uber, And the parking is free.

allReviews.title: Nice room but disappointed
allReviews.text: I booked this hotel for November 1st, one night only, because I was coming up for a funeral. I had to leave for Vegas very late because I had an event that night. I arrived very early , about 3or 4am with my husband and 4 month old child. Hours before I called the palms place customer service and explained that I would be traveling very early with an infant and would like to know if early check in was an option for us. I also let the customer service person know that I would be arriving by 3 or 4am and she told me to check with the desk when I arrive and was very rude. If I would have known that their earliest check in was at 12pm, I would have done things differently. Basically, I get there and they say that I can’t check in until 3pm. The lady at the desk never even told me about checking in at 12pm even though I asked. So I ended up paying for a room to stay in for the time we arrived until 11am (a waste of money but I wasn’t going to have my infant sitting in the lobby until 3pm)and had to go back to the front desk to switch keys because we were just going to stay in the same room for our actual reservation time. And that’s when I found out about early check in at 12pm from one of the guys at the front desk.Actual review of the room:Besides that, the room was nice,besides a few stains on the wall. The floor was very quiet , no real complaint about the room. I just wish my experience was better coming in.

allReviews.title: Premium room with excellent view - 51st floor booking with Mike (host)
allReviews.text: We rented using AirBnB (Host is Mike; description is "PH 51 fl. Best Strip View"). 51st floor room with Eastern exposure => sunrise and an amazing view of the strip lit up at night.Unit was in immaculate condition, and was 5 star calibre.Mike (host) was fantastic at communicating.<10 minute drive to Miracle Mile parking at Planet Hollywood, and easy access to Hwy 15 and 215, so great for day trips (we rented a car so this was great).Front desk was very friendly at check-in/check-out. Parking right in front was easy to get every night. Einstein bagels across the road for great morning coffee, bagels and breakfast sandwiches.Pool is great, though a bit crowded from Thurs-Sat.Would definitely stay here again.

allReviews.title: Great Vegas Views and Amenities
allReviews.text: Stephanie's place was great...as expected except for very slight wear and tear on furnishings but otherwise it is as exactly as pictured. The views are spectacular! The front desk staff and bellman were helpful and informed. I was hoping for a walking distance grocery or Walgreens but since there wasn't anything closeby we ordered food and supplies easily from Amazon Prime Now and got our delivery within a 3 hr window. Stephanie was very responsive via email and we felt like we made an excellent choice with her condo. If you're a first-timer to Vegas, the city blocks are long so we weren't really walking distance to anything but Uber was a fine way to travel to restaurants and venues. This condo was a great value considering the huge space and fun little extras such as his and hers robes &  slippers. The bathroom is the bomb with dual shower heads in an oversized glass shower and double sinks. Perfect couples getaway with lots of space. We felt pampered and totally in vacation mode.

allReviews.title: Resort fee rip off
allReviews.text: Massive resort fee even though main pool was closed and we had the pool the size of my uncles  for use.  Food was sub par for massive price.  I’ll stay at the cosmo or Wynn again as we had to go there for the pool party as palms closed theirs already.

allReviews.title: The most amazing balcony
allReviews.text: Absolutely loved it, really couldn't have asked for a better room / view We were in room 302 on the 50th floor and the balcony was soo huge we could see sunset from one side and sunrise from the other ...Amazing We had a kitchen , living room with amazing fire , massive bedroom with bath tub looking onto the strip , great big bathroom with biggest shower ive ever seen.Loved it and would definitely stay againJust a pity the pool was closed on our stay , would have been nice to have been informed beforehand but would definitely stay again

allReviews.title: Good clean hotel
allReviews.text: Palms place hotel and spa affordable clean room. Quiet centrally located! No complaints!! The hotel has a pool, gym, casino and restaurants on site. Friendly staff. I stayed in the 1 bedroom with strip view. Room had a kitchenette and fully stocked fridge.

allReviews.title: Airbnb is the way to go if you want balcony access.
allReviews.text: Palms Place was preferable to me over the Ivory or the Fantasy Tower rooms at Palms. The bathrooms have tubs. There's a kitchenette. It is further removed from the action, but I can live with that. In truth, I value the party being a little off in the distance.Hooray for reviews. I learned via TripAdvisor reviews that balconies don't have access. And that the kitchenettes don't have the niceties to be able to use the kitchen facility: cups etc.Explore your Airbnb options, you can get a better appointed room. I booked the room titled Palms Envy. I was able to enjoy hanging out on a furnished balcony with a view that had friends all taking selfies. I had glassware. And I had a great time. I had the opportunity to visit another couple's room, same room type, booked through the hotel. It's interesting to see the unique touches that owners have put on their condominiums. Even things as simple as some of the furnishings make a difference. Our room was more inviting for hanging with friends.The location absolutely worked for us. We like to kick back and relax. Nearby dispensaries. A chill breakfast at the restaurant by the pool. People watching at the buffet. This absolutely suited our needs.We'll be returning.

allReviews.title: Nice building - great stay
allReviews.text: We stayed for one week. This building is a luxury condo building.  It was built in 2006 so not the newest and shiniest but very nice.  Units are managed by the hotel or other management companies.  We booked our unit through Air BnB.  There are some high end units in the building and many studios that are rented out.  There were a lot of high end luxury vehicles out front.  Because we were here for a week, we wanted a kitchenette that we could make coffee and breakfast.  There is a restaurant on site that over looks the pool and a bar in the lobby (underwhelming).  There is easy access to the casino and main hotel through a walk way on the second floor.  There is a moving sidewalk.  There is a great casino.  Ate at Mabel’s BBQ - very good.  We would take Lyft up to the strip at night.  Roughly $9-10 depending on where you are going.  We parked in the self park open lot across from the entrance.  Always got a spot.  The building gets busy on the weekend with young people.  There were some partiers on Saturday that were screaming and woke us.  It didn’t last long and was not a big deal.  Great stay.

allReviews.title: Double booked !!!!!
allReviews.text: So we booked in August for a unit at Palms place for 2 nights and paid £480 that was non refundable so we were planning our trip around this!! We drove 6 hours from Salt Lake City to be told the “uncontactable owner” could not be contacted and may have simply forgotten that we had booked !!! Utter rubbish. I was turned away - do not book here !!  There is no guarantee your booking will be honoured and I’m now trying to get redress through hotels.com. Thoroughly unprofessional !!!

allReviews.title: Nice but the suite needs work
allReviews.text: Had a suite a the palms place for 4 nights. When we got there the room and bathroom were not clean. We checked in well after check in hours. Took them two møre hours to clean iT and iT still wasnt done very well. The room iT self is Nice But you can tell iT is used as a party hotel. There were shoe prints on the ceiling and most of the handels and Doors were damaged. The bed was very Nice and big and so was the view. During the nights iT was very noisy in the halls from people running around and slamming Doors. Check out was terrible. Very unfriendly woman at the counter.

allReviews.title: Not a care for the patrons
allReviews.text: We were upgraded to the suites in Palm Place. While nice and modern five years ago they were dated and showing wear. The reason for the upgrade was due to us paying a resort fee but with no access to the large pool. They moved us so we could be close to the only other pool on property. Resort fee aside, One of our friends staying in another room had to call front desk about the safe being ripped out of the wall and another about a used condom in a drawer. Imagine that.Back to the suites, our group had 4 of them and we all made a game of finding imprints on the glass of other patrons fruitful endeavors. Cheek marks, face and hand imprints painted a sordid picture. We expect this in Vegas so we can let this go. On our second day, at the pool my wife stepped on glass. Upon telling the bar tender there was a flurry of commotion to get the issue to the manager and security. However, No one checked on my wife, including life guards. It took about 30 minutes to get a bandage from the manager. Whom told us he would have security follow up. To no avail. We did not hear from anyone about the incident.When we returned on the 3rd day, I carefully checked for glass and guess what....I found another piece. This was after their thorough scoping and pool closure from the day before. These pieces were curved and about 3 inches long, fortunately my wife reacted quickly when she felt it. This could have been a quick trip to the hospital. Our bartender was also less than a peach with gratuity included on the pool side service. Maybe they were disappointed about the pool closure the day prior.I’m not sure what the life guards do here. They definitely do not check the pool with any sort of diligence. Maybe place that attitude on the responsible party for the previous days closure and not paying patrons. Personally, while the place was nice and suites were still above average I’m not planning on another visit. They did not really seem to care about us or the experience and certainly did not offer to make any amends.

allReviews.title: SMOKING WEED ALLOWED
allReviews.text: WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING! WARNING!If we have known we would not have stayed at the Palms Place.  Worst night ever, our adjacent room neighbor was smoking marijuana, and the smell was entering our room.The smell of marijuana was making my wife and myself sick.  We made a phone called and informed the front desk and nothing was done.  After waiting for 15 minutes for a response and putting a towel underneath the doorway.  This did not help with the smell of marijuana entering our room.  We had to quickly pack and go to the lobby.  While we were in the lobby, there was no security at the entrance to the elevator.  My wife was so upset, when she saw the front desk manager Sharee Hall, my wife approached Sharee. My wife explained to Sharee of the smell of marijuana.  Sharee said that smoking weed was allowed.  When we heard that smoking marijuana was allowed, we demanded a full refund, and we left the hotel.  WE WILL NEVER STAY HERE AGAIN.

allReviews.title: Excellent and Professional Staff
allReviews.text: From valet parking to check-in to waiters and waitresses in the numerous restaurants and the staff at the Pearl showroom, all were as courteous and professional as possible. Even the housekeepers were professional and gracious. The room was large, comfortable and an excellent sized bathroom as well.

allReviews.title: 33rd Floor
allReviews.text: We stayed in a private owner suite and it needed some work and attention.  Biggest negative was that we could hear the party at KAOS (Palms pool) both day and all three nights.  I would not choose a strip view in the future.We enjoyed being off the strip and loved the pool and restaurants.  Everyone working there was kind and friendly!

allReviews.title: Not a fan.
allReviews.text: Booked two rooms for myself and an employee who was traveling with me for the MAGIC trade show. My husband arrived before us and got us checked in to both rooms. There is a $22 charge a night if you request a high floor, however guests aren't permitted to access the balconies so it was kind of a bust. The t.v. in our room did not work when my husband got there nor did the t.v. in my employee's room work. The comforter on our bed was dirty.. housekeeping never replenished toilet paper... and check out was the worst. One person working the front desk at 11am which is the check out time. Overall, I would say it was just an o.k. experience at an o.k place.

allReviews.title: Dirty, dusty, Nasty
allReviews.text: Housekeeping is awful. After checking in we walked into our suite with someone still in it, claiming to be doing final housekeeping inspection. She left once we walked in. The suite was filthy. The furniture was torn. The room smelled disgusting from an old, dirty shower drain. Housekeeping came back when we called to owner to complain. This was booked through Air Bnb for full disclosure. Don’t go through owners Tony & Beth. They showed no care. They definitely have the Palms personnel care for their property and use their housekeeping services. We showed them how nasty everything was. The floor had not been mopped or vacuumed. The cleaning lady literally took a rag and wet it with just water to “clean” the floor. Needless to say, we couldn’t stay. It was beyond gross. We checked out and went to the strip. Awful experience.

allReviews.title: unwind here after a long flight before going to the strip
allReviews.text: we got one bed suite witch was stunning .so relaxing room had everything like washer dryier massive fridge freezer look up videos of this place like I did and that's what you get I will be back.......

allReviews.title: Palms Place - A great venue!
allReviews.text: I stayed at the Palms Place Hotel on August 3rd and 4th.  The room was upgraded to the 38th floor.  The view was incredible and the customer experience was excellent.  The Palms Place Pool was also a relaxing and comfortable experience.  This is one of the better hotels in Las Vegas. Highly recommended.

allReviews.title: I really enjoy staying at Palms Place
allReviews.text: I stayed here on a Wednesday - Friday.  It was not very busy, service was alright, the bell service was outstanding and very helpful.  The rooms all have TWO large TVs on the wall which is great for sports.  The pool is small but, very nice.  Great bar and you have to check out Drift Spa.  The do charge for EVERYTHING here so, becareful what you touch in the mini bar.  I will do a review on drift spa as well.

allReviews.title: No from me.
allReviews.text: Stayed here for 4 nights in july 20-25.  Almost 1k for a balcony suite.   The balcony was LOCKED, and i was informed by staff it wouldnt be opened for me. Downstairs, at the bar, the bartenders were extremely rude & un-wecoming. Made me feel like i was a hassle to them. I asked for a cup of water and they said "$6", i said id just like some sink tap 2ater in a cup and she said NO. I couldnt believe it.   1 vodka tonic cost me $14 + tip. There was a hidden resort fee of almost $50/day, even tho i didnt use ANY amenities.  They say it covers access to the pool,  wifi, free shuttle service (never saw that one),  a newspaper daily. I didnt get or use 1 of those things. Total rip off imo. Theres nothing to do too,  and its way off the strip, need to taxi everywhere! Not staying here aggain, the room was nice tho, big turkish baths. Front desk during check in was nice too.

allReviews.title: Terrible inside and out
allReviews.text: My husband and I booked room 319 from Expedia not knowing it was through a private owner. The only reason I gave it a one star is because the view was ok.. 10th floor. Upon arrival the front desk was rude and looked as if we were bothering them. Once inside the room was so dirty, chocolate chips left on the floor, windows were not cleaned , why have a balcony if there is no seating and filthy , gum on the floor just bad housekeeping. Broken furniture and lamps. Stained bedding.. Bathroom tub had mold didn’t even try to take a bath . We left and no one cleaned for 2 days. We booked 3 nights only stayed for 2.  Never again !!! Staff rude, room dirty, and expensive for what you get. Not worth your money look elsewhere

allReviews.title: Not a "condo" Experience
allReviews.text: After a tireless search for my housing during a summer work trip I settled on Palms Place.  KITCHEN:I did this primarily for the Kitchen space.  However I was extremely disappointed when I arrived and there was nothing in the kitchen.  NOTHING.  I called room service that brought me a setup which was -1plate-1cup-1 silverware set-1pot-1pan-1 large plastic spoonI had ordered grocery delivery the next day, and of course I Needed to make a 2nd order to get some knives, a cutting board, a can opener, a coffee maker, etc.  Well I had just accepted this but when my first grocery delivery arrived and I asked the bell man if I could use a cart to take my things up he informed me it would cost -$10 fee to use the cart because they were groceries. HUH? So not only did I have to pay the fee for the grocery delivery, I also had to pay a fee once they got delivered and I still tipped the bell man.  I figured it wasn't his fault Palms had a weird policy.  The worst was because I had to do this twice.  THE ROOM: -Blowdryer didn't work -Only 1/3 Televisions worked -Only one Phone worked ***The patio door is locked!  I called to get it opened and they said it is locked for safety?  When my friend had an AirBNB last year they said they were able to have theirs opened but if you book through the hotel you can not?  But that is just speculation.  It was definitely a waste of space.  -The room itself was nice and had a cool view. -Although I was really worried about noise due to the party atmosphere I was only awakened twice on my stay to drunk people screaming and talkingHOTEL: -LOTS of WASTED people, the elevators are a total show-Gym is great-Pool is small and had Super loud music.  I was definitely hoping it would be more low key and all the party people would go to the actual Palms, but it wasn't the worst.  I went once. SERVICE: -when two girlfriends came over for breakfast I called room service and they brought over 2 more set ups right away. -Housekeeping was hit or miss.  I started calling down every day when I left of there were several days when no one came even though I turned my "please service" light on.  Then there were other days I pushed nothing and someone did come and clean.  SO, just to be safe I started calling.  When I did this the service was usually good. Will I stay here again next year, No.  Found an Airbnb for the last part of my stay that was way cheaper and overall felt like much better value.

allReviews.title: Meh
allReviews.text: The good: The studio we rented through Airbnb was clean and comfortable. It was on the 20th floor. We had rented a car and there is free valet in self parking. It’s not on the strip but close enough to not be a big deal. The strip is not exactly walkable anyway.The bad: I came to Vegas to sit by a pool.  I realize I need to change my expectations of the pools in Las Vegas and accept that they are simply another moneymaking opportunity, and not an amenity provided for hotel guests. the music at this was horrible. And seems to be targeted to 18-year-olds people who were not at this pool... wtf.  And because it was incredibly windy, they took down many of the umbrellas. The only shade available were in all of the empty cabanas. Available to rent for $150...Lobby very crowded :(

allReviews.title: Noisey and poor value
allReviews.text: During the period 12 June to 06 July 2019 (23 nights), we visited several west USA National Parks and stayed in 17 different hotels/motels. This provided a unique opportunity to compare and review these establishments.We stayed for 2 nights, 04 & 05 July 2019, room 10318 (10th floor), and paid GBP98.99 plus USD44.22 resort fee, per night.The room was a suite with 1 king size bed, see photos.The main complaint was that loud music originating from the poolside, 4 floors below, could be heard in the room from 0900 to 1900 everyday. Despite requests to customer services, nothing was done to minimise the sound levels.Whilst most facilities and amenities were provided, the basic room layout/design was poor because:•	Glass partition wall between bathroom and bedroom means light in bathroom can be seen at night.•	Common glass door to shower and bath•	No towel rail near to washbasin (one could have been easily added under the washbasin counter)•	Poor location of towel storage rack over WC.In addition, the following were found to be missing:•	No shower gel provided•	No ice machines on each floor although in-room directory states otherwise. Front desk claim that as they provided refrigerators, ice machines were not. Ridiculous excuse!•	No USB charging points•	iPod/radio clock not working•	Damaged furniture (see photo)

allReviews.title: Missed opportunity
allReviews.text: After I had the privilege of aiding save the life of a fellow guest at the Laguna restaurant, I was promptly presented with my bill. I guess they were kind enough to comp my coffee, since it got cold while I was on the floor helping to revive the young man during his massive seizure. My breakfast got cold too, but who really cares. It took a long while for paramedics to arrive on the scene, I was glad to be there. Anyway, not even a proper thank you from management. I guess this is the sign of times in this new era. I was happy to check out earlier, and  comped them my room for the second night. Beds are comfortable, very pleasant suite with sound proof sliding doors to help block the blasting music by the pool.

allReviews.title: FALSE ADVERTISING
allReviews.text:

I paid $1,000.00 to be notified 24hrs before my arrival that they were double booked and canceled my reservation. I had to re-rent another suite through VRBO for the same hotel for $1400.00 for the same 3 night. This time the owner of the suite was the hotel. What hasn't what upset me the was that I now had to pay an additional $400.00. Why would that upset me :/ why would that upset anyone? :? What made it worse was that they weren't giving me the 2 bedroom suite. But they advertise a 2 bedroom suite by pictures and description. Not only am I paying more I'm getting less. But wait you don't know that until they send you an email of your purchase and send you the right picture of your room, The picture on VRBO shows a 2 bedroom suite. IT"S FALSE ADVERTISING!!!! PERIOD!!! VRBO has the nerve to tell me that it wasn't them that its the hotel "the hotel can put any pictures of the room" that they want. NO, THEY CANNOT!!!! allReviews.title: Great value near the strip
allReviews.text: I had a great experience at Palms Place during my recent three night stay. I think it's important to set your expectations that this isn't an ultra luxe hotel such as the Wynn. However, it's an excellent choice for travelers on a budget who are seeking a better than average room with all the frills of an on strip casino but without the price tag.Pros: 1. Free parking 2. Free WiFi 3. Very large rooms with kitchenette. One bedrooms have washer dryer and balconies.4. Beautiful views from all rooms.5. Amazing pool on casino side, but it's a long walk. The palms place pool is mediocre.Cons:1. Cleanliness. Both the lobby and my room needed attention. There were food spills on the fridge, counters needed wiping and the windows were very dirty. That said, housekeeping was amazing when I raised the issue about my room. They came immediately to clean, apologized and offered me a new room. 2. The pool is pretty lame. It's smallish, music is obnoxiously loud and generally uninviting. Walk to the casino pool for a much nicer experience. It's included in your stay.3. Lack of kitchenware. I ordered Uber Eats on two evenings. The kitchen doesn't have anything at all except two glasses and two mugs. No plates, silverware, nada.Again, my three night stay ran me just over $300 including the daily resort fee. I feel I got far more a value! It's not the Mandarin Oriental but it was definitely worth the price. I booked through priceline so not through an independent owner.

allReviews.title: Terrible customer service from front desk
allReviews.text: The hotel is just okay, the staff is not.  They are so rude at the front desk and not accommodating.   I have stayed at many hotels in Las Vegas of all different star levels and have never been treated so rudely.

allReviews.title: Elevated Escape
allReviews.text: Palms Place is where you go to spoil yourself with a spacious suite. The marble bathrooms and decor are beautiful. However, I noticed the bath tub had a few chips in it, so it's not perfect. I enjoyed the elegance here and all the amenities. As a hotel guest, you can enjoy the fitness center and spa for $25 a day. Super relaxing in there! This is also the perfect place to be if you want to go to Kaos- it's about a 5-10 minute walk to Palms. I also love that they have their own food court so you don't need to go too far to get anything- it's all right there!

allReviews.title: Mini Bar/ Rude customer service
allReviews.text: I booked a room for my birthday, mini bar fridge wasn’t working. I not once got told upon check in or anytime after that that there would be a cost for the mini bar if anything was taken out of it because I was like well if the fridge doesn’t work & im paying all this money, might as well take advantage. Repair guy came to “fix” the minifridge, said he couldn’t do anything about it because the compressor wasn’t working. Mind you, I had put a whole cake in there earlier which ended up spoiled btw. Checked out next day.. fast forward a few days I check my bank statement and there is a charge of a little over $500 plus the booking of the room. I call the hotel so i can get an explanation as to why there’s two separate charges on there, staff is extremely rude, saying that if im making it up just because its a financial issue that I couldn’t afford it then I shouldn’t have stayed there, so so rude & unprofessional btw! I asked for her name & she hung up on me. Later that day another person reaches out to me, once again very rude & yet no response whatsoever and also i stated that I wanted to talk to a manager/supervisor to which im still waiting for a callback. I’ve been to many hotels & have traveled & I’ve never gotten a charge like this to my account or gotten treated so poorly. I don’t think I’m ever coming back here. Im still waiting for management to reach out because I truly felt like it’s unfair & all they’re doing is ripping people off!

allReviews.title: Just Ok!!
allReviews.text: Stayed here for 4 nights, you’d do good to read trip advisors warning! Check in was ok BUT beware there is a $40-00 per night extra resort fee on top of your accommodation WHICH was not clear at time of booking and on hind sight if I had known this I would have booked elsewhere as it worked out the same in the end.  I still don’t know what I actually paid for to be honest. One can hardly charges $40-00 resort fee per day just for the use of the pool and WiFi?? Check in staff at the Casino side is pleasant, staff at the Palm Suite side on the contrary is unhelpful and unfriendly. Our room had a balcony, it was locked and when I inquire about a key to open it I was told it’s against rules and we can’t have a key to open it, however, I saw many rooms with their balcony doors open and occupants standing outside. It’s supposedly non smoking rooms, I could not sleep at night as the smell of marijuana was unpleasant and most nights unbearable! Even during the day the smell in the corridors were overwhelming and nauseating!! Rooms are starting to look dated but they are cleaned daily so no concerns there. Use of the pool casino side was limited, they have live entertainment over weekends and it gets so busy you cannot get in - unless you are there when they open. The pool at the Palm Suite building was super crowded and quite small compared to Kaos at the casino. Drinks were super expensive (but to be fair, that’s to be expected). Food is OK, although we hardly dined in the hotel. I can highly recommend the bagel cafe (Einstein Bros) across the road, they open early (06:00) and closes at 16:00 so be sure to get there in time. It’s quite a walk from the strip, there is a lift share (and date I say, might be included in the resort fee??) BUT it doesn’t run in the week so we couldn’t make use of it. You cal UBER, it costs about $13-00. The casino it self is on the quiet side, certainly not as busy as the ones on the Las Vegas Strip. If you fancy catching a movie, book early to ensure you get a good seat (and you beat the rush). I am not sure I’d recommend Palms place to friends and family - i could consider it if they are more open and upfront about the resort fees and if they have better control over the “non smoking” policy - which appears to be non existent at the moment.

allReviews.title: New owners still garbage service
allReviews.text: I used to stay here back in the day when the maloofs owned the property and it was nice. The condos are well done and very easy access. Understandably the maloofs met some hard times in 2008-09 as well the condo owners. Rooms and service upkeep was not not tenable during the recession. Finally came back after 8-9 years as the Fertitas took over the property. It was clean this time as it was not the last few times but you still get nickel and dimed for something so simple as a cork screw. It is supposed to be a condo but no plates or silverware. I called over to room service for a corkscrew and the women told me I had to pay $5 for it. I justed wanted to use it but ok. Then it shows up and it’s $10 as they added a $5 delivery fee for an item that should have been in the room. Bad business.

allReviews.title: April 23-26  2019
allReviews.text: This is a condo hotel. (CONDO AT PALMS PLACE )  Don't expect to received a good service like a hotel .They don't have a professional cleaner to clean the room.  .The aircon grill  are dirty, ( I got an allergy ) Lots of molds,dust and rust  in the bathrooms and roomsDark lighting at night, Hotel and room is not accessible. DESPITE MY COMPLAIN , MANAGER RHEA  DID" NOTHING."

allReviews.title: Great room ....
allReviews.text: Stayed here for a week on honeymoon....room was amazing on 36th floor perfectly cleaned everyday and extremely friendly front desk However so expensive to drink 2 beers were most expensive we found in Vegas $26 for two as they add $4 gratuity on no matter what ! For opening a bottle ! I prefer to pay a tip when I have received a service meant we didn’t spend much time at pool

allReviews.title: Great Room
allReviews.text: Great room and room service. I really never left the room except to eat at the buffet. I had a suite which was very roomy. Room service prices were comparable to surrounding hotels. Overall, I would definitely stay again!

allReviews.title: Awesome place for New Years!
allReviews.text: We stayed here for New Years to see the fire works on the strip.  The room was very nicely appointed. Marble was used all over the bathroom with large walk in shower with kind of a weird tub.  There is a single basin in the bathroom but it has plenty of counter space for two people.  The no smoking / no casino feature means no smokey smell on you and your clothes.  That is a real plus.  There are Gaggenau fixtures in the kitchen whcih makes the place feel rally luxe.  Pay extra for high floor strip view.  It is worth it if you can afford it / are going to be in the room.  The rooms have great strip views from a distance.  Make sure you get a room with a balcony that opens.  Not all do.

allReviews.title: Best hotel off the strip
allReviews.text: Tired to grab a room week ahead and was receiving offers of $199 and up. I finally called Palms after hearing the pool was newly renovated. After speaking with hotel reservations, I received a room for $50 Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. The hotel has been newly renovated and so was their old buffet. Only down side was the resort fees were as much as the cost of the room, but small price to pay for nice hotel (close to the strip). I would recommend this palace anytime.

allReviews.title: Very Disappointing
allReviews.text: We were really excited for our first trip to Vegas to stay at the Palms Place. Upon arrival we were greeted with a very friendly staff and they quickly checked us in. Upon getting to the room we were very disappointed to find the room very old and dated. Scratch marks all over the walls, dirty floors, dirt between the walls and the bed,Dirty under the sink and inside where they expect you to use ice from. For the price we paid to stay here I feel we could have stayed in a much newer nicer hotel that would have not looked so worn out. The rooms really need a facelift. Also keep in mind that the balcony doors are locked and they won’t give you a key to them, which I find ridiculous! Why did we come to Vegas and book a room on the 50th floor only not to have access to the balcony. Another thing to note, we waited over 2Hours for a wine opener to be brought to our room which cost $10. The garbage disposal stopped working after the first day. Be prepared to bring your own cups and silverware, they onlyProvide you with 2 glasses and no forks or spoons. Overall if you are not used to staying in nicer places then these things might not bother you, but honestly I have stayed in nicer Holiday Inn’s which were cleaner. Be cautious when booking this place and ask lots of questions about the condition of your room. Take a look at my pictures.

allReviews.title: Great deals with nice rooms, some details could use more attention though.
allReviews.text: This property has amazing rates for what you get. We were in a 1 bedroom, 1 1/2 bath strip view suite, managed by a outside property company - but you check in through the front desk like any other room. We had a kitchen with a four burner glasstop stove, a microwave, a fridge & freezer, and a dishwasher. Our room also included a washer & dryer, fireplace, TWO balconies, a big fold out couch, tons of seating, and wrap around windows. Having a small kitchen and two bathrooms are a lifesaver for a family, but we don't always want to stay at a non-resort/extended stay property, so having these available at a location like Palms Place is fantastic. Our room here was definitely larger, with more upgraded features and finishes, than our room at The Signature (which also offers multi-room suites with kitchens). I'll be exhaustively nitpicky here, for honesty's sake. You should know what you're getting for your money. The sheer size and amenities within the room make it a great value. I couldn't, however, give it a full 5 stars, because there were some details that could use a little attention. The two balconies were great to have, but they had ZERO furniture on them, not even those cheesy white plastic chairs, so it made them a lot less usable. The finishes were upgraded, but some look dated, while others have just suffered their fair share of wear and tear and need replacing or refurbishing. The giant tub was great to have, but a few times the jets randomly turned on by themselves, and it was a bit startling since in an empty tub that's loud, and it was sudden. All three bathroom sinks dripped from the cold water handle when they were on, even if only using the hot water. One of the toilets ran (quietly, but still wasteful) unless you jiggled the handle, the icemaker in the freezer was pretty noisy at times (opening and shutting the freezer door made the sound stop), a few lightbulbs were out, and the bedroom was lacking bedside outlets for charging your devices near you overnight. The two TV's are pretty small by today's standards, especially for this size room, and don't accommodate guests hooking up computers/gaming systems/ etc. very easily, while most hotels and have entered the modern age and make this a simple task with media centers and easily accessible hdmi inputs. The super limited amount of channels and no PPV options also greatly limited their use, as it was hard to find anything anybody wanted to actually watch while we were in the room. The TV system's guide also only showed the networks, not what was playing on them at the time, so by the time you made it through the channels looking to see what was actually on right then and chose something, you had missed at least the first few minutes of it. A guide that showed what was playing and not just what channel was what number would have been nice. Also, the bedroom tv would randomly glitch and black out for a few seconds here and there, and once entirely lost sound for nearly 10 minutes, throughout all channels, before we turned it off, waited a minute or two and turned it back on, which fixed it, but it was annoying when you're in the middle of watching something. On a positive note, the free wifi was plenty to accommodate a family of four, including streaming. I was confused at first because it was made to sound like the basic (free) wifi limited the number of devices that could connect, and offered very low-speed connections. I even upgraded ($9.99/day premium package) to start off with, but once that expired and we tried the basic there was no discernable difference and we were not limited on the amount of devices that could connect (we had 8 connected). It streamed just fine too. I recommend trying the basic first to see if it meets your needs before assuming you need to upgrade. The pool (next door at the Palms, but included for Palms Place guests) left much to be desired, but Mabel's BBQ (also, next door at the Palms) was the best BBQ I've ever eaten. The staff was friendly, the hotel is nicely quiet, no rowdy crowds anywhere, and it doesn't reek of cigarette smoke. Free parking, including free valet (gratuity is obviously up to you, but you SHOULD tip if you use it) is a nice change from the MGM properties that have found yet another way to squeeze an additional $15 a day out of their guests.  Overall I would definitely stay here again, in the same room, and I would also recommend it to others. Just have realistic expectations. It's not perfect, and it's not the best suite on the strip, but hotel rooms are NEVER as shiny and immaculate as they seem in pictures, and it's a hell of a deal for what you get.

allReviews.title: Mini bar
allReviews.text: Like i said I didn’t take anything inside the mini bar. I bring my own stuff like soda, water, etc. and when I checked out they charged me $59 to my card they claiming i take on their mini bar... when i check out probably the housekeeping thought all the thing on the trash like soda etc are came from the mini bar, like i said im not stupid. I bring my own stuff like that... they are steeling my money...

allReviews.title: Multi-Million dollar Penthouse ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING!!! I have tones of videos and photos!!!
allReviews.text: I went to the Palms Place for my Bachelorette party April 30th- May 4th 2019. I rented the penthouse on the 56th floor Room 304 Taking the elevator up to our suite -waking out to the 56th floor, there is significant water damage, and the smell of mold slaps you in the face, my sinus and eyes were bothered pretty bad everything I walked through the hallway.Opening the suite, the chairs were scattered, the set up just didn’t make any sense. The glass table is broken we were too afraid to eat on the table and it collapse! Not to mention the glass itself was cracked, didn’t want to cut our hands and legs up. The furniture is ripped, holes in the pillows, holes in the chairs, there is food on the wall where a BIG picture should be hung up. Cigarette burns in the floor and master bed night stand. The bedroom furniture in both the master bedroom and spare bedroom has banged up bad also in the guest room bathroom the light bulbs on one side were burnt out and there is water damage behind the mirror (pretty sure wall will need replaced- made a video you have to watch it),The wood trimming around the penthouse is either scuffed really bad or there’s entire wooden pieces missing, I stubbed the front of my toes on a loose wood piece with the nail JUST missing my foot. Master bedroom has a broken chair and wooden planks stuffed in the closet, master bathroom- railing on the one side where you hand the towels was broken off! Looking at the ceilings there’s water damage I’m pretty sure the owner is going to have to gut the place out. There was NO hairdryer, actually was a hassle to even get one! 4 girls in this room and no hairdryer??? We tried calling the front desk and they couldn’t be bothered it took us over half hour to get a dryer.The owner threw the hairdryer at my girl friend and gave her a nasty look... awesome. Kitchen doesn’t have any knives so we couldn’t cook anything while we stayed there. The deck- the couch, someone broke it as you’ll see in the picture I post, the condition of the upholstery was stained by white residue, the pool itself the jets didn’t work.EVERYTHING the ceiling, the furniture must go! I am absolutely appalled in the condition of the penthouse of all things?? We asked for a different suite and we were told we couldn’t... I booked this unit months in advance and the service we all got it’s pathetic and quite embarrassing to be totally honest. Shame on the owner of this building!!!** Strip View Suites manages this penthouse, I don’t know how the condition of this place slipped through the cracks??? My bachelorette trip was ruined this penthouse DOES NOT look like what it does in pictures!!!

allReviews.title: A quiet oasis
allReviews.text: This is my new favorite place to stay in Las Vegas. The pool is relaxing with good people to hang out with. The rooms are huge and we had a view of the mountains in the distance off our balcony which was a pleasant surprise. I can't say many bad things about palms place. Well there's a thick aroma of perfume in the lobby which was a bit aggressive. Self park was close to the door. Kaos night club is a must to check out if you're in to that nightlife vibe. I will definitely be staying at Palms Place on my next visit. Oh dogs are allowed too which is nice.

allReviews.title: Great Location and Rooms
allReviews.text: We stayed one night at the beginning of our trip then 2 nights at the end of our trip.  Both stays were great.  Our rooms were fantastic.  Our one-night room did have a pungent odor of cigarettes, which was a challenge because all our stuff smelled like smoke after check out.  We stayed in different rooms on each stay and both had wonderful views of the strip.  One complaint, which I do not know if the hotel can control, is the overwhelming smell of marijuana in the hall ways leading to the rooms and the elevator areas.  That, along with the cigarette stench on our 1st night, are the only things that kept me from giving 5 stars.  We will absolutely return to this hotel in the future.

allReviews.title: They refused to allow us to check in after we drove 4 hours to get there
allReviews.text: I book 5 nights at the Palms Place.  When we got there, the receptionist refused to take my credit card for a security deposit.  He said they do not take Greendot bank cards.  I told him that was the only credit card I had on me.  I have never had a problem using this card before and used it at the Wynn last year with no issues.  He said it had to be a card from a bank other than Greendot or Paypal.  I told him nowhere on the webpage does it say that and there was no mention of that in my booking confirmation email.  The website only says a $100/day security deposit is required, with no specific exclusions on certain credit cards.  I asked if I could pay the $500 in cash instead.  He said no, they don't take cash.  I offered to pay for the entire stay in cash and put down $1000 in cash for the security deposit.  He refused.  A manager was called.  She also refused to allow us to check in.  Another manager was called and he told me the same thing, that he could actually swipe my card and it would go through, but it was against their policy so he couldn't do it.  At this point our vacation was pretty much ruined and I was ready to drive back home.  My wife asked if they could recommend us a hotel that would take our card.  It turns out 90% of hotels in Las Vegas do take my card OR cash, including the Wynn which is now our go-to hotel.

allReviews.title: Money scamming
allReviews.text: This hotel is a joke. The staff are useless, do not bother booking. Or add an extra 500 dollars onto the price. They charge you for everything including a bottle opener. A hotel of this price shouldn't be charging for a bottle opener I've traveled the world and I've never experienced that. Also, they don't tell you that they charge you for every drink you MOVE AROUND in the fridge. We made room for our items and got charged for items we didn't consume. AMEX is still investigating the situation so hopefully I get my money back but if you paid cash or debit you'd be screwed. We were there with 15 people for a wedding and no one had any idea about the fridge charging their cards. YOU MUST INFORM YOUR CUSTOMERS. money scammers.

allReviews.title: Not the best experience
allReviews.text: Easy check in for 1 of our rooms but a mess for the other 2 rooms. As British on holiday we book a room and turn up and expect to get a room at reception right? This did not happen. We were not aware the rooms booked had nothing to do with the hotel and had to call the owner of the room!!! He had to meet us at the hotel to take us to the room. A lot of stress but room 2 sorted. Room 3 on the other had was cancelled without notice and it was another private owner room. Our group was stressed at this point. No contact prior to say so. We got told that we would have been contacted via email and phone. We were on holiday and did not have access to email and phones. Now back in the uk emails were checked and answer phone checked and no such emails or calls. Our only option by hotels.com was to stay in a different hotel ( splitting up our family) or pay over $1000 for an available room in the Palms. Welcome to the Palms. We stayed in Palms Place. The rooms we had were clean and spacious and great views of the strip. The staff were great from reception, valet, casino waitresses, bar staff and security. The casino was a good size and a mix of old and new machines. Pleanty of eating spots in the hotel and the A.Y.C.E buffet was great value and good selection. The hotel is a long walk from the strip so a taxi is recommended or the bus to Ceasers Palace. We learned the hard way!!!. We could not use the pool the first day as staff told us  it had broken glass in from a party and needed drained. It was to windy the rest of the stay. The bad start of our stay always played on our minds and our group could not relax properly. We stayed here on the launch weekend of kaos nightclub and saw how badly it was handled. People there will know what i mean. Thank you Hotels.com for ruining our stay.Thank you Palms we will visit again.

allReviews.title: Palms Place Penthouse Floor57 Heated Infinity Pool
allReviews.text: We booked the Penthouse on the 57th floor w/infinity pool at the Palms Place. On the second night, we phoned the front desk to report a noise disturbance next door and they did nothing.  By 3 am we physically went downstairs to the front desk and reported the disturbance again, since the initial request was ignored.  The rental had no drinking glasses. So, we went to the bar for glasses and provided 8 plastic cups.  We reached out to the property manager twice, who advised they were in the movies and would get some drinking glasses to the unit in 30 minutes. The experience and description was misleading.  For the price, the only thing you are paying for at this property is the view.

allReviews.title: STAY AWAY- CAMERAS in Room
allReviews.text: Worst place ever, stay suck, 21/2 hour wait to get in room. Girls weekend reserved in 2 bd with pool strip view end up being a one bedroom no pool not facing strip penthouse on 11 floor.. dirty room,staff rude unprofessional and to say a wireless camera facing the sitting tub in room.. no help to solve why it was there or who’s it was and what it recorded.my friend way too nice I wanted to file a police report end result it was booked thru home away from home.. regardless the hotel treats you like outcast that don’t belong.. worst hotel stay ever.STAY AWAY ROOM 11301..I have video but it I can’t load sorry..

allReviews.title: Amazing room!
allReviews.text: Clean & a great view! Had a blast, and was very impressed with room. Only complaints would be the pool area (pool bar not open yet, this time of year & pool would have been better heated. Wish the ice maker worked, but we made due with convenient store across the street.

allReviews.title: Great hotel awesone views
allReviews.text: Fantastic staff, front desk through bell and valet service. Free parking and fast bellman service. Good restaurant on premices and short skyway power sidewalks to Palms Casino. Ez uber Lyft pick up location just outside of valet loop. Views of mountains for sunsets just as good as city skyline side. Corner 1 br. Suites are super large but if you rent through hotel directly no balcony access. Try Air BNB for best value and patio access...

allReviews.title: Book through Airbnb!
allReviews.text: Booked through Airbnb and felt I got a good deal. No extra resort fees. The room was large and had all the amenities needed. The pool is nice, as is the fitness room. I left my book in the fitness room and when I called the front desk that evening, they confirmed they had it in the lost and found. Enjoyed the free parking for our rental car as well. If course staying on the strip in a nicer hotel would be great, but also much more expensive. This place was fine and a short Uber to the strip when needed.

allReviews.title: 3 nights @ palms place - overcharged
allReviews.text: This resort was clean but some parts under construction . Our check in took a long time and our keys didn’t work at first , then back to the front counter for new keys again they didn’t work so we had to again go down and we were put into a different room . The room was clean with a nice view of the strip . Biggest complaint is the hotel charging me for mini bar consumption  when we never took anything from  the mini bar . They put a few extra charges to my credit card 1 week after my stay including a higher resort fee than was stated and the mini bar charge that we didn’t use . After contacting the hotel they are saying nothing can be done because something was consumed for mini bar . 100% we did not use our mini bar . Unless the maid were thirsty ?? Also our room was only cleaned 2 out of three days , hair dyer didn’t work and we needed to request more towels . Resort fee was high 44$ per night and obviously the service we received was subpar . Over all I would not recommend the palms due to they overcharging , high resort fee and poor cleaning service . Be advised to watch your credit card bill for overcharges  for this hotel .

allReviews.title: Honeymoon suite
allReviews.text: Booked the suite for our wedding Night. The staff was kind and helpful. Could do an early checkin (had to pay extra for this Ofcourse). The suite was nice and the view was mindblowing. Unfortunately some things was missing. The bathtub didn’t work properly. No robes or glasses. The lighting system was tricky to use. But overall, happy with the place. The valet guys were Very kind and helpful at this hotel.

allReviews.title: Worth checking out
allReviews.text: Keep in mind that you can book directly with Palms Place but that many rooms are managed by their owners thru Airbnb.  You'll want to explore both options for best rate.My sister and I have stayed here twice now and each time she's snagged a great deal for SUITES.  Two entire walls of windows with patio, large bathrooms, full gourmet kitchen and the last suite had a huge tub!Palms place has proven to be a quiet property yet you can easily walk to the Palms for dining, gaming & entertainment.Worth the time to shop for great deals.  The rooms are slightly dated but the value of space is definitely worth the trip.

allReviews.title: Disappointed!!
allReviews.text: My husband and I booked this hotel Sunday night to celebrate our one-year anniversary being married. We were in town early and wanted to see if we can check-in and we were told no so we waited until 3:45 to check-in. We were told our room was not ready. Okay, we waited until 4pm. Our room should be ready by 4pm to check in, BUT...we were told to wait AGAIN! We waited until 4:30pm to check-in. Terribly disappointed with this hotel. Would not stay here again.We were too disappointed and upset. Wasted our time waiting.

allReviews.title: Never Again
allReviews.text: I should have followed my first mind not to stay here after reading so many other bad reviews. But my brother lives in Vegas and gifted me this reservation and paid all the ridiculous “resort fees” so I decided to stay. And still hated it, for all the reasons outlined in the other bad reviews. At first glance everything is lovely. It’s set back from the Strip, the lobby is lovely, at first glance the rooms are spacious and modern...but then. My sheets hadn’t been changed—visible dirt on the pillowcases & they smelled. Either staff took a nap in that room before I got there or the sheets just hadn’t been changed from the previous guest. There was hair (that wasn’t mine) everywhere. The floor had a huge stain that looked & smelled like something that had come out of both ends. The jacuzzi tub was dirty and the jets didn’t work. Everything was dusty and dirty. When I approached Cassandra at the front desk and asked “can you help me with a problem with my room?” she had the nerve to say “Depends...” *Eye Roll* When the room was cleaned they used so much bleach it gave me a headache. Just poor management and housekeeping all the way around. The final dealbreaker for me was that despite this room having a full kitchen with appliances and utensils, they don’t include a wine opener. Why? So they can charge customers $6.49 for one. It’s really ridiculous how counterintuitive their “customer service” is. Won’t be back.

allReviews.title: Beware of hidden prices
allReviews.text: The room was nice, and a great tub and shower. We didn’t utilize the kitchen, other than the refrigerator. We did request the kitchen set-up (pots, pans etc.) in case we decided to purchase food.  Walkable distance to the strip - providing no health issues. They do have a walkway to the casino, but some of the area is under construction, so not a pleasant walk or feeling of security. They do have a free parking lot if you rent a car, which is nice. HOWEVER, upon checking out, they informed us of a resort fee of $42 per night, and an internet access fee of $9.99. We had NO recourse to debate or decline payment.  Therefore, we will NEVER stay here again!!!

allReviews.title: WOULD NOT RECOMMEND
allReviews.text: We stayed for 3 nights in early February in a studio suite in Palms Place (adjacent to the hotel/casino).  Pros: The room was large and included some kitchen facilities (2 burner stove, microwave).  Bathroom featured amenities, but no bathrobes.  Walkable distance from the strip.  Lovely spa and gym.Cons:  The Palms Place tower seems to have been built as condos, the rooms are rented out as hotel rooms but are actually for sale - this was not disclosed when we booked the room.Service, attention to detail and follow up were non existent. Part of Palms Place is under renovation, we had to walk through the garage to get to the main hotel/casino.  Most serious:  when the reservation was made, we were immediately billed on our credit card.  Consequently, we were charged for an additional night, the Palms billing department refused to refund the $.  Also, there is an almost $50 resort fee per night which is fine if you are using the spa/gym but makes the room not that much of a bargain.   Check out is 11am- we asked for 12n and were refused.

allReviews.title: Very comfortable
allReviews.text: This hotel room was very comfortable. It had a ton of space and is very modern. I really liked the kitchen area and the bathrooms have ample storage space. The only drawback is that the casino was under construction, so some areas were closed. Overall, I would return here

allReviews.title: Great hotel for the price
allReviews.text: Great price and just a little off the strip. Nice giant suite. Nice view of the mountains from our room. We asked for hypo-allergenic pillows and they came and traded out all bedding to meet the need. Super customer service and attention to detail. Only draw back to the suite was there no refrigerator other than the one stocked to purchase from. Only draw back to the casino was the perfumey smell spray they use to cover the smoke smell.

allReviews.title: In desperate need of a renovation
allReviews.text: We booked two "studio" suites for a 1-night stay.  Upon check-in around 2:30-3pm, there was only a single person working the entire front desk.  The check-in wait was 15 minutes, and then the check-in process was anything but quick and smooth.  Our request for a high floor was accommodated, but when we asked for adjacent rooms, they could only give us rooms on opposite sides of the corridor...and on the extreme opposite ends of our floor.  That was not a good start.  Then one set of the card keys that we were provided during check-in did not open 1 of the 2 rooms we were assigned.  When I went back to the front desk 10 minutes later...still the sole employee working the front desk with a line of people waiting to check in.  When I tried to motion to him that the keys he gave me would not allow us in our room, he shrugged his shoulders and said we would have to wait back in the long line.  Twenty additional minutes later, he finally gave us a new set of card keys.  Oh by the way, it wouldn't hurt if their front desk employees would smile for a change versus the stern no-nonsense look we were greeted with both times.  Our rooms (both on the 36th floor) 303 and 316 were not very clean.  I have attached photos I took of a non-working lock of the bathroom sliding door.  Apparently, Las Vegas is a hard water area, and from the amount of visible calcium deposits that were built up and clogging our hand held shower head, apparently the housekeeping department has not considered cleaning or dunking these shower heads in a glass of the cleaning solution "CLR" to remove the lime and hard water deposits.  My white end table to the left of the bed had burn marks from what looked like maybe a past cigarette smoker.  The dark brown colored fake woodgrain  front credenza at the foot of the bed had all these visible scratches.  Before going to bed, I was stepping into bed.  My barefeet was touching the dark stained wood laminate flooring that covers the bed and mattress floor area...when my foot felt a very sticky material on the floor.  I don't know what "it" was, but it apparently had been thete for awhile, and somehow never noticed or cleaned up my housekeeping.  When I bent down to see what it was, I found what was half way exposed from underneath the bed, a used paper towel or tissue.  As I pulled it out to dispose of it, to my utter surprise and disgust, was a used condom!  Is the housekeeping staff at this place that lazy and not actually spending time to "clean" these rooms??  The studio suites come equipped with microwave, refrigerator, stove top, and dishwasher.  Although I didn't have a reason to use these appliances, when I pulled out the drawer of the dishwasher, i found it all wirh lots of lime and calcium deposits.  Once again, does the housekeeping ever drop one of those dishwasher "self cleaning" tablets to clense and disinfect their dishwashers once or twice a year??  When we arrived back at the hotel around 11:30pm from a show we attended earlier that evening, we were greeted at the front door entrance with a very loud exchange of some people that arrived from a ride sharing car service, with a heated exchange of non-stop screaming profanities and vulagarities for all to hear regarding the driver being horrible...and supposedly had run into or damaged a parking pole while dropping off his customers at this hotel.  Where was the hotel's onsite  security to break this up before fists were about to fly?  My family felt very uncomfortable, and thought we were staying at a hotel of thugs and overly drunken patrons.  It ended our evening on a very scary note.  Our room's so-called air conditioning never pumped cold air into our room, just room temperature air.  Versus, the other room in our party (36-316), way down on the other end of the floor's hallway, had cool air piped into their floor constantly.  Although the price for the 1-night's stay was less expensive than anything comparable on the strip, I can't recommend this property.  I took the photos to validate my concerns, and hope that the property's management will take my review serious enough to warrant some long overdue changes in their current policies.

allReviews.title: Over Priced Resort
allReviews.text: I called the hotel for an early check in the night prior to my stay and they said if a room was available at the time it would be a $25+ tax fee. No problem. I get to the hotel, check in at 9am and go to the room. It was FILTHY! There was a hand print on the mirror above the bed, the floors had dried stuff on it, the couch had stains on it and the wood paneling behind the couch had visible stuff splattered on it. After calling the front desk and behind on hold for 10min, I went down and asked for another room, which was frustrating that the 2 agents at the desk were not busy but I was on hold without answer. They did not have one and said they would send housekeeping up. I asked if there was anything they could do - reduce the $44 resort fee, waive the early check in and the gal said no just housekeeping. Not the customer service I am experienced to receiving from any Las Vegas property, being a local at a now locals casino I would have thought they'd have treated me better. Housekeeping did come up and changed my bed linens and did a throughout job as I sat there and made sure of it.

allReviews.title: Do not stay here!
allReviews.text: It is rare that I write a review that is negative but this place is a rip off! I flew in and arrived at the hotel to be treated by 2 nice ladies at the front desk who were very nice and helpful (they are the only good thing about the experience). When we got to our rooms they smelled of smoke pretty badly. We decided to try and tough it out since we were so tired from traveling all day. After tossing and turning for hours we decided early in the am to just check out and find another hotel. Now the real issues begin, When we explained that we wanted to leave the hotel they told us they wouldn’t refund any money and that we had to pay for the stay since we didn’t make the cancellation deadlines... I’m not sure I saw smelly, smoky rooms as the room type we reserved... hmmmm I should look closer next time I guess🤷🏽‍♂️. Needless to say we asked for a manager. When he arrived and heard our story we got the same reply, you’ll have to pay for the room. We told him that this is ridiculous but we were willing to pay for the one night we stayed. When the cc bill arrived we were charged for 3 of the 4 nights of the rooms and I was also charged hotel fees, room surcharges and etc for the entire stay! I have been disputing these charges ever since and. The hotel is fighting giving me a refund. If you want horrible customer service, smelly and smoky rooms, your time wasted if you decide to speak to management, well then you have found the perfect place to stay!!!!!!! I am open to discuss this issue with senior management if they choose to reach out.

allReviews.title: Entire staff needs lessons in hospitality, property is disappointing
allReviews.text: I am just sitting down after a 45 minute journey from check in to my room. This disaster started with the Front Desk at the Palms. If there are separate lobbies for Palms versus Palms Place, wouldn't it be smart to email guests that information in advance so they know where to tell taxis to drop them? I have 4 heavy bags for a week's stay and am nearly 7 MONTHS PREGNANT. I check in and, upon inquiring about how far the walk is to my room, Karmel tells me it's 5 minutes. It is not. No offer to get a belman, nothing so I figure I'll just step up and do it myself since it's super late. It's about 10-15 minutes for me to drag my heavy bags along the carpeted floor (much harder to wheel luggage) through a desolate and potentially unsafe parking garage with hardly any signage to the far away Palms Place. I finally get there and have to search for that lobby. I explain how unhappy I am about this treatment (or lack thereof) to the front desk manager and she barely bats an eye. My back is now full of shooting pain and my neck stiff from dragging everything, doesn't seem to care. I ask nicely if they can offer some kind of massage for my awful journey on property... denied! All they do is get me a bellman who doesn't even offer to lift up my suitcase and set it up on the rack!To top it all off, the furniture is tattered and the room is tired and rudiementary.A complete disappointment and I feel that I received grossly negligent services.

allReviews.title: Surprise? Yes! Nice? No!!
allReviews.text: I had not stayed at Palms Place for more than four years. My memories were good ones in general. New ownership, Station Casinos,  have cut corners and belt-tightened to the point of failing the customer badly.  I cannot recommend staying here. When I visit Las Vegas, I always try to have a kitchen to avoid going out for breakfast and snacks. So I gravitate towards places like Palms Place and Hilton Grand Vacations Club. Problems started with check-in. 4:00 PM check-in time and there are only two agents on duty. Far too long of a wait. The beautiful kitchen was in a great state of disrepair.
