The ice maker on the Sub Zero refrigerator had been removed and ice was nowhere to be found. No kitchen utensils were provided. When I requested full kitchen materials, I was provided two plates, two glasses, two forks, two knives and two spoons. So I would not be entertaining in my room. The faucet in the kitchen sink was loose as was the handle on the refrigerator that was stocked with items to buy.  Many other things in the room showed great wear. This room had not been updated since before my last visit in 2014. Housekeeping was horrendous. I was completely ignored and had to call two of my four days to get someone to come. I did without the other two days. Room service had a habit of not picking up their phone either. Add to this the inconvenient location (unless you want to purchase some marijuana - there are two dispensaries directly across the street), you are better off spending a few dollars more and staying at one of the Hilton grand Vacations Clubs, like the Elara. And finally, I have now been home for 36 hours and am STILL waiting for them to E-mail me my final bill, which they could not provide me with at checkout. I had this hotel booked for another trip in June but I cancelled today and booked elsewhere.

allReviews.title: Nice Surprise
allReviews.text: I had not been to The Palms in years. I had a business trip coming up and they had a pretty good rate so I thought I would try them even though the last time I was there I did not think much of the place. I arrived and much has changed. For the better. Totally redone since I’ve been there. The place is great. Nice casino. Great sports book. A movie theatre. Concert Venue. Great night club. Great spa and workout facilities. Many restaurants. Great bar. Rooms are great. I had a long week and wanted to see about a room upgrade. The great girl at the counter and gave me very reasonable price to upgrade to s suite. Needless to say my upgraded room was incredible. Everything was five star. Highly recommend staying here. Just off the strip so you get a much better deal on a similar type room on the strip.

allReviews.title: Average hotel, too far off the strip, dated rooms
allReviews.text: We stayed here one night because we were in town for a show and the show was at The Palms Casino Resort.  The Palms Place hotel is part of the resort but is a separate tower on the same grounds.  The great thing about the Palms Place is that you do not have to walk through a seedy casino to get places in the tower.   It does feel more like a boutique hotel - small lobby area and no casino however it has kind of a "miami vice" feel - dated and definitely too dark.  There was only 2 agents checking in guests so it took about 20 minutes plus it was 5 PM and we were told the housekeepers were still vacuuming so we had to take a room on a much lower floor (10) than we had originally booked (53). Our room was a 1 bedroom suite but there was just a half wall separating the bedroom from the living room which was not disclosed to us at booking.  There was a kitchen but it looked like it had taken a beating and needed some help.  The room was very dark and in the bedroom the lamps which were the only light source were entirely encased in big pink transparent bubbles so our room was pink.  Not a good look.  The worst part was the street noise - it was horrendously loud.  Seriously, felt like we were next to the interstate - cars at all house, 3 police cars blasting sirens, 1 fire engine, 1 car alarm for about 15 minutes, etc - all between midnight and 7.  VERY LOUD - must get a room at least above the 20th floor.We didn't like the dining options at the resort and wanted to try Trevi at Caesar's (a great choice).  It was very busy in town so we decided to walk as we could see Caesar's  from The Palms - took 30 minutes each way.  Most areas off the strip are pretty seedy and this area was no exception - passed over the 15 on a covered bridge and had to dodge a few people in sleeping bags.....So in all, OK hotel, too far off the strip, too loud at low rooms, dated rooms, and average dining options.

allReviews.title: No full disclosure
allReviews.text: Standard rooms were OK.  We didn't expect to get a sun tan in December but wanted to sit the pool and there wasn't one.   You had to walk about ten minutes to the sister resort past construction/construction workers  and temporary walls, into a garage and up and down elevators and through the spa.  All that being said the pool at the other resort was beautiful, but its hours were erratic and some days not open at all with no prior notice.  The Palms also sent us on this same walk to the use the Gym.   All of this should have been explained at booking, nothing was said.  Nothing was said at check in either, so it was a nasty surprise to find this out on your own.   Also there was a big construction site outside so there will not be any pool there anytime soon.   There were also other restaurants that were not open.

allReviews.title: Away from the STRIP
allReviews.text: If your are a regular LAS VEGAS visitor like myself, The Palms Place HI-Rise Suites is the place to STAY.  Go to AIRBNB and look for TYLER and rent his condo. It's quite..bed is comfortable, clean, and you will love the bathroom. This place has it's own kitchen area with refrigerator, stove, microwave etc.  He's a great host and communicates timely. It's very modern, and the images shown on AIRBNB is exactly how it looks in person. Price is affordable and fees are decent. Unlike these other hotels on the strip, they charge for resort fee, parking, etc.  This location does not charge for parking and it's very convenient. Even if you don't have a vehicle, there's taxi, lyft, uber...  The major plus for me, is that once you park your car,, you go into the hotel.. walk in the elevator ... not like the other places you go through the stress of having to find what tower your elevator is on.. etc.. LIKE I said.. I recommend this place, but most return VEGAS visitors.. understands why it's best to say away from the strip from time to time..

allReviews.title: Quiet Off Strip Place To Stay
allReviews.text: If you are looking for a Vegas hotel that has more of a boutique feel this a great spot.  Hotel is off strip so you will have to walk or drive over to the strip.  This is the residential wing of the Palms Hotel so it's a lot quieter and calmer then some of the other hotel casinos.  The room was spacious with a kitchenette and an amazing bathroom.  Limited amenities, no mini bar.  Only one lobby bar that closes early but your attached to the Palm Hotel and Casino so you can just walk over there for the action.  Definitely would stay again.

allReviews.title: Wsop 18
allReviews.text: I highly recommended this place for long poker stays in Vegas.. try booking a place here well in advance through Air BnB or contact them directly.. ordering room service everyday can be a bit unhealthy for us for I recommend getting your own groceries or ordering in , eating out basically mixing it up.. there’s a food court in the hotel as well... can always watch a movie in the In-Hotel Theatre next to the food court on the casino floor... this is just a u turn away from rio... I walked it once when there was no sun otherwise too hot to walk it , I recommend Uber over renting a car as you can waste a lot of time finding parking!! Perfect place to stay if you’re on the grind for poker or any other sport which  requires you to spend a long time in Vegas! oh and that view <3 I wish I could stay here forever! #Fingerscrossed

allReviews.title: Tired Hotel with Exorbitant Resort Fee
allReviews.text: We stayed for one night in a studio suite. Room was reasonable but pretty tired, the toilet roll was half pulled out of the wall and the thermostat for the heater/cooler was broken so the room was either too cold or ridiculously hot. Pool is nice but not heated enough during winter to make it swimmable. My main gripe with the property is the $45 resort fee, the highest resort fee I've ever seen in my life. I was initially okay with paying it because I thought it included a shuttle to/from The Strip, but The Palms canceled the free shuttle a few months before our stay so for the resort fee you basically get...nothing. Will never go back, the resort fee is pure extortion.

allReviews.title: Beautiful View of City
allReviews.text: I really enjoyed my stay here at Palms Place Hotel & Spa. The room & accommodations were spectacular. The hotel staff were very pleasant and welcoming. Everything we asked of them they made sure was done. We stayed December 12/4-12/7. The suite was immaculate. very nice. I Loved it! The only two things I had issues with were that we couldn't open the balconies (due to some Air B&B policy or something), and the dryer DID NOT work.

allReviews.title: Great Place To Stay
allReviews.text: spent 2 days we hired a suite which was amazing up to date decor fully fitted kitchen with oven, fridge, dishwasher, washing machine. Very plush apartment we were on 52nd floor amazing views. Separate toilet, large bathroom with walk in shower, toilet and sink. Large flatscreen tv in lounge. Bed very comfortable further large flatscreen tv in bedroom and also free standing bathHighly recommended

allReviews.title: Dirty rooms and the most terrible service
allReviews.text: I don't even know where to begin with our terrible experience at this hotel. We had to switch room over and over again because how dirty they are. The first one had a dirty mop hanging on the ceiling, and fridge smelt. We moved to the second room and there was a coffee and sugar all over the floor. Kitchen sink was very dirty. Okay at that point we were so tired we just asked them to clean the room. The manager that night was nice (and the only nice one) who waived the resort fee for us. Then in the middle of night, the AC unit is not working and my husband could barely breath. We called the service in the morning, no one came to fix in the entire day while we were out. We had to call again and they sent someone at 10Pm and started to make noise. We had a young baby in the room and he started to spray toxic gas without even asking us if it's okay for the baby. Then the AC broke again in the middle of the room, and released toxic gas. The next day after much back and forth with manager, they move us to a bigger room. but instead of making it convenient for us, they forced us to move everything before we head out to start our day. We have a baby with lots of stuff. The move took more than an hour and pretty much ruined our last day there at vegas. Then we moved to the new room, there was an used soap in the shower. We spoke with manager the next day. They said there is nothing they can do.  The place is so dirty and disgusting. The windows are full of dust. the services are terrible. We spoke with four managers. other than very first one, I forgot his name but he was the tall and skinny one - very polite and the best one. everyone else was unhelpful. The  female manager Sharee was the worst. lots of attitude. rude and unprofessional. One of the worst of service individuals i have met (and I have traveled to 54 countries and stayed at thousands of hotels). She was upset because we were telling her the issues we encounter. She was upset because she had to do her job to make her customers happy.

allReviews.title: A nice place to stay
allReviews.text: At the end of a grand tour of California I decided to stop and relax at one final location. I have stayed in many places in Las Vegas over the years but this was the first time at The PALMS.I was wanting to have the ability to stay somewhere that provided a variety of food outlets but also allow me the opportunity to look after myself, food wise if i wished. Although the suite seemed to offer this, upon inspection I found that the galley was not fully equipped. The top fridge was full of hotel goodies and worked on, a take it from the unit and you are charged basis, even if you put it back!The room temperature control was difficult to fathom.However, overall a great place to stay, even though there was a lot of construction taking place. Once complete I'm sure it'll be even better.Scotch restaurant was excellent.

allReviews.title: 36th floor stunning views
allReviews.text: 3 nights stay here as part of a road trip across USA.Easy check in and polite staff.Room on 36th floor with glass balcony and fantastic view over the strip.Lovely apartment room with kitchen, sofa , comfortable bed and bathroom.Good location to visit strip. Good facilities nearby with shops/ restaurants.Parking onsite was free.Loved our stay here.highly recommend

allReviews.title: Dark and dreary
allReviews.text: The staff here are all very friendly, Our room was extremely dark and dreary. Makes it almost impossible to get any work done, or even to put on makeup. The tile floor was grimmy in the kitchen area and the red bed stand lamp was really dusty. We have stayed here before and deal with the darkness of the room, however the cleanliness is a deal breaker for me in the room.  Way way overpriced for what you get

allReviews.title: Stayed for my Birthday !
allReviews.text: Stayed in room 18102Although they are still doing construction, (they were on our last visit as well) we had no complaints.  Sad the pool is not available but anxious to see the new pool when It is all complete.  Staff from the Valet, Baggage men and front desk staff all were very pleasant.  Are room was clean and comfortable. Large and spacious bathroom. We have not checked out the spa but hope to on a future visit.  Nice newly decorated front desk and bar called Unknown in Lobby area.  We will stay again in the future and really looking forward to see everything when the construction is done.

allReviews.title: Great space!
allReviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at Palms Place. The location is as awesome as the condo. The host was very responsive when we had a problem connecting to the internet. We were there for a concert at the Palms which is next door.....very convenient.

allReviews.title: Odd stay and not in a good way
allReviews.text: An unusual set up in that these "studio apartments" may or may not be privately owned.Pro: quiet entrance and lobby with no need to trek far and through a casino.Room is a good size with small kitchen, large jetted tub and separate shower.Cons: $44 per night "resort fee". Resort fee charges continue to outage me, especially in a season where there is no possibility of pool or other resort type use.  Also room is pretty shabby, which is really obvious given the contemporary decor.  Couch cushions are very faded and bed cushions are stained with what is clearly hair oils.Finally, rooms were advertised as with balcony, but doors are permanently locked so balcony is not accessible.To sum up: not worth the close to $300 a night total. For that money (we stayed sat and sun) you can find a much nicer room without the stains.

allReviews.title: Looks Good But Only On The Surface
allReviews.text: Our tub we leaking sewer gas into the room. The shower backed up into the bathroom when draining the tub. It absolutely reeked the whole time. The refrigerator in our room was broken so they put a tiny mini fridge in there. No apologies from the staff and they treat you like dirt. I spent my time and my gambling money at the Rio instead. This place left a horrible taste in my mouth that won't soon be forgotten.

allReviews.title: 2 nights visit to Las Vagas
allReviews.text: The room is very large and complete in every sense of it.Very comfortable bed.  The facilities provided in the hotel room are nice. The hotel staff were courteous and friendly. The hotel was undergoing renovation and yet the inconvenience was minimal.

allReviews.title: Out Standing
allReviews.text: We have friends who stay here all the time so it was a no brainer not to visit, the staff cant do enough for you and the rooms are spotless, even the cleaners were nice to talk too.The place was undergoing a major re fit while we were there but apart from areas being boarded up for work it was fine, look for to a re visit

allReviews.title: Excellent Hotel
allReviews.text: We recommend this place, we celebrate marriage anniversary, excellent buffet, nice room with strip view, very nice staff, excellent pool, excellent spa , we recommend this place to couple , we enjoyed it, romantic place. Thank you.

allReviews.title: Weekend treat to see the rock band Blink 182
allReviews.text: What a perfect location to stay at whilst watching Blink 182 at the Pearl theatre at the next door Palms hotel resort.Check in at 2pm on a Friday afternoon was easy and quick, I asked for a high floor and strip facing. Got room 50310 on the 50th floor.Perfect and a fabulous view of the strip.The room was immaculate , large and everything is good order. I could not have asked for more.Pool area is small but for the amount of people around it on a Friday afternoon it was fine.I would recommend this hotel if you don’t mind been of the strip a little and is perfect for when all the renovations to the Palms resort next doo are complete, I believe it is to have the biggest pool area in Vegas when finished by the middle of next year.Now that’s worth a visit.Well done the Palms Place Hotel and Spa.

allReviews.title: Good off strip option Shuttlebus discontinued
allReviews.text: 2nd time we have stayed here and value for money is amazing.We had a corner room, room 26102 which had amazing views.best bit is the cleanliness of the rooms, they are immaculate.Building works are still ongoing so only 1 pool which suited us.Only issue is that they have stopped their free shuttle bus from palms to Caesar’s forum shops.Not really a dealbreaker Feel like they are going to go more upmarket a fed think maybe their prices will change too

allReviews.title: Don’t waste your money
allReviews.text: We booked a three night stay with the Palms, which has turned out to be a huge disappointment.  Our room, unknown to us, was privately owned.  So when I called down to the front desk to get a couple extra pillows and a coffee cup for in the morning, I was informed that they couldn’t help with a cup and that it was going to cost me $5.00 a day per pillow.  To make things worse the towels were so hard and dingy in color that I wouldn’t even wash my dogs with them.  So unless you want to pay $250.00 a day for a room without room service, only one coffee cup, and ugly hard towels, don’t book a night at the Palms

allReviews.title: Awesome room
allReviews.text: I found this room on Airbnb looking for a space close to the Strip, but with a balcony. It was more than I could have imagine. The balcony was very spacious and had an amazing view of the entire Strip. The mini-apartment was extremely modern and well maintained. Parking was free and easy and the staff in the lobby were polite and helpful, even though they don’t offer all hotel amenities like daily room cleaning. The price was great for all you get. The bathroom was our favorite!

allReviews.title: Amazing place
allReviews.text: I have stayed at Palms Place with my husband for over a week at the end of July/beginning of August 2018. We had a 1 bedroom suite on the 26th floor with two massive balconies and a view of the whole Strip. It was close enough to go by Uber (about 6 usd one way trip) but far enough to be away from all the noise. The suite was very modern, with plenty of room, huge bathroom with double shower and a bath in the bedroom! Kitchen lacked few utensils- no knives or other silverware, few pans/pots etc. and the fireplace did not work but we did not mind. Very comfortable bed, great water pressure and a touch of luxury by the furnishings. During the weekend we had to present the room key to enter the premises. Very nice gym and pool- a little quieter than the ones on the Strip but we still had lots of fun (like everywhere no food/drinks allowed to the pool site) and never had a problem finding the sun bed. SPA was on a rather expensive side so we decided not to use it. There is a little shop in the lobby should you need any essentials. Across the street plenty of shopping options (walkable but in the summer heat I do not advise that). All in all, we had a great stay!

allReviews.title: Rooms are comfy and cozy
allReviews.text: I booked a room here for training. These rooms were large and spacious. The staff was friendly. Rooms had 3 TVs hot tub shower stove fridge and appliances and a large couch. Casino was fun. Movie theater was cool.

allReviews.title: Needs adjustment
allReviews.text: Not sure if we caught the staff during a bad time or not but they were very hateful and resentful towards us from the moment we arrived to the moment we left and we haven’t even said one word to anyone yet. The 1 bedroom suite was beautiful and nice, clean and very comfortable, which didn’t match the level of service of the staff. I understand that there were loud and arrogant people staying there too but we all shouldn’t be treated in the same way since we were not rude from the beginning and for the entire duration. Upon check out, we were advised that we were being charged for use of the mini bar for excessive amounts of spirits which we did not touch at all as the mini bar is hooked up with an alarm and charges will be automatically charged to your credit card. We were out most of the time anyway! Again, the staff were dry and disinterested. Zero f*cks were given.

allReviews.title: Vegas boys
allReviews.text: If nice hotel the valet parking is excellent and the room the are ok it’s  nice location next to the palm casino the restaurant on the 6 floor is nice nice view to the city if you go to party is perfect

allReviews.title: Not the best
allReviews.text: Stayed for 2 nights and got charged £120  for resort fee which was in the end use of Wi-Fi. Hotel going through building work which resulted in certain parts being closed off.  Bathroom lock was broken in room as well as dirty windows in room.

allReviews.title: Horrible Run Down Hotel
allReviews.text: This property is a timeshare property and is very rundown and they don’t tell you About extra costs like $15 per day per device for WiFi that has normal speed. The surrounding area isn’t too great as well. In the entire kitchenette there was ONE cup. The carpet, bathroom is not up to mark. It feels like I was staying at a cheap motel !!! For just a slight price increase, get the room at mgm signature you will NOT regret it.

allReviews.title: Palms Place Review
allReviews.text: The room was not cleaned properly with a lot of dust on the floor and table tops not wiped down.  Did not clean the room after my first night there.  They were great about it and sent someone up right away.  Their resort fee which is supposed to cover internet was the worst I've ever seen.  Cant even check your email with their resort internet.  Or, they have an upgrade feature with better speed.  Isn't that what the resort fee covers? Descent internet?  Always looking to get extra money out of you.  Also had to walk pretty far to get to the casino and the food area.

allReviews.title: Great place to stay
allReviews.text: The Palms place is a fun cool place to stay..that comes with a great dining/ kitchen area!  It is great if you like take out or left overs.  The rooms were clean and the service was solid.  Only hang up is the location..its definitely a long walk to the strip.

allReviews.title: Good Stay - Room for Improvement
allReviews.text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel. Our 1st time in Vegas. We liked that it wasn't right on the strip but just under $10 Uber ride away. The front desk and doorbell staff could have been friendlier I found. The room was a studio size so plenty of room for unpacking. Clean and tidy.The bed was comfortable although I wish the bed was a little higher, in fact, all the furniture felt low in height. Perhaps it was the modern look they were going for. We had a nice view of the strip from our room and the beautiful desert mountains. The bathroom was spacious and comfortable. The pool was very nice and not too crowded and good hot tub. The service poolside was probably better than the front desk frankly. Gabrielle who waited on us was very nice and accommodating. Out of 5 stars I would give it 4.

allReviews.title: Had a great stay
allReviews.text: My trip to the Palms Place didn't initially go as planned. I checked into my Airbnb without any issues. When I arrived at the room I found a leak by the balcony door and there was mold growing on the wall. I reported this to Airbnb and to hotel management. I couldn;t contact the host due to it being after hours. I called Palms Place Management and spoke with Natalie. She advised she would send someone up to the room to take a look. She also noted that since it was a private residence she wouldn't be able to move me, which I understood.  Literally felt like 2 minutes and an engineer came in. He took some photos and said he would talk to the manager. (The engineer was very professional and helpful) About 5 minutes after that I was shocked by the response. Natalie called and apologized and said she would be moving me to a new room due to the health hazard of the mold in the room. I'm very thankful as this wasn't the responsibility of Palms Place, however, they stepped up and did the right thing. For that, I'm very grateful.

allReviews.title: DOG attacked us in elevator!!!!!!!
allReviews.text: Just had the most terrifying experience today while staying at the palm place hotel. My partner and I were taking the elevator up to our room and a German Shepard off the leash ran into the elevator and then a second German Sheppard came in the elevator. The  door closes,  then the damn dogs attacks my partner. The hotel has done nothing to rectify to situation. They can't tell us who the person is and the person is still roaming the hotel with his dogs. Haven't heard one apology, they haven't offered any type of remedy. They also said they aren't liable. Dogs attach strangers at this hotel...beware!!!!

allReviews.title: Nice stay on the 51st floor of the 47 story Palms Place
allReviews.text: Palms Place Hotel and Spa is a decent, somewhat sterile, condo hotel resort off the strip.  For significantly less money than a strip resort, you can stay in a large room with a kitchenette and great bathroom.  It is also much less hectic.  I stayed on the "51st" floor of Palms Place but there are no floors from 40-49.  There are only 47 floors.  I wonder if the owners of the condos from 50 to 56 floors knew they were actually purchasing units on the 40 to 46th floors?  The view from my room was also obscured by the fact that I couldn't access the balcony.  The balconies now sit empty and dirty. (If you book a room through "Palms Place Hotel and Spa", you can't open the balcony for liability reasons now.  I was told some AIrBnB owners may still allow guest to open the balcony.)  The room had nice wood accents but the lack of art work on any of the walls in the room or anywhere in the hotel made the place feel dull.  Room entertainment is poor with few tv channel options, a tiny Bluetooth radio and no local magazines like Las Vegas Weekly or Where to let you know what's happening in town.  The spa was a highlight of my stay.  I purchased a reasonable spa day pass and enjoyed the various sweat rooms and bathes as well as the well equipped gym. Another highlight was being off the strip and having access to local non-touristy businesses within a 5 to 10 minute walk from the hotel.  I enjoyed the new Bourbon Street Bar and Grill directly across the street from the hotel.  It's closer than any of the restaurants in the Palms Casino.  There is a small grocery and 2 dispensaries across the street as well.  (Wish that balcony door opened!)  I enjoyed Da Lat Vietnamese food and a bone-crushing 90 minute deep tissue massage at the Avalon Day Spa within walking distance.  Other than the movie theater, there is absolutely nothing that distinguishes the Palm Place Casino from any other of the many better casinos in Vegas.  It was mostly empty the weekend I stayed there.  A large construction project didn't make the stay any better. Overall, a good but not great stay.

allReviews.title: HOLY MOLY THE HAMMAM CHANGED MY DEFINITION OF RELAXATION!
allReviews.text: Staying at Palms place was absolutely the ideal Las Vegas spot to stay! I will never stay anywhere else! YES it was THAT AMAZING! Palms Place was more than accommodating. I had to leave the hotel I was at for business and had time to kill before I could officially check-in. They let me leave my bags at the front while I went for my scheduled massage at Drift Spa and the 5-star treatment started the minute I signed in! I cannot recommend staying here enough. The use of the spa and pool facilities were only outdone but the 1 bedroom corner suite and view of the strip at night! Seriously an outstanding time!!

allReviews.title: Superb Place to Stay
allReviews.text: I stayed in a privately owned apartment on the 53rd floor. The place was clean and the area was great. It was 1.3 miles to Caesar’s Palace. The pool area was awesome and the Palms Casino offered food and a movie theater. There was a place across the street to get coffee and breakfast items. Overall I would highly recommend staying here.

allReviews.title: Las Vegas Break
allReviews.text: What a fantastic hotel. Michael on reception welcomed us for check in and we were treated as celebs. What a really helpful gentleman. Thanks Michael. We stayed in an executive suite on the fantasy floor, wow. Spotless, beds so comfortable. It was difficult to leave the room.😀. Of course we tried a spot of gambling, didn’t win anything, but never mind, great fun. Everyone at the bars so friendly and chatty. We had drinks at the entertainment bar on the ground floor. The guys and ladies were brilliant. Great service. Breakfast choice was great and reasonably priced. The waitress and waiters were really helpful in our choices. The courtesy bus every 15 minutes to the strip was great. Wished we had stayed longer. Thank you all at the Palms.

allReviews.title: Value Hotel for Las Vegas Repeaters.
allReviews.text: Stayed here in this hotel for 3 times (3 nights 4 days each,) last several years. I am always impressed by the bell men and valet parking staff here. We always bring 10 pieces of the luggage, bags and ice cooler box with us, but bell man always unload all of the belongings out of the car, then take it to the room all by himself. Valet parking men are always fast, and they all know how to get to the certain destination. As you see all the websites about this place, some part condos are belonging to hotel, and others belonging to the individual owners. (But, hotel does not tell you, which one is which..）So, some rooms are maintained really well, and some are not, so you need to make sure to check every corner of the room, once you enter your room.  There are no casino in Palms Place, so you have to walk to Palms Hotel, about 5 minite walk from Palms Place. AYCE Buffet was cheap, and fairly good, and the servers were very friendly and nice in any restaurant s in Palms Hotel. You also need to know that the shuttle bus is available for guests, but you can catch it on Palms Hotel only, and Every 30 minutes, and last shuttle bus from Caesars Palace Hotel is 8:00 pm, so you want to have Uber ready on your cell phone, as always. Palms Place has nice gym facilities, spa, and outdoor pool, and I always use gym and pool whenever I visit here. Distance between Palms Hotel and Palms Place to walk, and accessing from Palms Hotel to Las Vegas main strip are issues... Otherwise, nothing wrong with this place, and I always love to stay here.

allReviews.title: A gem off the strip
allReviews.text: We stayed for 3 days at their elegant condos, very modern with excellent views of the strip, the pool area is ver small ( roof top) but has a very interest shape an accommodations, sauna and spa area very nice and up to date in pleasure!, the restaurant and casino area are far away from the condos..., if you don’t like to walk this can be a nightmare!, great restaurants and the ghost restaurant at the rooftop is for many a one time experience as it is very expensive..., couples can spend 200-500 in a few hours easy!!!

allReviews.title: August Get away!
allReviews.text: Had a great 4 night stay at Palms Place. We typically book the studio suites, but decided to go bigger this tine.The 1 bedroom suite was perfect for the 4 of us. The staff had the cribs ready and waiting in the room when we checked in. The bellhop that loaded everything from the car to the room, in 1 trip, was the true MVP of our stay. And trust me, with twins we don't travel light anymore.The room itself had a full sized fridge and freezer, cermaic top stove, dishwasher and a lockable mini bar. There was also a 4 person table attached to the cooking area which gave us plenty of room. The front room was very comfortable with their couch setup and thick glass coffee table. There is a balony coming off the front room.The bedroom was vary spacious with a super comfortable king bed. Tons of storage space in both nightstands and the wall closets. Try the soak tub in the bedroom with the curtains open at night. The view of Vegas from here is unbeatable in my opinion. There is another balcony off the bedroom.The bathroom has a large walk-in shower with overhead water. There are also wall shower heads on opposite walls. His and Hers sinks were also convenient. A huge plus for us was the in unit washer and dryer. For a longer stay, it was very helpful!We had an exceptional experience with all the staff at the property. The valets in particular were very professional and impressive with remembering us as we were in and out throughout the day.We visited the pool right after it opened with our little girls. We beat the crowds so they were able to at around for an hour or so. Very clean pool without eye burning chemicals or chemical odors.Lastly, I highly recommend trying the AYCE Buffet inside the Palms itself. Very good buffet at cheap prices for what is offered.

allReviews.title: Run Down
allReviews.text: Unfortunately, this was a huge disappointment. Pics looked great - and it probably was at some point - but the room was very run down and beat up. Damage to almost all the furniture, holes in the drapes, not cleaned. Fridge barely worked. Huge let down. Add in the location away from the strip and it is tough to recommend this place. Checked out after one night. I understand now why the rate was reasonable - not cheap - but reasonable. Booking pics are deceiving.

allReviews.title: Excellent Value For Money But Shop Around For Rooms Here
allReviews.text: I stayed here twice in July in a normal apartment and in a suite. Whilst the normal apartment was nice the suite was a significant upgrade for a moderate increase in price. The location is a short £10 or $13 Uber from the airport which is handy after a long flight. It has to be said check in can be a bit chaotic and busy if you’ve booked via another site and not the hotel directly but nothing to be of major concern. I booked the first room via Air Bnb and the 2nd via Home Away & cut around £250 in costs that way as opposed to the Palms prices directly but it did delay my check in by around 40 minutes. There’s a $100 security deposit to be paid that is promptly returned on check out. (I paid cash so received the cash straightaway, I’m not sure the process for card) It’s a nice and welcome break that you step in to a hotel entrance and deal with everything as a hotel initially as opposed to having to wade through a casino entrance and the hub of activity there like some other hotels. There’s a walkway that can connect you to the casino on the 2nd floor. Getting to and from the strip there is a shuttle that will take you to Cesar’s Palace every 15 minutes but this only runs until 8pm, after that it will be a case of £6 or $8 Uber or Lyft service. I highly recommend both for cheap and efficient ways to get around as opposed to the Taxi’s.The normal room (20303) was pleasant and had kitchen facilities with a stocked ice freezer. The bathroom had a shower and Jacuzzi bath tub. The bed was king sized and had a balcony with a shop and distant desert view. The corner suite (17302) was exceptional with a separate bedroom facility, two balconies offering views of the strip as well as the city and desert. A television in the front room, bedroom and bathroom and a fireplace. The staff varied and I had some great experiences and some less so, however even with my negative experience the hotel afforded me significant hotel credit which then paid for all my food whilst staying. The casino itself is vibrant and vast with plenty to offer and even a cinema. There’s a whole food court with a buffet, McDonald's and several other food outlets. The hotel has its own pool facilities which are manned by a very good and professional team of staff so that you feel safe and your belongings secure. All in all it truly was a great place to stay and I would happily return.

allReviews.title: Quiet, large room with a view
allReviews.text: Stay here with the family in late June 2018. Got room on the 26th floor. Quiet place away from the busy Strip. Free parking is a plus and the entire hotel is Non-smoking. Don't confuse this with the Palms casino resort which is a smoking facility. We would stay here a again for sure to make use of the kitchenette area.

allReviews.title: Stayed at Palms Place via Airbnb and was charged for a service animal?
allReviews.text: I've stayed at this hotel many times. In fact, a good friend of mine owns property here so it's always nice to be in th same location as him when I come to visit. Imagine my surprise when I used Airbnb to book my stay for a work conference for the week and the host asked for a cleaning fee for a service animal. Apparently, they are unaware of the laws regarding such. Even after I explained the laws, the booking company which lists through Airbnb, insisted on me paying the fee, regardless of the law. The add insult to injury, when I showed for my stay the room had not been reserved and I had to deal with multiple parties to get resolution. It took multiple hours to get my name added to the room so that I could check-in. I know most of this is not the Palms fault, it's the result of what I like to call the "inception factor", a dream within a dream within a dream, or more specifically a listing within a listing within a listing. However, there is just too many parties involved to provide a positive experience. When a guest has an issue they have no idea who to call or get help from. There is a lot of blame shifting. If it was my hotel I personally wouldn't want guests to have a poor experience when things are out of my control. I would rather control the guest experience end to end.The other issue I had was with internet. For some odd reason the first day I was charged 6 times for internet!?! How does that even happen? Basic internet is free!As for the room and such. It was nice. Same as I am used to everytime I have stayed at Palms Place. Staff are all nice. Shared spaces are clean. Parking is located next to the tower if you want to park yourself or valet is available and I think it's free. Just make sure to tip.

allReviews.title: One of best affordable place for suite with full size kitchen
allReviews.text: Very cheap minutes a way from the strip. On Monday they have a $5/6 dollar movie theater inside the casino. They have a yummy bbq buffet best in Vegas for very cheap price like $12 a person for club members. A nice co Ed spa and separate section. Very nice modern contemporary room and bathroom with jet tub and standing shower for cheap

allReviews.title: Clean but cheap
allReviews.text: This was a clean hotel room. It looks fancy on the outside but was pretty cheap on the inside. We had no complaints but it was definitely not luxury like advertised. The bed was fine but not amazing. The amenities were sufficient but we have stayed at better places. Clean but ok.

allReviews.title: BEST PLACE TO STAY FOR WORK OR PLAY
allReviews.text: I can prepare my own food if I choose, hang out by a fairly private pool, not walk through noise or smoke, go away from the strip without the traffic issues, take a lyft to the strip for next to nothing and the suites are sweeeeet!  Good restaruant on this side and the lounge bar is great for a nightcap - the front desk is amazing - I have made mistakes booking or needed things and they are authentically helpful.

allReviews.title: Off the strip with lots of room
allReviews.text: The room was great for the price. I would definitely recommend Palms Place, especially if you have a large group. I booked via Airbnb, and stayed in a suite, which is good for 4 - 6 people. It was beautiful, modern, comfortable bed, full kitchen, washer/dryer, 1.5 baths, wrap around balcony. It is off the strip, so you will need to Uber to the strip, though there is a shuttle from the hotel to Caesar's palace (only from 10am until 6pm).

allReviews.title: Outstanding!
allReviews.text: We never really wanted to go to Vegas because we are not Casino fans but then we arrived from Los Angeles, the ride was amazing, the weather, the lights and the apartment was the cherry on top!There was nothing wrong with it! The huge bathroom with that amazing bath tub, even the toilet with the self cleaining system is great!The guys at the reception are super nice and ready to help at all times of day and night.That viiew from the balcony is something that we will forever keep, the decoration, the bed, everything! We will come back for sure and truly recommend it

allReviews.title: Some Locals call it Vegas' Best Kept Secret
allReviews.text: Or so I've been told.  Hotel is situated to the west side of the strip so you don't have to battle with traffic on the strip itself.  If you're looking for a place to stay and play at, with no intentions of leaving the hotel for a stroll outside, this will be a good hotel to stay at.The rooms, or condos, are typically privately owned.  Think of it as a service apartment.  Though the layout of each room is identical, some of the furnishings may differ.  Each condo is equipped with a kitchenette that has a stove top, refrigerator and mini bar (2 separate refrigerators), microwave and cabinets.  Utensils and pans also provided.  The hotel also offers a grocery run service.  The bathroom is spacious with a walk-in shower, tub, single sink, and a separate toilet area.  One of the major plusses for us is that the room had several closets for his, hers and others.  There is also a safe deposit box in the room.Each room has a king sized bed plus an L-shaped pull out sofa bed and another arm chair.  There are also 2 TVs.  However, they're almost placed about 5 feet or less from the other.  The idea is to let someone sit on the sofa to watch and someone else to be watching in bed.  But the dialogue from the 2 tvs could drown the other. The room also has a long table that you can use for work but unfortunately, it was missing a chair.  So other than having lots of table space, you couldn't really do any work on it without standing.Flooring in bedroom area is wood.  Flooring in the living area (sofa bed) is carpet.  Foyer has marble-like tile flooring.If you're looking for a little casino fun and don't mind the long walk to the casino which is housed in the Palms Hotel & Casino side, Palms Place could be your little oasis.The lobby area is smaller than that at most other casino hotels.  But, it was clean and modern.  There is also seating in the lobby area.  Located off the lobby is a lobby bar and convenience store.The auto entryway to the main entrance of the hotel is small but nice.  At the front of the hotel parked several high-end cars like Rolls Royce.The biggest thing that bothered us was how messy the parking lot traffic was.  Cars seem to turn and drive at will.  There are no proper traffic markings so drivers went at their will. Some were polite and will give way to pedestrians.  There were a few that I don't care to rave about.  I will suggest that the property look into bettering its traffic flow situation.Parking is free.  There is open air parking as well as a parking structure.  However, there is no direct access to the Palms Place property from the parking structure.  From what we experienced, if one is parked on the 3rd floor of the structure, one would have to walk down the stairs to the ground level and then walk out to the hotel.  Hotel does charge a resort fee which will include wifi.  However, we were told by the engineer who came to fix a couple of non-operating switches in our room, as well as lights, that only 1 computer/phone/tablet is allowed access. This seem strange and we should have confirmed with the front desk but didn't.  Prior to booking here, if wi-fi access is important to you, I suggest for you to confirm with the hotel first.There are no eateries in the Palms Place tower.  But, you can certainly walk to Palms Hotel & Casino where they have a buffet and cafe, as well as other eateries.This property also provides complimentary shuttle service to Caesar's Palace and back for those who wish to explore the strip.  Closest hotel/casino that's within walking distance is the Palms Hotel & Casino and Rio, which is diagonally across the street.

allReviews.title: good sized room with reat views
allReviews.text: We booked an individuals suite through Airbnb that is on a high floor, strip facing.  We had great views from the balcony from the Strat down to the Delano.  Our balcony was unlocked - apparently some owners lock theirs up.  Service checking in good, minor repair to AC done fast, fitness center ok, pool ok - free parking.  Nothing not to like but 2 niggles:  1.  the crowd there were young and generally noisy - as we were leaving a group of young girls moved into next door and were smoking some V smelly weed whose smell was getting into our room when the balcony door was open!!  2. internet reception v spotty.   We got a 2-4-1 ticket to the buffet at the Palms casino (connected) and that was fine.   Would I stay there again?  probably, yes.

allReviews.title: Needs TLC
allReviews.text: Stayed here for 5 days. Was disappointing.  Pictures are deceiving.  The place is not well maintained.  Upon entering the room.  The kitchen and desk chairs were ripped up/torn all 3 chairs.  The carpet and hardwood floors need replaced.  Flooring is worned and showing signs of damage.  The one frigde shelf was cracked.  The shower door was not properly installed.  Did not shut properly.  Shower guard piece missing so water was splashing out of shower.  Shower knob is barely hanging on.  High speed internet that I paid for in the resort fees did not work!  When I mentioned these things at checkout to front desk they did not seem to care!  Would not stay at this place again.  It is off the strip and shuttle only runs from 11-8.  Not a clean environment. Stay elsewhere!

allReviews.title: Very clean and modern looking hotel with a touch of class
allReviews.text: What a fantastic way to enjoy an evening after a long day of business in party town. The room was spacious, felt like a home away from home. The amenities were great, the room service was great, all in all a very pleasing stay. Water pressure could be adjusted a little higher but that is my only complaint.

allReviews.title: Nice stay, disappointing service!
allReviews.text: Last week we stayed at The Palms Place. Nice stay but very unhappy with the service afterwards!! Stupid and our fault, but we forgot a Adidas Joggingsuit in our room (at the 12th floor). A minute before we left the room, I took a picture where you can see the joggingsuit at the couch. Even we have prove we forgot it in our room, they told us after calling and leaving a Lost & Found form, they did not found anything. They do not respons to our mails we sent to info@palms.com where we provided the pictures. Just a pitty!! Even more since the suit was a gift with personal value!! We’ll be in Vegas again next week and hope to receive a response before then..

allReviews.title: Palms Place
allReviews.text: As glamorous as the hotel was - and it was - some of the basic amenities weren't working. Sadly, the Jacuzzi was one of them, and it was a little further out than we were expecting. Still, with valet parking, a refreshing shower, and other options, I can see how others would enjoy it. I just wish everything had been working. And the view of the outside was really nice.

allReviews.title: Location
allReviews.text: The location of this hotel was its best quality. It was a few minutes away from the Vegas Strip and my room had an amazing view. Being that rooms are owned by separate groups, then each person's experience can be different.

allReviews.title: Not a good option any more
allReviews.text: This is my second review of the Palms Place. Since first staying here in 2013 I returned every year, as I am in Las Vegas for a conference once a year.This year will have been my last stay. While it still looks like a good value if you just look at the room rate, there are so many small and not so small issues that add up, and just make it an overall very unpleasant stay.I am just back from a 7 nights stay there , and here is what went wrong:- Houskeeping is unreliable. They come at different hours every day, one day we didn't get service at all, 2 more days we had to call in the late afternoon and probably would not have received service those days either, had we not called. When they do come, service is inconsistent, and every day something was missing (shampoo/ coffee/ toilet paper/tissues not refilled).- Maintenance issues. The place shows it's age. The two bar chairs in the kitchenette area were badly frayed, one lamp had a broken shade, furniture is badly scratched, some of the drawers don't close right, the shower handle is loose and there is mold on the caulk around the tub. The highlight: The ice maker was broken. I called to get this fixed, and they told me they would send up maintenance and an ice bucket. When we come home after dinner, there is a note from maintenance informing me that since there are three ice cubes in the tray that means the ice maker is working. Those ice cubes were in there since our arrival the day before. Also, I never got the ice bucket. Or any more than those three ice cubes.- High Resort fee. Their resort fee is $31.99, which is comparable to what some of the upscale places on the Strip charge. For this off strip place thats undergoing renovations at the moment this is ridiculously hight. It gets you virtually nothing (gym and pool access and whopping fast 1 Mbit internet).- Construction is happening on the property, mainly at the Palms, but it does impact the Palms Place as well. A big part of the parking lot is unavailable due to construction equipment and material- And the kicker is this: I had originally booked for 9 nights. Plans changed, and I could only stay 7 nights. I informed them about this at check in. I had booked a non-discounted rack rate through my corporate travel management company, nothing prepaid, not through Expedia or Hotwire or anything like that. They told me that there would be an "early check out fee" of $160. I have travelled a lot, but have never heard of such a thing, especially not when the hotel is notified of the change 7 days in advance, and is still getting to bill a 7 night stay. I am fighting this charge through both my travel management and CC company, but this alone is enough for me to never wanting to go back to this place.

allReviews.title: Almost Perfect
allReviews.text: I traveled with my girlfriend and it was our first visit to vegas. We arrived late on a flight from NYC 11pm. Check-in was smooth and the girl was nice. The room is very nice and views are great as well. The balcony doors are locked because of previous issue with guests throwing things over the edge. I wasn't too disappointed because I knew this when I booked however, there is no way to get them opened, we tried so if this is an issue for you don't stay here. We stayed for 5 nights/6 days. One of the reasons I did book here was because of the jacuzzi in the bathroom, ours did not work and when we called for service the person could not fix it. Nothing was done to resolve the issue as they did not have any more rooms available in the same category we had booked. The next night we went to buy some groceries for the kitchen in our room. (water, beers, chips, eggs etc.) we had around 10 or 15 bags. we pulled the car to the front of the hotel to unload and use one of the luggage carts, we were told to use one of the carts we would have to pay a fee. Apparently when you first check in you can use the cart for luggage free of charge..after this theres a fee. Most bazaar thing I have encountered. We decided to carry all the bags on our own...less than pleased about the situation. All in all not a bad stay the room was clean, looked just like the pictures on their website and parking was free and easy to come by. Would I stay again? Probably not unless I was on a budget.

allReviews.title: Nice place, for the most part.
allReviews.text: For our first trip to Las Vegas we decided to spend 2 nights in the Palms Place. This hotel is nice but not perfect. I was happy to see that they offered free self parking and that the rooms were nice but it seems like a lot of riff raff end up staying here. On our first night we ran into 2 couples on the elevator that were arguing and one of them was obviously on some sort of narcotic. The rooms themselves are nice, they are very roomy with a great bathroom and a kitchenette.  It was nice having the kitchenette but they do not provide any cookware, dishes, or utensils in the room. I think that you have to ask them to provide them.  I am nor sure if there is a fee. It was nice to at least have a small fridge to use for items we picked up at the grocery. Overall, this is a nice place to stay and I might stay there again.

allReviews.title: Great hotel property with a high level of overall value
allReviews.text: I was very pleased with my stay at the Palms Place.  Upon arriving, we were able to get a free upgrade to a one bedroom suite which was HUGE (THANK YOU!). The rooms are spacious with modern fixtures and awesome views of Las Vegas. Paige, the concierge was friendly, helpful and provided 1st class customer service. Great spa and fitness center and the food from room service was very good. My only gripe was that upon checking out, it took nearly 20+ minutes to get our bags from bell desk. I understand that there were only 2 bell men, however I think on Sundays, between the hours of 10-12pm, the hotel should expect that is a high checkout time and probably should have more than 2 bell men working the baggage checkout. Since we waited that long, my partner and I nearly missed our flights back home (we were literally the last two people to board the plane). The hotel property overall is very nice and I was happy with the customer service, but my checkout experience with my bags changed my 5 star rating.

allReviews.title: Don't book this hotel via AirPads!
allReviews.text: I've booked a package-trip with Expedia. Apparently Expedia made the reservations for our two rooms with AirPads. When we arrived at our rooms we were welcomed by a funky smell from the bathrooms. Immediately we saw that the rooms were not clean while we pay $80 cleaning costs per apartment. My room had the most problems: mold on the bathroom walls, dirty kit-edges, furniture torn and worn out, curtain couldn't be opened because it was stuck and the safe was on low-battery. The same evening we immediately talked to the receptionist about our problems. He said he could send someone up for cleaning. But a new battery for the safe was not possible because the apartment was private property. We had to call with Expedia and they had to authorize the costs for the replacement of the battery......Also there was a constant smell from the weed that's being smoked at the rooms. In the room next to me they were filming a adult movie. And the guy in the room was very rude to the girls (aggressive). At the end of the week we've been at the reception desk every day with our complaints but every time the staff said they could not do nothing about it because the apartments are private-property. The apartments were never cleaned again. There is a company at the hotel (InnerCircle) that is the intermediary for the private-owners and the hotel. But we've had the same experience with them; they could not do anything about the problems and we should call Expedia. It's just very frustrating that we couldn't go anywhere with the complaints and problems during our stay. Everybody is pointing to somebody else. Please make sure you don't book this hotel with AirPads. The service is terrible, better said; there is NO service. And also the hotel is not to be recommended. This is not by far a 4-star hotel. And certainly don't book this hotel with kids.

allReviews.title: If you want open balconies? This is not the place.
allReviews.text: I’m so sick and tired of Hotels & Discount Hotel Websites. It’s like you have to do your own detective work & investigate if you’re getting exactly what’s advertised, and this place is no exception. I’ve spent days considering this place, reading all reviews, calling the hotel twice, etc. and just when I was about to reserve? I asked about the balcony and was told that “ALL BALCONIES ARE LOCKED”  you won’t find that mentioned in ads circulating, but they’ll promote the hell out of the fact that they are there. To me it’s like “Here is a brand new Lexus, but you can’t have the keys”  This was the only thing that set them apart, because I was looking for city views & a balcony. Also, when reserving? Make sure you know if you want to stay at PALMS PLACE HOTEL & SPA or PALMS W/Casino Just adjacent to Palms Place (as rudely explained by reservations) otherwise you’ll get rates that may apply to the other and be surprised it wasn’t applied to your room once you get there. But “Yes” the locked balcony was the deal breaker.

allReviews.title: Very dissatisfied
allReviews.text: I accidentally left my wallet in the locked safe upon checkout. After repeated calls over 3 days, I received no help as far as retrieving my item from the safe. All of my credit cards etc, suddenly went missing as I finally got an email they couldn’t find my item. Obviously it was stolen by their own staff! If you do lose something , beware of zero protocol on their part to help you, and get authorization to check the safe as I was told they do not disturb other guests. I’m sorry I think any guest would appreciate someone knocking on their door and asking if they could access the safe because someone lost their personal items of value...I would appreciate that and be willing to help another person. Horrible security staff in charge of lost and found.

allReviews.title: Beautiful view of the strip
allReviews.text: Clean, nice hotel with big pool. We were here during summer and than in February we stayed in different hotel on the Strip so we can compare. Palm Place Hotel deserve 5 stars.Pros:- Spacious renovated room with modern bathroom- Very comfortable beds- Friendly staff- Shuttle bus to Cesar Palace (Strip)- Beautiful view of the strip- No smoke and noise (hotel and casino are little bit separate)Cons:- Poor options for eating (we tried Chinese Cuisine but meal was cold, Buffet was closed for a renovation)- Not walkable distance to the Strip

allReviews.title: 5 star stay!
allReviews.text: The Palms Place studio suites are awesome.  It feels like you’re living in a luxury apartment. There is plenty of space and then some. Our check in was easy and our room was clean and much bigger than we expected.  The room was equipped with three TVs, a full kitchen, and a huge bathroom which included a rain shower (heavenly) and jacuzzi tub.  Housekeeping was pleasant and a great service. We’ll definitely be back!

allReviews.title: Book through Airbnb!
allReviews.text: Room was great!  30th floor with balcony and beautiful view of the strip.  Wonderful shower and jetted tub!  Loved the bathrobes!  Only downfall was the cost of drinks at the pool...I got a frozen drink and a Blue Moon.  The beer was served to me in a can not even opened, put inside a plastic cup with an orange laid on top of the can...cost $25.00 then informed there was a 20% gratuity...mind you I went to the bar myself and she couldn't even pour the beer from the can into the cup???? Ate breakfast at Café 6, it was very good but service was extremely slow...

allReviews.title: Nice stay off the Strip
allReviews.text: Palms Place is a hotel that is next to The Palms Casino Hotel. It is made up of residences. Ours was a one bedroom with a king bed and a small kitchen area. It was very nicely decorated and very spacious. The bathroom was large and modern with everything we wanted. A large shower and whirlpool tub stood out. Our view of the strip was beautiful. The building does not have a casino which was nice, since there was less smoke and noise. They was a nice outdoor pool and a nice gym and spa. The steam room was huge and the spa areas were beautiful and relaxing. The lounge in the lobby was nice but a little expensive. Cafe 6, the restaurant was closed for an update so we didn’t see that. Here is a walkway on the second floor to access the casino and other food options. The staff was very friendly and polite and answered any of our questions as well as made recommendations when requested. I would have scored the Palms Place a 5 if we could have visited Cafe 6 and it was good.

allReviews.title: Don't stay here!
allReviews.text: For the love of God, please DO NOT stay here. My amazing husband planned a staycation for us to celebrate my 25th a couple of weeks ago and our stay was so much worse than any other experience we've had. Literally, everything that could have gone wrong, did go wrong. We expressed our concerns very kindly to the staff and the response was apathetic at best. This place inspired me to write my first ever negative review - so disappointed!

allReviews.title: Week get away
allReviews.text: We stayed here from the 2nd through the 5th of April and loved it! We booked through a private owner and everything went smoothly at check-in. The view from our 51st floor room was unbeatable! We enjoyed the Drift Spa and found this to be one of the highlights of the trip. The pool was nice, just a little more crowded than usual because they are still working on the Palm's Pool.

allReviews.title: Relaxing Home Away From Home
allReviews.text: Loved our stay on the 35th floor. Unit was super comfortable and bathroom was luxurious. I could live in that bathroom forever.Nice movie theater and decent food court in the Palms Casino, a short walk away through the "Sky Tube".Pool, though a bit intense, was pretty gorgeous though I don't think children should be allowed in the hot tub.On one occasion, my key card stopped working but luckily I used the hall phone to call security and he was helpful. Annoying though!Will definitely be back!!!

allReviews.title: Home away from home
allReviews.text: I stay at Palms Place around 3 times a year and consider it my home away from home. The comfort of the rooms is undeniable, I have stayed in the 1 bedroom suite and the standard suite. The rooms are always impeccably clean and well appointed. 5 minutes off the strip, but only a shuttle ride away from Caesars Palace. We took the shuttle, and we were pleasantly surprised at the level of comfort. The shuttle driver was friendly and a wonderful driver. The casino bar had great drinks, and even though the lobby was under construction there was no dust or disruption. We traveled at the end of March and checked out on Easter, if you are looking to book for Summer I would highly recommend this hotel. First time we utilized the room service and we were delighted at the speed of delivery, wonderful service and best of all delicious food!

allReviews.title: Construction/Communication/Service
allReviews.text: I’ve stayed at the Palms and Palms place over the years.  In November I stayed at the Palms for three nights and was very dissatisfied. I posted a review here and was asked to reach out to the manager upon my return. This weekend I stayed for three nights at the Palms place.  I reached out via email and also called and left a message. No one responded.- cafe was closed due to construction. When I called the front desk before booking at the palms place they assured me they were fully operational. -parking is extra tight with the palms main garage under construction.- Pool does not allow you bring any outside water bottles or food while offering a very limited food menu for the pool.-drink service at the pool is top notch and fast. (Gabby was stellar)- kids had floaties (big round one) in thePool which I thought was odd considering the strict enforcement of other rules- security told multiple patrons they had to keep pool chairs where they were located in order to keep the look “Ascetic” after they moved them two inches.-  Another guest played fabulous’s new album on YouTube from his MacBook Pro even though the hotel pool has its own music??? - Girlfriend got the massage Groupon at drift and highly recommend the Spa service. A +- The room has a great layout very comfortable bed and couches.- kitchen/microwave/fridge/ burners are great for the long weekend.-no pots , pan , or kitchenware provided. I called downstairs and front desk transferred me to house keeping it rang and rang.... nobody answered. I ended up grabbing the cheapest set Walmart had. - the chair in my room for the kitchen looked like it ha been chewed by a dog and needed to be replaced.- NO balcony key provided by the palms. - Airbnb guest around my room had keys for there units. When I return in two weeks if I’m staying at the Palms I’ll go this route.

allReviews.title: Pleasant stay, but away from the strip.
allReviews.text: This was away from the strip so you can't just go out and walk around.  Older hotel but well-maintained. It smelled like smoke though, they need a new ventilation system in the lobby.  It was all over and all of the time.  The pool pictures are beautiful and I was so looking to have some hours by it, however we went in January and it was all closed down, no chairs, no people. .  disappointing.  Look at Groupon for spa coupons.  I found some and had one of the best mani/pedis of my life.

allReviews.title: Hotel
allReviews.text: Would avoid hotel noisy and in need of love poor hotel and service. Rooms old and need updating . There is general construction going on and woken up at 600 with repair work. Would recommend if you like sleeping at a building site.

allReviews.title: Balconies! Balconies! Balconies!
allReviews.text: I am drawn by balconies, in general, but especially in hotel rooms, and super especially in hotel suites. I booked through an Airbnb listing, which gets you almost the same experience as booking through the property directly. When you book through Airbnb you still go to the front desk to register, can get room service, and have access to the amenities. BUT, if you book through Palm's Place there is no access to the balcony! That's right, one of the biggest selling points, not accessible! That said, the rooms, at least the 1br I stayed in, was phenomenal. Great design and finishings throughout and a fully functional kitchen, should you have the urge. There is a pullout couch and a half bath, making it easy and comfortable for 2-4 (maybe more) guests. Oh, and there were TWO balconies in these corner units -- one off the master bedroom and another off the living room. Head over the Palms via the people mover for all that Vegas has to offer.Negatives: Check in was super slow and the walk to Palms could be a little less, well, boring (come on guys! get the people hype!)Pro Tip: Get off campus and take the five-minute ride to Raku. You will not regret it.

allReviews.title: Off to a horrible start
allReviews.text: Checked in today 3/26/18. Off to a rough start with the family vacation.Prepaid for 3 days but might look for alternative accommodationsCons- jetted tub doesn't work - nice kitchenette but NO DISHES- room not clean, found random items in restroom and under sofa bed- one of the tv's didn't work <it was fixed fast tho>PROS- nice room- rain shower - nice view

allReviews.title: Amazing view, close enough to everything yet far enough from the noise!
allReviews.text: The Palms Place Hotel and Spa is a great value for money! We hesitated staying here and considered other options but most other well-known hotels were completely sold out! It worked out well for us though because we didn't want to be right on the strip and we don't gamble so that wasn't important to us. The rooms are very clean, well appointed and had a fresh, modern vibe. The view was amazing, far enough to get great pictures and a full view of Vegas! There was a waterfall shower and oversized spa tub which was a pleasant surprise. :) The only downside to staying here was the odd arrangement for breakfast- we had to walk over a skybridge about 5 minutes to the dining area, then wait in a line and only then were we seated. That was really frustrating and we almost got out of line and left but the manager came to apologize and was professional about it which we appreciated. Apparently, they are renovating the dining area on the Palms Place side of the property so it should only be temporary! Overall, great hotel- no regrets! :)

allReviews.title: Airbnb Rental - 50th Floor
allReviews.text: Having read recent reviews, we must’ve lucked out. Our local host contact was extremely responsive & accommodating (extra towels & bath tissue; she also provided extra K-cup coffee pods). There’s a beverage chill unit above the mini fridge & a courtesy “pay it forward bar”. The bottoms of the closet doors & appliances could’ve been wiped down after mopping (signs of splatter), but that didn’t affect our comfort). We had full access to our balcony & enjoyed it throughout the day.Parking is free & plentiful, just don’t use “self park” garage unless you need to fulfill your 10K daily steps - access only to casino, rather than the hotel. You must show your room key to access elevators at night; floors noted above doors, first two cars only go up to 36. As a guest, fitness center (must be 18 & older) & pool are free, but not 24-hr accessible.

allReviews.title: Worst hotel I've ever stayed in...in 15 years of weekly travel.
allReviews.text: I wish I would've read reviews before booking here.  This hotel has made me want to cry, scream and cancel the rest of my trip to just give up and fly home.  The service is horrible.  I could go on and on, but I'll only point out a few items to save us all time:- Any time you call the front desk, or the spa, or room service, or ANY hotel area from your room, you will wait at least 10 minutes on hold until someone can pick up.  THEN, when you walk down to get faster service, they will actually pick up the phone of someone on hold ahead of you.  WTF???? - Right now a pool and a couple of restaurants are under construction, so that is definitely unfortunate timing for this trip. I would call to confirm that everything is open before you even begin to consider staying here.- I went downstairs to buy bottled water.  The gift shop is closed for 30 minutes.  Who gives their employees a 30 minute break without having someone fill in for them?  It's the only gift shop on property.  So, the front desk said the minibar has water.  I go back to my room to get water out of the mini bar and wouldn't you know it, the two spaces for water are the two empty spaces in the refrigerator.  It had apparently not been restocked before I checked in.  I'm sure I'll be charged for that, based on my experience thus far.  So, I ask housekeeping (who was delivering toothpaste, since the gift shop was closed where I wanted to buy toothpaste!) if they could re-stock the water in my mini bar, but he said that had to be done by the front desk.  I call the front desk, who tells me that has to be done by room service, so I call room service, and when i speak with her she says they can send me up water but there would be the standard room service charge on top of the cost of the water.  WTF????  I told her I'm in the desert and need bottled water and I'm not going to walk 10 minutes to the casino in a separate building to buy bottled water, that's ridiculous.  She said she'll send up someone from "mini bar" to restock for me.  That was ten minutes ago, who knows if it'll happen.That's all I can share so far, but I've only been here four hours. I'm positive that I'll be disappointed again in the next two days...

allReviews.title: Great Place Great Price
allReviews.text: We rented a condo for our 5 day vacation. Room was nice, clean and ready to go. The staff was friendly and help full. Easy access to pool and casino with out having to go out side.Reason for 4 stars, we rented a condo which included a sink, microwave, cook top and fride. We how ever did not have silverware, plates, or cups. We proceeded to order them thru the call line. Waited 2 hrs and they did not show up. Ended up calling 3 times to order them and waited just under 7hrs by they time they arrived at our room. Also the second day requested more coffee which didnt get to our room while we where there so we had to go buy it in the mornings. Easy access too coffee in building or in the area but its not as easy when you pay for a room with a coffee maker.

allReviews.title: Palms place.....a Disgrace!
allReviews.text: Where do I begin.....We had to spend 5 hours in the outlet mall because we arrived at 10am and check-in was not until 3:00pm.  We showed up at 3:20 and were told that the rooms were not ready and it would be a "few hours".  No "sorry for the inconvenience" or anything.  Front end staff were not welcoming or friendly and certainly not customer oriented.  Finally get a room at 5:20.  Room looks nice-BUT-on the website and other places where the Palms Place is advertised, it says "Our state of the art kitchenette means you can also have a relaxing night in"-yes - just what we needed.  We also like to eat a light breakfast and have a leisurely coffee in our room in the morning so I thought this was perfect.  WRONG!  We went out to buy a few groceries, came back to eat some salad and chicken - opened the cupboard and there were two glasses and two mugs - NO plates, NO bowls, NO utensils, NO paper towels or dishtowels - BUT-there was a dishwasher!  There is also a two pot stove top - BUT-NO pot to cook anything in.  We had to go back out to buy plates, bowls, utensils and a coffeemaker.  I had called ahead (because I can only drink certain coffee) to ask what type of coffeemaker they had and was told "a regular coffeemaker" -BUT- it is actually one of those crappy hotel "one cup at a time" coffee makers with the coffee pouches and they give you two pouches of coffee. The RESORT FEE is very HIGH - $31.99US plus tax and you get nothing for it.  WIFI SLOW.   POOL not open.  Shuttle only runs until 8pm and only picks up and drops off at the casino which is quite a distance from Palms Place.  It would not take much for the driver to stop at Palms Place first and then the Casino. The "Sky Tube" is a joke - just two long "people-movers"- they make it sound like something out of the future. There is a balcony but they will not open it unless we upgrade to the Penthouse or if I was an owner. Day of check-out, 11:02 housekeeping was knocking on the door to clean our room even though they made us wait for hours on day of arrival.  BIGGEST CON:  When you check in, they use your credit card to bill $100 per day that you are there - perhaps for damage deposit(?)  HOWEVER, when you check out and ask about your $100.00 per day, they tell you it will take 3 - 5 business days for it to be refunded.  So we spent 6 nights  - so they billed my credit card $600.00US and they keep that money for 11 days - nice interest for the hotel considering how many rooms and how many people they are doing that to.  Somehow that does not seem legal.  I cannot recommend this hotel.  Even with researching in advance, we were mislead.  I hope this review helps some other couple not have to regret their vacation choices.

allReviews.title: Worst hotel service in maybe the galaxy
allReviews.text: Incredibly poor service. If you try calling the front desk, get ready for a twenty minute wait. We ordered a movie on demand and it didn’t work TWICE. Took us one hour to remedy the situation. No apology. The room service also gave us FOOD POISONING. No apology or even a refund! Instead they made us, in the depths of our illness, file a report. They do not know the word “sorry” and I think they are unaware that they are a hotel. The concierge also is incompetent. She said if we wanted to find out about car rentals we can “Google different companies and compare ourselves.” Ok?

allReviews.title: Beautiful View of the Strip
allReviews.text: On Valentines Day, we stayed on the 39th floor of this awesome hotel which is close to all the action in Vegas.  The view stretched for miles and was beautiful any time of the day. The valet parking was a nice convenience and the staff is very patient and helpful. We had a room with a Jacuzzi, full kitchen and a balcony. Everything was very clean and elegant and I would recommend staying here to anyone visiting Vegas

allReviews.title: Not what we expected
allReviews.text: Booked this hotel after the review gave it 4 stars... was disappointed. Room was ok but in disrepair, the shower leaked horribly and the water faucet was falling off the wall. Housekeeping spoke no English and we were unable to communicate that we needed towels to mop up the leaking shower mess. No taxis available or close by and we waited at least 10-15m each time we went out. Pool out of order for maintenance. We WONT be back.

allReviews.title: Las Vegas Affordable
allReviews.text: I just attended a 70th birthday party for a family member who's favorite destination is Las Vegas.  I stayed at the Palms Place Hotel and Spa.  The location is conveniently located about a half mile off the strip and it made for a very affordable weekend.  The Palms Place Hotel is connected to the Palms Casino Resort however, the Palms Place Hotel does not have a casino which was perfect for me since I don't gamble.  There is a sky walk from the Palms Place Hotel to the casino at the Palms resort, a short five minute jaunt.  The hotel is lovely and updated, very chic and modern.  I had a king size studio suite on the 17th floor with a great view of the Las Vegas Strip.  The room also came with a kitchenette and the bathroom was huge with a large shower and jetted tub.  It couldn't have been nicer.  The front desk staff was courteous and friendly, check in and check out was handled timely and with ease.  I will definitely recommend the Palms Place to anyone looking for an affordable location to stay in Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: RESORT FEES AND INTERNET DOESN'T WORK WITHOUT PAYING MORE!!
allReviews.text: Plan on having to upgrade the internet service even with the high resort fee and customer service is lacking.  Front desk need some customer training!!  Not well managed for sure!!  Room was quiet, but smelled like cooking from the previous occupant!  I would not stay here again.

allReviews.title: Low class front desk manager
