The shower was awesome.  Had the regular shower head and the rain shower head.  Two tvs and a sofa.  All in all the room was nice.  There was a pool on the 6th floor of this hotel and I liked it a lot.  Smaller than the main one but with a bar and bathrooms.  And free!  The main pool was big with lots of people wanting to be seen and if you get there after 12pm, it was $10.  Crazy.  Drinks were very expensive so we didn't get any at the pool.  I was not impressed with the casino.  It wasn't as big and as nice as the ones on the strip in my opinion.  The cocktail waitresses did not come around very often.  I didn't gamble there too much so can't make a comment on the payouts.There were many dining options.  We ate at the Chinese restaurant and Hooters and they were both good and had good customer service.  We ate lunch in the food court.  That was a good option to save money.  We would Uber to the strip and it was fast and affordable so it wasn't a big deal being off the strip and their shuttle to and from Caesars ran until 8pm and we used that once also.  Las Vegas has become very expensive.  That is not this hotels fault, just an observation.  I remember when it was more affordable. You will spend a lot of money here.The Palms is a nice place all in all but I would probably stay on the strip next time so I can just walk from casino to casino and be in the middle of all the action!

allReviews.title: Wow
allReviews.text: I usually always stay at MGM properties, but this time a friend of mine wants to stay here. So to make things easy I booked my room here as well, wow! I am so surprised. The room is so nice, BIG. I love the room smell, the living room area and the balcony. I am sold now and will stay here from now on. Plus the price is really nice! $60 per night. This is call value.

allReviews.title: Save your money
allReviews.text: Waited 25 minutes for the pool to open......chronically late employee, then there were no towelsTV and remotes work poorlyEntrance looks like the back door of other hotelsStaff........not very interested in guestsWay over priced for VegasKitchenette, but no pots,pans,or utensils,   Dah

allReviews.title: Pleasantly Surprised
allReviews.text: Visited 16th-22nd May.Having booked our holiday as a package with flights and accommodation combined and for a good price we were a little worried that the accommodation would not be up to its 5 star rating.Being a 20min walk off the strip this didn't bother us and it's only a $5-7 Uber (cheaper than Vegas taxis) if you don't want to walk. Ubers were great by the way, loads of them around and pretty reasonable. We arrived at the hotel around 3pm for check in which was quick and easy however be warned about resort fees!! I think we were $210 for the week, all hotels have this few I believe, which seems a bit of a con to me but we figured we were not paying much for the hotel in the first place so didn't kick up a fuss. We asked for a strip view room, instead of mountain view, and were duly obliged. On the 27th floor, about half way up we had a good view of the strip from our room. It was very clean upon entry and large. Nice marble flooring in the initial hallway which extends into the bathroom which has a large walk in shower with a jacuzzi tub big enough for 2!! 1 sink and large walled mirror and toilet just off, but with no door on the toilet which is a tad strange. There is a small kitchenette area before the bedroom with a sink, dishwasher and microwave. No oven or hob. Plates, cutlery and glasses can be acquired from reception at no extra fee thankfully.The bed is huge, I think a super king sized one, and also the most comfortable I have ever slept on. Sheets were clean and changed every second day. Rooms were cleaned every day if desired. Plenty of space for clothes and storing suitcases too. Also a large wall mounted TV at the end of the bed.There is also a nice living area at the end of the studio room with a L shaped sofa and another wall mounted TV in this area, literally feet away from the other one which seems a bit unnecessary.The only downside to the room is that you cannot get access to the balcony as the sliding window doors are permanently locked, which means the outside balcony looks quite dirty which spoils the view slightly. Overall I thought the rooms were great and the hotel wasn't a usually fancy Vegas one, the building is separate to the main casino building so a bit quieter. There is a skywalk with travelators to get between to the two meaning you don't need to go outside. There was also a pool at the casino resort which was quite good and also a quieter pool at palms place building. There was nothing I would complain about in this hotel other than the lack of places to eat but mostly you head out to the strip for that. We enjoyed our week in Vegas and the hotel accommodation was a pleasant surprise to us. 5 star quality but maybe 4 star service.

allReviews.title: Beautiful and Accomodating
allReviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at Palms Place.  The studio unit was just perfect.  It was clean, spacious and room service/housekeeping were both fantastic!  It was an easy phone call to get all kitchen utensils.I was also able to check in early without any problem.  Always a bonus after hours of traveling!The location of the resort is wonderful, just across the bridge onto the strip.  The pool is quaint and charming.  I'm looking forward to returning to Vegas and booking this same studio unit with Hoteltron.com

allReviews.title: ONE OF THE WORST HOTELS I EVER STAYED AT
allReviews.text: We booked three rooms. One of the three rooms was not available until 11 p.m. because "housekeeping" did not have the room ready. We finally got into the room after 11 p.m. and we discovered that the toilet did not work. They sent someone up who tried to fix it but it didn't work. The next day I asked to speak to the manager. He/she couldn't be bothered with me and sent an "assistant manager" out instead after a few minutes. They said that it couldn't be fixed (I wonder if they knew about before we checked in and that is why it wasn't ready) and gave us another room and offer a whopping $30.00 credit for a room that didn't have a working toilet. That was insulting.We had another problem the second of our three rooms, That room had an odor like a sewer. Again, we called down and they supposedly sent someone up. The odor did not go away and they had to switch that room too. Even a staff member (who will remain nameless) said that they didn't know how we could stay in the room with that odor.We also had an issue with a hair dryer that was sparking. We went to the front desk to ask for a new one. They refused to take back the sparking blow dryer and said that engineering had to look at it. They sent someone up to our room and even he was confused as to why he was there since he said housekeeping should replace it.We also had other issues which were minor: (1) Not having the coffee refilled by housekeeping (2) shampoo bottles that we nearly empty and (3) no sponge in one of the rooms.The rooms were nice and have potential. It is the management that is lacking and not responsive. I did not get the impression that they even cared about the issues in the room. The Palms Place appears to be a  condo. People buy them and the Palms "manages" (I use that term loosely) the condos for the owners which are then used as "hotel" rooms. Maybe this is why the management doesn't seem to care.I have stayed in many hotels in the US, Canada and Europe and this would have to been one of my worse experiences. I would not go back to this "hotel" since the condition of the room is a gamble and the management doesn't seem to care.

allReviews.title: Bachelor party
allReviews.text: I just visited Las Vegas for my bachelor party and stayed at Palms Place at The Palms Resort and Casino. Overall it was a good experience however the suite did not completely live up to expectations. I stayed in the 2-bedroom suite. There were 2 large balconies that we were looking forward to using, but withhout anyone letting us know we found out that they were inaccessible! One of the televisions did not work until an engineer came up to fix it. I also called the hotel ahead of our trip to verify that our suite had some sort of sound system or radio for the bachelor party and I was assured that there was. After finding that out I did not bring my wireless speaker. We showed up to a broken i home and no other options! The entertainment and food at the resort was AMAZING! He gaming and service were also highlights. If you are going for a fun weekend or bachelor/bachelorette party I would recommend n9ne steakhouse, Ghostbar, and Ditch Friday's(pool party). Once again overall it was a good experience. Although since I stayed OFF THE STRIP I was expecting nearly flawless and there were definitely flaws!

allReviews.title: Poor customer experience, won't ever return
allReviews.text: The rooms in general were nice here, very large, but the overall experience of the hotel was a disappointment. Not only did they close the pool at 4pm, well before sunset, we had massive attitude from the lifeguard when we got there at 3:45 immediately after checking in for the one afternoon we would have there. The spotty and clunky wifi was limited to a single device per room...I haven't experienced this in even cheap hotels in the last five years, when we had a package arrive the front desk said we needed to come down and carry it up because they were short staffed and when we checked out we had a $30 "resort fee" added onto our bill on top of other taxes and fees that was not disclosed at any point before. Quite rich in a place where we specifically felt like every nice bonus you expect in a hotel of this calibre was non-existent or not open for us to enjoy. Also be aware if you want to pop in and out of the strip easily, even though this hotel is close, a major highway sitting in between makes it almost impossible to walk.

allReviews.title: Not your average Vegas Hotel!
allReviews.text: Check In was easy. Pool gorgeous. All Palm Place guests have full access to the palm Casino and Pool. Shuttle to Caeser's Palace Shops was prompt, comfortable and in a luxury air-conditioned Mercedes van. A nice dark safe ride. I waited a bit during rush hour to check out but they were nice and accommodating. This place is No smoking so it was nice not to have to deal with that smell. No icky Casino vibes, Palms Casino is elegant and clean. It's a great place to gamble and enjoy yourself. Casino is a short walk through the walkway. I liked Palm's Place a lot because of the large rooms. Fridge was great and available for personal Items. Bathroom was gorgeous. I like large bathrooms with amenities and this place has it. Spa was a $25 fee. I LOVED the steam room with Eucalyptus! Whirlpool large. And the co-ed steam room (The Hannanum) was nice too. Very shiek. Very relaxing. Liked the spa period. Worth every penny. The whole spa was well done. I felt very comfortable there and I am picky about this stuff. I don't like smelly or places that can be germ breeding grounds. Spas are wet and they can be but the staff at the spa was present and on top of everything - temperature of saunas, towel service, and overall cleanliness. I am checking out other places to stay next time. But I am tempted to revisit and rebook the Palms Place. I stayed in the Studio Suite high up on one of the upper floors. It was quiet. i never heard so much as a whisper any time I was in my room. Yes the balcony is locked, sigh, but I managed. The view was gorgeous regardless. Television worked well. Bathroom tub was cracked all around. they should get the contractor that did those tubs to re-do all of them, it seems to be mentioned in a lot of reviews. Overall Palms Place gave me exactly what I wanted a sense of luxury, a room with a view, a decent spa experience, good food (when I did not want to leave the hotel) Access to the strip but tastefully removed from the chaos. Cafe 6 was not an extensive menu, but I liked what I ordered (kale caeser salad and sliders). The bartenders know how to make good drinks. Rojo is a nice lounge spot for a drink. Everything is visually appealing. Did not love the pool bar. Something was not quite right there. Needs some life, some music, something. It was like a ghetto corner of the place. Extensive beer menu in Cafe 6 not available at Pool Bar.. BOO!! Prices were way over the top for the size of the drinks coming out of pool bar. Did not like that. I like my pool staff to be a little more attentive and not be wearing bikini up the butt while serving me. Sorry there is fine line when handling food and drinks and walking around in a skimpy bikini. Wear a sarong at least girl. Not hating just think for a classy place the staff pool attire needs a make-over. They also gave plastic fork to eat my salad out there. Eek!Overall I loved Palms Place. And I will be back.

allReviews.title: Nice overnight room
allReviews.text: The room at Palms Place was nice and big.  We had a great view of the strip from a high floor.  There was a kitchen with gourmet appliances, Refrigerator, dishwasher stove and microwave.The bathroom had a jacuzzi bathtub that was huge!! There was a raintree shower upon entering and exiting the tub.  Roomy vanity area and a separate water closet made it very convenient for couples and families to be able to use.There is a walkover to the Palms Casino, which a a little long, but there is a moving sidewalk for a portion of it and it is covered so you can remain cool in the summer and warm during the winter months.  That is the one downside, the distance to the eating facilities and casino, although there was a place to eat at Palm Place. I would definitely stay there again.

allReviews.title: Home away from home
allReviews.text: Palms place is a hotel that makes u feel like your at home with expensive taste and amenities! I love the staff and how they catered to my needs. I love the rooms, full kitchen and wonderful views of vegas!!! I loveeeee stay here! I had the 2 bedroom penthouse with the pool on the balcony. I felt like the President.

allReviews.title: 1 night stay at The Palms
allReviews.text: My boyfriend and I stayed for one night at The Palms, in 'The Place', which is the residential tower without the casino. This doesn't make a difference because there is a simple indoor walkway between The Place tower and the Casino tower. Being located off the Strip the hotel offer a shuttle service to and from. - we didn't use this but they told us about when we checked in. The room was massive with a 'L' shaped sofa, big comfy bed and 2 TV's as well as a big bathroom.  The hotel had loads of restaurants; both fast food and fine dining as well as plenty of other things such as a cinema. We went to the pool based in the residential tower and it was really nice with great music being played.The main reason for staying at the hotel was so we could go to the Ghost Bar. It has the most incredible view of the strip at night. It was happy hour between 8pm and 10pm so we went up early so we could get 50% off drinks and photos without other people in the way! I would recommend this hotel, however having stayed on the strip I would recommend staying on the strip due to location or do what we did and have the best of both worlds; one night off the strip and three nights on the strip!

allReviews.title: Over the top kindness!
allReviews.text: I booked and paid for a trip to Vegas through a fraudulent vacation rentals company. Cascadevacationrentals.com.We arrive at the Palm's place with or fraudulent paper work. The front desk associate Thedda Eslava  could not find or reservation, because I got scammed. She took my cell number, gave us pool keys until she could figure out where are reservation was. She called me back and told me I was scammed. We returned to the front desk where Thedda greeted us with a smile. She informed us that it was indeed a fraudulent company. Before I could ask what we could we do she offered us a comparable suite at about the same rate. She made a bad situation a good one!! Thank you for your excellent service and kind heart. All the staff we interacted with at the Palms were nothing but pleasant and helpful! We will be back and tell everyone! Thank you again Thedda!!

allReviews.title: Stylish Modern Suites and away from the Strip
allReviews.text: Lovely spacious suites with decent kitchen, nice bathroom with huge tub, twin flat screen TVs, everything you need for a self contained stay.The Palms Place tower is away from the resort and casino so is nice and quiet, the Palms Place resort is busier and has the pools etc, so choose which tower you prefer.The whole complex is about a mile from the Strip and if that suits you it's a perfect place to stay away from the madness.Excellent value, friendly and helpful staff.

allReviews.title: A surprisingly great location off the strip.
allReviews.text: This was my first time staying at The Palms property and I had found a deal online that made Palms Place, the property's upgraded tower, very affordable.As you approach the tower you immediately realize they've created a place where you're close enough to the action to be apart of it, while at the same time having the option to seclude yourself in an environment that's far more calm and relaxing than the main property. The suite was built in a condo style with a spacious living area, full kitchen, and a large bathroom that sported a Jacuzzi tube and shower with a Swedish shower option. The suite was kept very clean and well maintained and the view from the 31st floor was amazing. There was a balcony but it was not accessible as the sliding door did not open (normal in Vegas hotels). The staff was very polite and helpful. The spa & gym facilities were very nice and easily accessible. The pool area at Palms Place was separate from the pool at The Palms. Smaller, more intimate, more of a relaxing environment than a party pool. But if a party is what you're looking for you have access to The Palms pool too. My stay was a great experience and I'd definitely stay there again.

allReviews.title: What a great hotel!
allReviews.text: Stayed there for a week! On the 42nd floor! Amazing view! The great thing about this hotel is that it takes you 10 minutes to check in and you're in your room 5 minutes later where as it can take you up to 2 hours to any hotels on The Strip. Like any hotels food is not cheap! But there's a lovely bagel place right next door to the hotel called Einstein Bagels. We went there every day! The pool is small but perfect for a morning swim. The hotel is about 20 minute walk from The Strip but I hired a car for a week as we wanted to explore. Driving is super easy and all hotels have free parking!

allReviews.title: Incredible
allReviews.text: We upgraded to a 1200 square foot suite and it was worth every penny!  What an amazing room on the 31 floor overlooking the Strip.  The suite has 1 1/2 bathrooms, a beautiful gourmet kitchen with a fridge, cook top, microwave and dishwasher.  Floor to ceiling windows, fireplace and air tub in the bedroom. The decor and furniture is modern and comfortable.

allReviews.title: Great Spot
allReviews.text: I visit Vegas annually with the fellas for NFL action and stay at a different hotel each time. We got a smoking good deal at this hotel and it was too good to pass up. You pretty much are staying at The Palms. When checking in we were able to upgrade to a really nice suite. Great way to set off my trip. It was a very nice room. Even though it was off the trip, it was worth it. I wasn't too thrilled with the pool area, but that's it. No casino, but that didn't matter as you literally are just a short walk through the parking lot to The Palms.

allReviews.title: Best Hotel off the Strip
allReviews.text: Best Luxury hotel for anything off the stripHotel Itself: Clean, luxury, no casino. These were suppose to be condo's but they converted them into hotel rooms. Very Modern, sleek and worth the price. Dont confuse this with Palms Hotel. This is this the Palms PLACE Hotel.Rooms: Some of the best. It rivals Aria, Cosmo and yes, even Hard Rock. Clean, modern, sleek, and the beds are amazing. Good view of the strip tooService: couldn't ask for anything betterRoom Service: Top notchWould I stay her again? - I travel to Vegas twice a month, I always stay here because I want piece and quiet and I like the luxury qualityDownfalls - you need to uber/lyft/taxi to the strip... which only takes a few minutes.

allReviews.title: 1975 Concert Weekend
allReviews.text: Resort fee high for the property but the biggest issue were the elevators, completely inadequate to service to the building. Always waiting, forever, no matter what time of day. The in room coffee service was a one cup machine.

allReviews.title: NEVER again - dont do it!
allReviews.text: Just like the previous customer we arrived having travelled 25 hours to be told our room had been cancelled by "an unknown third party" and there were no rooms available. they gave us a room in the Ivory towers - no kitchenette- at an EXTRA cost of 300$ We were exhausted and it was 2am back home so couldnt contact our travel agent. Room was booked in Feb. Travel agent fixed it eventually today. Reception advised us to stay where we were - however we needed a fridge thats why we booked the original room. What a hassel.Still havent got it. Eventually we decided to try out the pool. What kind of idiots run this establishment? We are 57 and 50 and "guests" but had to provide ID in case we wanted a drink from the bar - give me a break!! Ok Id like a little sun so we did that. I went ahead of my husband and took a lounger - half hour later he joined me asked other guests could he take an unoccupied lounger - well the crown jewels are not as well protected. Attendant told him he couldnt take it - he apologised and asked why he couldnt move it 20 feet to my lounger..... the child in charge responds by muttering into his walkie talkie and 2 burly security personnel approach. APPALLING!!!! We left immediatley. I have NEVER been treated so disrepectfully. Unfortunately we cannot just leave this hole right now - we are here on business.

allReviews.title: Loved it!
allReviews.text: My boyfriend & I booked this hotel for 7 nights during the Viva Las Vegas rockabilly weekender as The Orleans & associated hotels had sold out by the time we made the decision to go.For those considering this as an option for next years event (The Orleans sold out whilst we were there), the Gold Coast is within walking distance & they run 24 hour shuttles to The Orleans for VLV.We had no issues with checking in - very smooth process & were even offered an upgrade at a special price. We declined & I'm glad we did as the basic room that we had booked more than met our needs.We were on the 12th floor with views of the Palms Casino & the Strip (no access to the balcony for 'security reasons' though). The room was massive. Easily bigger than my 1 bed flat at home! We had a spacious bathroom with separate whirlpool bath & rainfall shower. Toiletries were provided & more could be requested from Reception.There was a kitchen area with mini-bar, fridge & dishwasher. Be warned - do not even open the door to the mini-bar! We opened the door before we realised there was a fridge below where we could put our water & even doing this must have activated a sensor as a bottle of water showed up on our final bill. This was however removed by the Receptionist without argument when we checked out.The king-size bed is one of the most comfortable I have ever slept in & we both slept very well (after we put in ear plugs to drown out the very effective AC).The living area was also spacious & comfortable & we ended most nights just sat on the sofa with a night cap looking at the view.The room itself was clean, tidy & didn't show any signs of wear & tear. The 2 large flat screen TV's in the living room & the little TV in the bathroom (which the boyfriend thought was hilarious to watch when he was in the bath) showed a range of American channels. You could also view your hotel bill on the TV's.Housekeeping were lovely & friendly - nothing seemed like too much trouble for them. The few times that we spoke to reception (trying to figure out how to log onto the free Wi-Fi) they were also very friendly & helpful. With regard to food, I would definitely recommend the buffet at the Palms Casino. We stayed 2 nights at the Golden Nugget in downtown following a mini road trip to Arizona & was surprised that their buffet was more expensive & didn't include beer & wine at lunch & dinner.We ate at the buffet at least once a day for breakfast, lunch or dinner & all meals had a large variety of quality, hot, well presented food. The staff here were also very friendly & helpful & kept topping up our drinks - even the mimosas when we went for Sunday brunch :)There is a complimentary daily shuttle bus from The Palms Casino down to Caesar's Palace Forum. It runs from 11-8 & you just have to show your room key to the driver. The Casino is easily accessible from Palms Place by a 'sky tube' as they called it. Go to floor 2 & follow the corridor round. Keep going over the travelators & down the lift at the end & this will bring you out in the casino. Keep to the left, walk past the Sports Bar & another bar & you'll come to the main entrance where the shuttle picks up/drops off.The one night we spent on the Strip, we got the last shuttle over there &, if you get a taxi back from The Mirage, you avoid having to go onto the Strip & get stuck in expensive traffic.All in all, we had a great time at the hotel & didn't feel too disadvantaged about not being on the Strip. We have decided to go back to Vegas again &, if we couldn't get a Strip hotel (it has to be done after all), we wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.PS we did find the whole resort fees thing a bit confusing. Travel Republic offered the room at a much cheaper rate but didn't mention resort fees whereas booking.com had the room at a higher rate but this included some fees. Be careful to read the small print so you know what you are getting as part of the nightly rate.

allReviews.title: Not the worse, or best
allReviews.text: The Studio Suite was nice, but I don't think the Palms Place will be my first choice my next trip to Vegas. Spacious, however there were too many little things "wrong." The whole left wall did not have electricity so my lamps, clocks, and outlets didn't work (which was inconvenient when we were looking to charge phones and tablet). By the time I was unpacked and realized it, it would've been another inconvenience to move to another room.Also, they provide an iPod dock so guests can play music... However it is outdated and doesn't fit any model past an iPhone 4 (which hasn't been sold for over a year). So we just blasted music from our cell phones the best we could, but had to keep it in the same spot since I could only charge my phone on one side of the room.It was also an inconvenience that there was not a dresser or any place other than the closet to put clothes. There were shelves under the tv, which left all the wires exposed (tacky in my opinion) since there was no cover, and didn't have any drawers for me to place my intimates and folded clothes. I expected more for a Palms hotel. How do you accept pets but not have smoking rooms? It's all a preference I suppose. It was also a HUGE bummer that the outside door was locked and didn't allow guests out on the balcony. It was tease to have a balcony, but not be able to walk out and enjoy it. At least have a window to crack for some fresh air.

allReviews.title: Million Dollar Views-spacious, modern
allReviews.text: We stay for $53 plus $25 resort fee.  Got a room on the 26th floor, facing the strip.  Incredible view.  This property is a little older but can't really see it.  I believe units are individually owned, but seems like they are kept standard with same furnishings.  Our room was huge.  Full kitchen, which we didn't use.  Very modern bathroom with rain shower and large jetted tub.  Two big screen TVs.  King bed (very comfy), and an L-shape sofa.  One good restaurant.  But Palms Place adjoins The Palms.  This is where you'll find the casino, buffet restaurant (breakfast included in our rate), a food court, big pool area, Hooters, another 24-hour cafe, and the fabulous Ghostbar.Only drawback for some might be that it's a few miles off the strip.  But that's why the view is so great.  Get a rental car.  Very inexpensive and parking is easy.

allReviews.title: Very good hotel with hidden charges
allReviews.text: I reserved a room and paid several days in advance. When I arrived , they charged me extra $33 "hotel fee". Why? I did not have time to argue and payed.  It's not honest. I reserved hotels online hundreds times and always paid only amount shown at time of reservation.

allReviews.title: Great Room, not so great location
allReviews.text: When I first arrived, it was late and they couldn't find my reservation.  I had prepaid for the room so I knew it was in there somewhere.   It was odd, but after a while, they found it.   By the time I got into the room I was over it.    This is where things turned around though as the room was absolutely beautiful.   It was HUGE too with an incredible view of the strip which was waaaaaaaaay over yonder.    The bed was incredibly comfortable and I slept like a baby, thank goodness.      So the next day I woke up in a much better mood.   I had a convention to attend during the day and again, it was waaaaaaay far away.   I pretty much had to wait for a taxi no less than 10-20 minutes every time I had to go anywhere.    That was pretty frustrating.   On the last day of my stay, I finally had enough time to check out the casino and wow was I disappointed.   At 11pm it was all but empty and those who were there were older, and to me, a little shady.    I was disappointed as i was hoping to watch a bunch of people gambling and having fun.  (I don't gamble but I like to watch those big loud groups playing craps and roulette)       The next day I went to the pool which and had a really nice lunch and a few drinks before heading to the airport for my flight home.   The pool definitely was a redeeming factor, for me anyway.   I was ready to relax and it wasn't loud, wild or crazy.   It was pretty tame for a vegas resort poo.   But like I said, I was ready to relax so it was great for me at the time.   Had I wanted a little more action, I might have been disappointed.

allReviews.title: Nice Interior, Poor Service!
allReviews.text: I was attending a major conference in Vegas, and found this hotel online. Based on their website it seemed to be very nice place to stay, offering various rooms and good deals. I wanted upper floor suite, with all major assets, and nice view of the city at night. I wanted to relax with a drink and sit on the balcony - watching the lights of sin city. The customer service told me (on the phone) that my suite has all of those things, including nice BALCONY WITH A VIEW! Great. So I booked 6 nights, and showed up to find the following: balcony with a view is LOCKED and you cannot access it due to "safety reasons" (the front desk actually said that), the hallway on my floor smelled of marijuana every single day (so strong - that you will get high second hand), missing drinks in the fridge (and they will try to charge you for it), 3 TV sets inside the room, but very POOR cable reception (almost unwatchable)... Plus, the front desk service has some very unprofessional employees who need serious training in customer service (I guess they care only about that rich guy on the top floor who drives Ferrari and gives large tips, so they abandoned middle class guests)... Just sayin' - what I experienced myself. The bottom line is: this hotel looks nice from the outside and has a nice website, but there is clearly FALSE advertising involved here, and you will NOT get what you're paying for (unless you consider free get-high-experience as a nice gift). Oh, did I forget - the faucet handle is broken and a bottle of water costs 6 bucks in the Pool Bar (the pool closes at 6pm, but the advertisement shows "shiny happy people" around the pool enjoying a nice evening around the fire (good acting for sure). I'm a film director, I spot those things... So, my advice is - find the "palm" elsewhere. Peace.

allReviews.title: Las Vegas Best Kept Secret
allReviews.text: This hotel is a five star self catering apartments. It was stunning and so were the views. We were on the 27th floor facing the strip what a view! We checked out of our strip hotel for a cheap weekend just off the strip. We were up Flamingo road which is central to the strip and the strip is so accessible by the free shuttles and a bus out the front of the hotel. The casino is linked at Palms you just walk through the sky walk. The pool was quiet and in a sunny position it was so peaceful. The rooms are outstanding with two TVs in studio one in front of the bed and one in the lounge area. There was even a TVs in the bathroom. There was a spa bathe and a walkin spa shower. I would definately stay here again and look forward to booking this later this year. The best kept secret in Vegas and you won't be disappointed.

allReviews.title: Good, would recommend to others
allReviews.text: Everything was fine; I was there solo for work and liked being off the strip. Lovely spa, gym, pool. The only thing was that i had a wonderful terrace but the door was locked and they said I wasnt allowed to use it, bummer! Wish there was more coffee in the room.

allReviews.title: Will Not Stay Again
allReviews.text: I actually like the rooms at the Palms Place and Spa, but I find the front desk staff to be one of the worst I've experienced.  Having traveled all of my adult life for work, one comes to expect basic things... like having the room I reserved available.   More than once, I have been informed that I need to pay for an upgrade or I can have the room I reserved at the Palms Casino... not acceptable.   I'm tired of "rolling the dice," so to speak on whether my room type will be "mine" at check in.  Even though I arrived after midnight, I cancelled my room and moved to another hotel.  They don't deserve my money for the room... or for gambling at their casino.  Goodbye Palms...

allReviews.title: Nice hotel would stay again
allReviews.text: We've been to Vegas a lot never stayed at the Palms thought we would try this resort it was a nice surprise.This is hotel is located near the Palms casino which you can access by an indoor walkway which is convenient and if your not a fan of staying in casinos this is great for you.We like having fridge and microwaves because sometimes we just come to chill and don't always want to go out so always nice to have somewhere to store snacks.The room is set up great has everything you will need, 2 tvs large, couch/living area as well as a balcony with a great view of the strip.Bedding is excellent as are the linens, towels and water pressure in the shower was greatWe enjoyed the the hotel and amenities will stay again, was a little surprised that some of the areas were over looked, needs some touch ups done in the rooms.The tub areas was moldy due to the tub and shower being enclosed, needs to be redone asap.But a nice stay off the strip and a great condo set up, fitness facilities were great, didn't use the pool as it was cold.Wifi was included in the usual resort fee scam

allReviews.title: Absolutely magical
allReviews.text: I am an Expedia Elite Plus card holder, the highest tier I believe of their rewards program (which isn't saying much), but Palms Place is a Expedia VIP Hotel. I had a corner 1 bedroom suite for five days, and it was one of the most brilliant experiences in Vegas, and I am there A LOT. Don't listen to these negative reviews. Sure its a bit off strip, (ohhh watch out a few blocks), there is always the ample shuttle. The resort is so quiet, and the Suite at Palms was heavily insulated for the ultimate in privacy. The layout of the corner room is stellar. If you are going to base not booking there on tiny negatives about frosted shower doors, etc, then you really are in the wrong town. The place is extraordinary. I will never stay anywhere else (save Mandalay Bay), when I go to Vegas. Treat yourself, it's simply an oasis to escape to and into.

allReviews.title: Hotel okey
allReviews.text: We checked in at this hotel in las vegas,as my daughter already had a good experience in staying at this hotel.true enough, its home away from home..the only thing i dislike is the bathroom.though its clean and tidy. In the  toilet bowl area.. It smells stinky, and i see no dirt, but the smell gets inside my nose, i still need to spray a little perfume to lessen the odor. Maybe they need an exhaust to fix the problem.i also like the location, its not along the strip, which was so crowded almost always, and this hotel is also near to many restaurants which are not so expensive.

allReviews.title: Going down hill
allReviews.text: I have stayed at Palm Place for many years and have enjoyed it until this last stay. Furniture falling apart, toe nail clipping in the carpet room not clean. Customer service not the same as it used to be.

allReviews.title: Palms
allReviews.text: Too far away from all of the action.  Rooms are very nice.  Spacious, clean and modern.  They need more people working the front desk.  It can get little spooky at night because it's so dead quiet.  Wouldn't wanna stay here again

allReviews.title: Clean but so many issues!!!
allReviews.text: The place is clean, and the beds are triple sheeted, but we had so many issues I would have a hard time returning.  This place is so dark it is almost dangerous; even with every light on in our room it was too dark to see- esp the bathroom when putting on makeup. Perhaps it is to hide the 70's veneer furniture that is so dinged and damaged I was shocked it was still in use. We had a suite which I believe is the standard room, but the kitchen has nothing in it but a broken leaky coffee pot. They don't even have towels or anything to use in the kitchen, which is ok since all we found were 2 mismatched coffee cups. Not even a fork to eat my leftovers from a restaurant. They never restocked our coffee or toiletries either.      We had breakfast included with our room but the wait time was so long it made it impossible to utilize. We waited  over 45 minutes in line with only 9 people in front of us; by the time we were seated they had stopped breakfast so we were stuck with the dregs. It was strange because there were at least 20 empty tables, and yet we waited.  Once seated we waited 10 minutes for lukewarm  coffee served in a paper cup. Never got a refill or top off despite asking twice. It did look like a nice breakfast from what we could see from the remains. The staff acted like we were a bother at the restaurant and pool, and you can't sit in the shade without a hefty fee.  We have been to Vegas many times but this place may as well have been a Motel 6! I can't recommend this place- I don't require a lot over cleanliness and some basics but come on,  at least deliver what you promise- even the "free" wi-fi" was a joke unless you paid dearly for the normal speed.

allReviews.title: Nice and comfort place
allReviews.text: My wife and me went on vac. last November and we booked a fly with hotel, so we really did'n know what to expect from the hotel, the price was really good to be true, so I look at the pics and everything looks awesome, but you know how are the sites when talk about pics, sometimes they are fake. Well we drop the coin to the air and went there, we were surprise to find a nice and luxury hotel and Spa as the palms place, room clean, big and a huge hot tube, 2 flat tv's, the bed soft, kitchen also clean.  The personal always kind and the best part its connected to palms hotel, so you have movie theater, hall concert, fast food area, casino, night club and so many more things to do.  They have a shuttle from hotel to Cesar's Palace, which save you lots of many on cabs, and from there you can move to anywere.

allReviews.title: Great spacious premium room
allReviews.text: Room was very spacious, clean and modern. Amazing bathroom. House keeping do an excellent job. Fast wifi. Swimming pool could be cleaner.Watch out for extra charges - resort fee per day. Otherwise great stay. Staff are friendly.

allReviews.title: Awsome Pool
allReviews.text: A Diamond in the rough! Listen the Palms Place just doesn't get the kind of credit it should. I'm guilty myself that I haven't gave them much of a chance because after being spoiled on the strip with MLIFE and all the MGM hotels I really had no need to stay here. My only gripe would be the customer service but I won't ding them too bad because the property and pool is beautiful. I came here last week for a private party that hosted a pool party. When I walked in and asked the front desk or concierge person about this party they apparently didn't know anything about it and the lady was rather rude about it. Gave me a look like I was from outer space. Weird but anyways it's a good thing that another guest standing by knew something about the pool party and was able to direct me in the correct place. Not the job of a guest but sure glad they knew because I wouldn't have got up. You would think that for big events everybody would be in the loop but that wasn't the case. The pool itself was amazing and the entire property was so clean. We went also into one of the suites and again just spectacular! No complaints on that end. If you are wanting something off the strip and away from all the strip craziness then this would be the place!

allReviews.title: Lots of Flash, but Lacking Some Substance
allReviews.text: I am the type of person that doesn't spend a lot of time in his hotel.  I use it as a "home base" to go see things and then come back and crash.  As far as that is concerned, this hotel was fantastic as it was reasonably priced, didn't not have an exorbitant resort fee, had a convenient location for both getting into the main parts of the Strip quickly and also for getting out of town.  The valet was quick at getting the car and made it easy to hand off my car to be parked.In regards to the hotel itself, it is definitely very flashy.  The drive up to the valet will be met with a lot of hot cars parked outside; in the time I was there (3 nights), I saw a McClaren, Rolls Royce, several Ferraris, a Lamborghini, and the like.  Additionally, Nicholas Cage was supposedly staying at the hotel.Customer Service could be a little slow at times -- or non-existent if you tried to call the valet or something; it was better to just walk down and hand them the ticket -- but everyone seemed friendly and they got the job done.I did not get to see the pool on account of other activities and windy weather that closed the pool area.We had a room on the 52nd floor and the view was awesome even though we weren't looking at the strip.  Unfortunately, this was a little hamstrung by the fact that they have a balcony, but lock the balcony doors.  The room was spacious and elegant-looking.  The bathroom was big and the shower was awesome, with the ability to do both overhead and snake head shower; even at the same time -- or take a bath.Upon closer inspection of things, however, some of the amenities seem a little dated, such as a TV in the bathroom that takes DVDs.  Additionally, simple things like turning on the lights or plugging in your phone charger or trying to connect an Amazon Fire Stick to the television seemed overly difficult.  There are two refrigerators, one for your use and one stocked full of alcohol and the like.  The one for personal use wasn't bad except that there was no way to get it to stop making ice, which was not only a bit noisy at times, but if I wanted to use the freezer for something else, it required that I dumped the ice out first and then expect more ice to be dumped on top of whatever I put in there.The Internet Wi-Fi was free, so long as you want really slow Internet.  You have to pay up to $15 a day to get Internet as fast as my cellular; I just used my phone as a hotspot to stream movies instead.The bed was really comfortable, but the pillows left a bit to be desired.The room does have a stove top and a nice counter, but with rather uncomfortable seats to sit in.  There were two televisions in the room: one in front of the couch area and one in front of the bed.  I didn't bother using the couch and/or the second television as it didn't make much sense for the two of us -- we'd rather lay and bed and watch the other television -- and the couch was rather uncomfortable anyway.One definitely plus of the room is it seemed to be completely sound proof.  I can't recall hearing anything outside of my own room, ever, and never felt like I might be impinging on others if I had my television loud.The casino is not in the hotel, but it is very close by; besides, if you're like me, you tire of casinos quickly and it is actually nice to walk into the hotel and not be met with one.All-in-all, for the things that I did in Vegas and the convenience it provided, I would likely stay in this hotel again.

allReviews.title: Upscale hotel but a but worn and rough around the edges
allReviews.text: Overall our stay was great. Everything from the check in staff to the valet/door attendants to room service to check out. We never ran across a staff person that was unfriendly.Rooms are large and bathroom/shower was very nice. We had a great view of the strip but they lock the balcony door which sucks because we could not enjoy standing out there and enjoy the cool morning and evenings. We stayed there because they had balconies but if I knew we could not have used them I would have stayed elsewhere.Room was clean enough, a few very minor details were overlooked but I'm very picky so most people would not even notice. Our room had Dishwasher, stove, microwave , blender, toaster, fridge  and coffee maker.

allReviews.title: The dumb blonde of hotels!
allReviews.text: I've stayed at this hotel 11 of the past 13 weeks as my company has a corporate rate and I have no choice.  All style no substance.  Great looking rooms.  Very stylish.  But that's it.  There is nothing comfortable about it. Lousy couch, lumpy beds and horrible pillows.  Bag that "they don't want you in the room" Las Vegas rhetoric. There is no casino (except the adjacent Palms).  Customer Service is non-existent.  If there is 1 person in line or 15 you get one front desk associate.  The other associates do a great job of not noticing the line and moving quickly away from the front desk as they pass.  Because I arrived on the same day and time each week, the same guy checked me in 9 times.  He still asked me every time "have you stayed with us before?".  My response of, yes XXXX, you checked me in for the past 4 weeks wasn't even met with a knowing glance up.  Just the robotic "well welcome back".  That said, this is most definitely not a complaint.  In fact I find the entire thing kid of funny.  It's a good hotel.  Just like every other hotel room in Vegas.  "Average".

allReviews.title: Feels like home
allReviews.text: I've stayed at the Main Palms hotel this is on the other side which is more of a residential section. ( it's a bit of a walk to get to this side it's like a maze but after a while you get use to it) I have to say the rooms are way better and the suites are ridiculous!!! The only thing is you do not have access to the balcony. Which defeats the purpose of the beautiful view of Vegas. The restaurants at the Palms are to die for. Ghost bar was pretty cool at night but the day party on Saturday was off the hook!! I usually took an uber to go to the strip it's much cheaper. I will definitely will be staying on this section of the palms.

allReviews.title: Awesome
allReviews.text: I found a deal for the Palms Place online and was initially hesitant because it wasn't on The Strip, but the deal was too good to pass up! I am so glad I jumped on the deal! The room was gorgeous and very clean! The bathroom was amazing: jetted soaking tub, waterfall shower head, tv! Since it was a family stay, I greatly appreciated that we didn't have to walk through a smoky casino to get to our room! The pool area was gorgeous, but we didn't get to spend much time there because there was a very chilly wind most days! I would definitely recommend this hotel!

allReviews.title: Big rooms. That's it.
allReviews.text: Stayed here because our booking at the Hard Rock was messed up. If you're traveling without a car be prepared to drop a lot on taxis to get around the place as the Palms is a long way from anywhere. The studio suite was big, a little worn but well appointed. I'm not sure why you'd ever need 2 TV's next to another but just go with it. It's a shame there is no balcony access but I understand a few have ruined it for everyone. Perhaps glazing out the balconies would ensure guest safety and provide adequate access.

allReviews.title: Great hotel!
allReviews.text: Awesome Hotel! Great fitness area! Accomodating staff, clean and big rooms that do not smell like smoke! Not a young party scene here. The shuttle is perfect arrives on the 1/2 hour, takes you into Caesars Palace forum shops. Uber is about $5-7 from the hotel to the strip.

allReviews.title: Enjoyable
allReviews.text: Nice place. They have a shuttle between Palms and Caesars Palace, but you must show room key. Spacious room. Mini kitchen with fridge and dish washer. Plenty of closet space. Room had a balcony but the door to it was locked.

allReviews.title: Better than a casino hotel room
allReviews.text: The room was awesomely decorated and laid out. 2 flat screen tvs, gas fireplace, full kitchen. Pretty sweet views of the palms towers and the strip. 2 large balconies that weren't accessible to guests anymore. The amenities were bare to say the least (full kitchen yet only 2 coffee mugs and 2 small glasses, upon asking for more the front desk said we had to pay for them?) The front desk and management staff weren't very helpful either. Our original room that we got thru Expedia wasn't going to be ready due to a maintenance issue and instead of doing their best to fix the situation, the front desk was just going to put us in lesser rooms. Obviously not ideal so after my wife made a few direct comments they magically found us ideal rooms on a lower floor. Given all the choices in Vegas, I don't think we'd stay here again.

allReviews.title: Palms Hotel Review
allReviews.text: We stayed in the older section, not the towers, in a room with 2 queen beds.  Even though we reserved a king, they had evidently overbooked their rooms.  We didn't use any of the "resort" amenities, like pool, etc.  Our room was facing the strip.  The beds were just ok, the pillows were hard and uncomfortable (kink in neck in the morning), the bathroom was adequate, however, the sink was very slow draining, cheap toiletries, no shower cap, and the shower door was European style i.e.  the "half" shower door where the shower water runs over the edge of the floor--not a good design for comfortably using the shower, but probably pretty cheap to build.  The bed sheets were rough, and I doubt they even cleaned the coverlet on the bottom of each bed for awhile.  All in all, it was a basic, "bare bones", cheap Las Vegas hotel room. I will not be returning to the Palms anytime soon.

allReviews.title: upgraded to palms place-LOVED IT!!
allReviews.text: very chic and upscale. condo style hotel rooms. They even have door bells.   the room is spacious and had a whirlpool tub-we didn't want to leave.   Great romantic valentine's weekend.  One drawback was the balcony os inaccessible...it looked nice and had room but you cannot use them :(

allReviews.title: Great place, and free strip shuttle!
allReviews.text: From the moment we walked in to the moment we checked out I was in love.  Unlike the Casino hotels in Las Vegas you walk in, hop on the elevator, and there you are! The elevators are fast, and there are no long waits.  Now, the room.... everything you need, and for sure more!  Fridge separate from the mini bar, cook top, microwave, coffee maker, dishwasher, toaster, oh my goodness, and thats just the kitchen. Now, the bathroom the usual, toilet, sink, tv, hair dryer...now for the good stuff!! The shower is a stand alone shower with a rainshower shower head and also a detachable shower head.  You can switch between the 2, whatever you prefer which is nice. Next to the shower is the tub, or mini pool, mini hot tub, however you want to play it.  It is for sure big enough for 2 people, the jets work, and everything is clean! Moving on the bedroom/living area the bed is super comfy, more than enough lighting, seating, and storage space.  There are 2 tvs, 1 for the bed area, and 1 for the living area so that is 3 tvs total in this studio.  The balcony is locked off so you cant actually go out, but the floor to ceiling windows allow for an amazing view of the strip and mountians...beautiful!So, Palms Place is connected to the Palms so you dont have the crowds, but it is easy to get to the food, bars, clubs, and casino.  The Sky Tube allows you to walk between the 2 without going outside.  It is a bit of a walk, but its nice to not have to deal with the desert elements.  You are off the strip, but they offer a free shuttle that takes you down.  You are picked up in the casino are of The Palms, and they drop you off at The Forrum Shops which is where you will be picked up when you are ready to head back.  They do only offer the shuttle between certian hours, but its enough to get you to the strip for free.All said and done highly recommend Palms Place! Can't wait to return

allReviews.title: Chic Trendy Hotel and Casino
allReviews.text: Large stylish room with sleek kitchenettes and also great views of the city. Definitely a hotel for adults not so much for children. Although the few dining places we tried were upscale and good, the Palms could benefit by having more dining choices.

allReviews.title: Great View With So Much To Do!
allReviews.text: The problem with so many resorts on the Strip is that they are often overpriced.  And while large resorts are impressive and easy to admire, they aren't convenient for someone staying there.  Palms Place isn't huge but it offers a lot and it's where you want to go when you honestly want to relax and intermittently enjoy Vegas life.  Transportation to the strip is offered for guests so getting there isn't a problem.  Definitely take advantage of this since it's not a nice walk to the strip and doesn't cater to pedestrians.  The view of the strip is gorgeous and you can see all the way from the Stratosphere down to Mandalay Bay easily.  We were on the 23rd floor and our panoramic view was lovely.  Getting to the Palms is accomplished via an indoor walkway.  The Palms itself has a food court and many dining areas.  It has a movie theater and nice bars and lounges.  With the Gold Coast and the Rio nearby, there's a lot to do if you're staying at Palms Place.  Our room was gorgeous with a nice modern look.  It's very spacious and looks inviting.  There's a kitchenette and dining area so eating in the room feels comfortable.  The room has 3 TVs.  One in the living area where you can relax on the corner couch.  The corner couch is also a great place to relax and read with the adjustable lamp lights.  Another TV is found across from the bed and yet another is in the bathroom to watch while you get ready.  The bed is comfortable and if you like having lots of pillows the Palms has every other place beat.  I think it was a bit of overkill and we threw most of the pillows on the couch and didn't need that many.  The bathroom is really nice.  You have a nice hot tub with adjustable strengths on the jets.  On top of that, the jets have different modes.  One mode causes undulating waves or you can simply enjoy the constant stream of pressurized water giving you a massage.  There's a detachable shower head or you can use the shower head on the ceiling for a nice simulation of rain.  If the bathroom had twin vanities it would've been perfect.  We didn't get to check in early and I'm used to that at all other resorts.  I've usually been allowed to check in anywhere from 30 minutes to 2 hours early.  I understand that our room wasn't ready and at least we didn't check in late.  They held our bags for us no problem and the lounge was a great place to wait and relax.  The next time I feel like relaxing in Vegas, Palms Place will be a heavy contender.  It's worth the visit in every way I can imagine.

allReviews.title: Meh
allReviews.text: We booked this place as an 'off the strip' non-gaming hotel in order to get away from the casino vibe in LV. Much to our chagrin, we discover that there is no breakfast restaurant in the non-gaming wing- instead we have to go into a nasty casino to get a coffee in the morning. The room was stale and cold, cheap, fake wood floors, scratched up from use, laminate countertops, and scratchy sheets. The 'resort fee' does not cover use of the gym, and if the pool is closed (which is was), then let's be honest, its just a deferred cost to the room. So we're off the strip, with casino based food options, near a strip mall- worst of both worlds. The staff at the desk were nice, which counts for something.

allReviews.title: Great hotel for the price!
allReviews.text: My husband and I were passing through Las Vegas on our way home and selected this hotel due to location and price. We were pleasantly surprised by the hotel when we arrived. Initially I was a but concerned because we were not staying on or closer to the strip, however an $8 uber ride cured that concern quickly.  They also have a shuttle from The Palms Hotel & Casino to Caesar's Palace.  The only downfall is the last shuttle is at 8 pm. We took the shuttle to CP and then uber back. The hotel is just a block down the road from the Palms Hotel & Casino. They offer complimentary valet with welcome gratuity. The lobby of the hotel is simple yet modern and has a small bar and hotel shop. We enjoyed a drink at the bar before heading to our room and found it to be pleasant. Our room was on the 9th floor which was quiet, spacious, contemporary, and very well situated facing the strip. The bathroom was large and cleanly decorated in marble and glass. Overall we were quite please with this hotel! Though off the strip you can save quite a bit on your stay and spend a little each way to uber to the strip and back.  Definitely would stay there again!

allReviews.title: First visit to The Palms...
allReviews.text: This is our first visit to the Palms. Valet and check-in was easy, and simple. Nice to be greeted with a smile and some real friendliness. We booked through Expedia, and we were granted a 2pm late check. That was unexpected and nice perk. We were given a 50th floor room with a view.  Nice full kitchen room, although you had to request plates, glasses, and utensils. They had now problem bring them up promptly.  Some great dining options, with a food court for munchie time or feeding the kids. Full casino options, however not sure if they have a poker room. Recommend for a great weekend!

allReviews.title: The condo suites are the best...
allReviews.text: We booked a great deal on the condo suites which are 600 sq feet. Living area beside bed. Big screen, wifi and a small but very useful kitchen. Bathroom was large,clean and had a over sized tub. Staff were pleasant and profesional. Great restaurants in hotelshort drive to the strip without any traffic dilemmas. Over all way better than many hotels on the strip unless you are willing to pay top dollar.

allReviews.title: Vegas Trip
allReviews.text: The Studio room was excellent!! very clean & comfortable! The casino is excellent! restaurant were on point! Didn't like that the beautiful balcony was locked with a key for guests and if your were not an owner it could not be opened per the front desk! Also the WIFI is paid for service.

allReviews.title: Superb Rooms!  Palms Place is in an oasis away from the typical Vegas scene, but close enough to Palms Casino
allReviews.text: Superb Rooms!  Palms Place is in an oasis away from the typical Vegas scene, but close enough to Palms Casino

allReviews.title: A little below average
allReviews.text: We stayed there for 3 nights in response to a promotion that included breakfast. The pictures marketing the hotel are quite deceiving. The rooms although spacious are not nearly as beautiful and glamorous as their pictures show. The hotel is unappealing. The lobby is huge and empty, like a train station. The rooms are not well taken care of. Our room looked very tired. The beautiful wood like floor had a lot of scratches and really the room was not spotless. One day they didn't even wash the soap dish. The breakfast buffet is located in the casino that is connected to the hotel by a long and impersonal walkway. The buffet food is very average. The bed was comfortable. I will not stay there again.

allReviews.title: Quiet, Clean, and Very nice rooms!
allReviews.text: I spent a trade show trip at the Palms Place Hotel.  The trade show was at the Sands, so it wasn't exactly the closest to the location, but that wasn't bad.  Thank goodness for Uber.  be forwarned that when using Uber, they default to the Palms Casino entrance which is a bout a 2-3 min walk.  The room was very nice and modern, with a kitchen and great view of the mountains.  Towels were always fresh and every day for the 5 days i was there it was very clean.  House keeping was very cordial and friendly.  I liked the button to inform them of a do not disturb or house keeping.  I had two TV's but only one had sound. not that it mattered to me, i didn't watch much TV during my stay.  You have to walk (moving walkway) from the Palm Place to the Palm Casino to eat and get to the casino, vending and bank machines..  Remember that you need to get off on the 2nd floor of palms place to get to the moving walkway.. then take the elevator down to the main floor of the casino.I managed to get to the pool area.  Seemed very nice, but it was too cold during my stay in vegas.Not alot of local walking distance things to do in the area.  WiFi was free with the room, but it was only at 1MB.. way too slow.. that would be my only complaint.  My cell phone LTE service was faster. if i wanted faster i had to pay 6-12$ per day.. not going to happen.Overall i enjoyed my stay and would come back again.

allReviews.title: Beautiful room but disappointing features
allReviews.text: Was really excited to stay here, but was disappointed in a few things. The room was large, great furniture and views, also quiet and relaxing.However: the balconies are all locked. So no access is allowed. I was very excited to use the hot tub at their pool, but it closes at 5. A little early for Vegas no? I understand 10pm, or heck even 7... But 5pm? So instead we used our jacuzzi tub for relaxing, but the water smelled like mildew. In fact the next day the entire bathroom smelled of mildew just from using the tub once. Also, no ice makers, and our freezer was broken, so we had to call room service every time we needed ice. And no free wifi like I understood there would be.With a few adjustments catered toward their visitors, this place COULD be amazing.

allReviews.title: Overnight
allReviews.text: The studios are sleek and modern. Two TVs and luxury shower. Bed sleeps well and kitchen is practice and useful.  Nice views of western Vegas away from the strip.  I would recommend this place.  Use Priceline or their website to get a good deal.  I was on the 25th floor.

allReviews.title: Nice, but very dark
allReviews.text: The room was very nice and gave an exceptional view of the Las Vegas Strip.  The casino was quite a walk as well as the buffet restaurant and food mall area but still very nice.  The hotel was very dark...which may work for others but felt very depressing. My first night there - the front desk gave away my room key to another guest who walked in while I was sleeping - then they called me to say I was in the wrong unit.  Really?  So of course that deactivated my key and since my husband couldn't sleep - he walked downstairs and when he returned couldn't get in the room. Again front desk called me and asked me if my husband was staying with me. Duh.  Bad first experience - but rest of stay went smoothly.

allReviews.title: Very comfortable without all the headaches from the Strip!
allReviews.text: Upon arrival, I was created with a warm smile and great sense of humor from the lovely young lady at the front desk. The check in process was quick and painless without that HUGE line that you'll get from most of the hotels you get on the strip.  It was like walk up to the counter.. check in.. go upstairs. Why can't every Las Vegas hotel be that easy?    The rooms are beautiful and spacious. The bathrooms have huge jetted tubs with separate shower with rainfall shower head as well as a detachable shower head.  The beds are huge and there's also a living room area with a huge sectional couch. The kitchenette has a fridge, separate mini bar, sink, microwave, electric range, and even a dishwasher. We mostly used the microwave and fridge, but I think if you need more kitchenware, you have to call housekeeping. There's also a couple glasses, mugs and a coffeemaker. There's also a safe in the closet!   The 6th floor has another restaurant (which looks like amazing burgers!) a spa, gym, and pilates studio. I was so busy this trip, I didn't have time to take advantage of the workout facility, and it was too chilly to use the pool. But it looks amazing!   The 2nd floor has a sky bridge that leads to the main Palms hotel/casino which has more restaurants, fast food court, and movie theater.    We decided to stay and extra night, so extending my room was quick and hassle free.  The housekeeping staff were very respectful to the do not disturb sign (which is a switch you turn on or off), but long story short, this is one of my favorite places to stay in Vegas. It's clean, swanky, great staff, close enough to the strip to still be by the action, but far enough to be away from the craziness. I can't wait to stay here again!

allReviews.title: Cheap.  Time for a refresh.
allReviews.text: I knew I made a poor choice when the hotel marquis boasted Panda Express and Hooters.  The rooms were big but tired.  Chipped furniture, dusty.  A half eaten snickers bar in the fridge upon arrival was gross.  Being charge for the half eaten bar was a problem (they did remove it from the bill).  It is work mentioning that The Palms Place has no restaurants and room service is served in "to go" containers.  You can walk from The Palms Place to the Palm but fast food is all you can get for breakfast.  Would not stay there again.

allReviews.title: Beautiful Room, Wi-Fi Disappointment
allReviews.text: We were greeted upon check in with very friendly staff. They kindly gave us a room on the 33rd floor after I asked if we could have a room with a good view. The room was clean, spacious, and had a gorgeous view of the strip. The bathroom had a jetted tub and separate shower with 2 shower heads. There were 2 large flat screen TV's in the main area, and a small flat screen in the bathroom. There was a full kitchen (with utensils, supplies on request), an in room safe and large sofa. Our only complaint was that free wi-fi was advertised as part of the resort fee, and we had none. I tried resolving this with the front desk multiple times with no resolution. We were greatly disappointed by this. Also, the room has a blow dryer, coffee maker, toaster, dishwasher, sink, microwave, fridge with a mini bar, and 2nd empty fridge for your items.

allReviews.title: Epic Vegas trip
allReviews.text: We stayed at Palms Place for three nights at the end of our 4 weeks in the USA. Visiting Vegas was by far one of the highlights of our entire trip.Plans place was a fantastic place to stay. We got a great deal on one of the Studios, which was amazing. Bed, sofa, TV, bathroom (including great bath and shower) all luxurious and top quality. Recommended as a great value option for staying at one of the top hotels in Vegas.Off the strip location was quite refreshing and probably gave the more relaxed feel of the casino and pools. Really easy to travel to and from using the hotel shuttle. Taxi costs hardly anything to get back late at night. We spent more time at the rooftop pool in palms place, which was great. The private booths were all a bit worn down, but they were all reserved anyway despite no one using them! Absolutely brilliant pool for chilling by though.The time of year we went meant there wasn't as much going on in the hotel - less parties and events due to the run up to the halloween festivities, but I think this actually meant for a really relaxed stay at the hotel. We made up for this when we went out on the strip though!Casino was also great from the perspective of someone that doest play much else other than blackjack! Isn't as much traffic through there, more relaxed and less pressured than the main casinos in Vegas. We went to the rooftop bar the first night, which has stunning views of the strip, and is a great place for drinking and dancing. Didn't visit the other bar as we went out the other nights.Otherwise, interns of other recommendations for things in Vegas:We saw a Cirque Du Soleil show - which we couldn't recommend more...probably the most amazing show we have ever seen. Also walked through all the hotels on the strip one night, ending up at the the Paris Las Vegas, with he club at the foot of the Eiffel Tower which was also great.Would highly recommend to anyone visiting Vegas.

allReviews.title: I loved the hotel being separate from the casino!
allReviews.text: I would come back to stay, the location was just what I needed, not on the strip and in a great neighborhood environment. My stay was wonderful. But I had one big problem the tub deep Jacuzzi looked so good, I had to get in and enjoy the comfort of a long bath with bubbles. The problem is that there is no handles to hold on to, to get in and out. The tub had no grips to stop you from sliding or slipping. I was a little afraid being by myself it was not safe. I think that the hotel managing team should re-evaluate the jacuzzi grips on the bottom and the handle grips to get in and out is very much needed. Thank you

allReviews.title: Fantastice room view, clean and friendly staff
allReviews.text: Wife and myself just stayed at the Palms Place in Las Vegas for a Builders show. The room was located on the 38th floor and had a fantastic view. You could see the entire Vegas strip along with the surrounding mountain range. Just at 1 mile from the strip center, a quick and cheap UBER ride gets you there. Use UBER, not the taxi service and you'll save drastically. The room itself was very nice, contemporary with a big walk in shower and big tub. The bed is very large and comfortable. Only issue with our room was at night as the temp would fluctuate and you would either be really cold or extremely hot. All in all a fun business trip and we would recommend the Palms Place unless you want to be on the strip.

allReviews.title: Palms Place isn't what it used to be
allReviews.text: I have visited the palms/palms place for the past 4 years with a group of friends booking multiple rooms for an annual guys trip each time booking through the hotels website. The rooms were clean but showing some wear and tear. We usual like Palms place due to their balconies as we like to watch the skyline and shoot the breeze in between gambling. Last year however the balconies were locked. This was brought to the attention of the front desk who couldn't of had more of a so what attitude. I asked to speak with the manager, who's name is Dustin, but he did not offer any explanation of why there shut down eventhough the balconies can be seen in several photos while booking. The only option were given was to upgrade to another room for $800 more per night. Another issue with the palms is the casino and clubs within are not popular at all anymore. From Friday to Tuesday none of the venues had a significant crowd. Also, please use the in room safe. I left a necklace in the room and after cleaning service, it came up missing. The front desk did radio the maid but to no avail. This year we will move our guys trip to strip, since the amenities we liked about the palms are no longer available.Safe travels!!!

allReviews.title: Great place off the Strip
allReviews.text: This property is nice and away from the Strip and somewhat of a walk to the main Palms Casino but it's all connected.We arrived around 1AM after delays and other issues getting into Vegas. The staff at the front was great and so was the Valet service. The nice attendant at the desk upgraded us when asked to a Penthouse.All around the penthouse was a great room, wish we had more time to enjoy it. We had a large kitchen and eat in area, living room and bed room along with a large bath with steam shower. We also had a balcony that overlooked the mountains along with a spa with glass wall.

allReviews.title: First Time
allReviews.text: I travel a great deal, more than 200 nights per year.  Vegas has lost it's appeal to me from a vacation perspective, mostly due to coming to work trade shows several times per year.  With that said, I avoid the strip unless I absolutely have to stay on it.  This is the first time staying at this hotel after visiting it in November to get away from the strip.  I have to say, there are good and bad things about it.  Being realistic, no hotel is perfect.  With that said, the good:The 1BR suite I upgraded to on the 50th floor was spectacular.  You walk into marble floors, spacious living room and a very nice kitchen area.  The bedroom has a large jet tub and plenty of closet space.  The bathroom (the full one after I found a half one right when you walk in the door) has two shower heads and waterfall head above you.The bad, the carpet had repaired and you could see the seam.  The shower handle broke off when I turned it on, but maintenance fixed it by the time I returned to the room.  The shower also had a burned out lightbulb as well.  The sink handle had a leak and would drip when water is running.  Valet is VERY slow to respond, and hardly ever answers the phone if you call. The restaurant on the 6th floor has a limited menu, but spectacular view.  Lastly having two balconies, it was a shame that you are not able to walk out on them because of some crazy hotel policy.Ultimately for the money you cannot beat this place, especially if you are staying of the strip.  Granted, there are things that can be improved upon, but, no hotel is perfect.I more than likely will stay here again next time I am in Vegas, even though I am also tempted to check out some other properties off the strip as well.

allReviews.title: A very Nice First Stay...
allReviews.text: Stayed at the Palms Place for the first time earlier in January for work trip.I was upgraded from a studio suite to the one bedroom suite and...my gosh...it was just magnificent.1200 square feet of goodness. 35-301 had a view of Downtown Las Vegas, with partial views of the Strip and mountains.Enjoyed such goodies as the full size refrigerator, triple headed shower, whirlpool tub, and separate bedroom and living areas. There is a balcony but unfortunately they are kept locked unless you own a unit.A couple maintenance issues here and there were taken care of quickly.Access to the main hotel and casino is through a SkyTube on the 2nd level.Cab rides to the Strip are like $10...but the Flamingo Rd double decker city bus goes by frequently and will get you there in 10 minutes. A Day Pass is $5.Planning another trip for the Spring and the Palms Place is definitely on my list...

allReviews.title: The best hotel in Las Vegas
allReviews.text: This was the best hotel!!!!!! This was my husband and I first trip to Las Vegas it started out really bad, upon arriving at the hotel we discovered that my wallet was left on the airplane. Even though I was not allowed to check-in at the moment. Andrea immediately got on the phone and computer to locate the proper people I needed to talk to quickly to resolve this matter. They put our luggage in a safe place until we got back from the airport. My wallet was found!!!!!!! Once we got back to the hotel, due to the fact the we started out having such a hard time on our 5th year wedding anniversary we was upgraded to a one bed room suite. Needless to say it was breathtaking.... ABSOULUTLY BEAUTIFUL!!!!!!! Our stay here was wonderful!!!!! If you think that's all I got think again. Here is probably another reason why every time we come to Las Vegas we will always stay here is because, we ran into some more trouble this time with our card. For whatever reason our card stop working completely the last day in Vegas...Can you all imagine this having no cash!! Oh my goodness this was another most stressful times that I had ever encountered. With our flight leaving almost less than an hour away. Once again our hotel staff pulled together for us and made it happened... Starting with Andrea, headed to manager. While Cam printed off our boarding pass, Paige (manager) set up ride for us to the airport at her expense, and Christian the bellman driving us safely there and making sure we arrive on time. Without this crew at Palms Place our trip could have been so much worst. My husband and I would like to thank you all greatly from the bottoms of our hearts for everything you all did for us. On top of all this the hotel was amazing, the food was amazing the spa was amazing.... I could go on but you people must check it out for yourself. you will not be disappointed....

allReviews.title: Return visit. Same issues. Seeming indifference.
allReviews.text: This was a return visit to the Palms Place and sadly not much had changed since my previous visit. On arriving in the room, there was strange stains on both the couch and the walls - so in credit to the reception they did move us immediately. Strange smell in both the old and new room - I guess the product of having a kitchen so any previous guest who cooks, then you get stuck with the smell.Room just didn't feel clean - albeit incredibly spacious. Shame that the balconies don't open but seemingly a hotel policy. Rates at this hotel always seem cheap, but I just don't think its worth it - especially since you have to trek back and forward to the strip.

allReviews.title: Nice off strip
allReviews.text: I loved this place because it has such a beautiful view of the strip mostly and it has a balcony. I will stay again . It has everything you could possibly want. Not on the strip but that makes the view all the better.

allReviews.title: Spent New Year's Eve in the Palms Place
allReviews.text: This was a great pick if you want to be off the strip! I was a bit skeptical about this hotel after reading a bunch of reviews, but our experience was very different...the Palms Place didn't disappoint! Stay in room 31-306 it has the best view :)

allReviews.title: I Like It Here
