allReviews.text: I really liked this location, the rooms, the atmosphere and the staff. I spent my birthday here and while they have a "no party" policy enjoyed the night and made our way to ghostbar. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. I would recommend this hotel to my friends.

allReviews.title: Mini Apartment
allReviews.text: I have wanted to stay at the Palms for a very long time but Palms Place went beyond my expectations for a hotel in Vegas.  It has a very nice bathroom with a Jacuzzi tub, and a nice kitchen area.  The only draw back was the wifi was only free for one device.

allReviews.title: New Years Eve fun
allReviews.text: I have to say that my initial perception of the check in was NOT enjoyable. After a grueling flight delay (due to de-icing the entire plane) and the insane shuttle ride from the airport to the hotel which took an hour due to the strip being on lock down for NYE, we were told our rooms would not be on the same floor, let alone next door to each other, and we would have to take a double queen room even though we paid for Superior King rooms online a month in advance. When we asked for this to be corrected we were told we would have to  go to the casino side to make room changes as they could not access that part of the computer from their side. So we had to drag all our luggage over to the "other tower" which was no small feat, up the elevator, thru the sky tube, down another elevator, all the way through the entire casino before reaching another desk. Again we were told about the lesser rooms. I politely told the girl this was NOT okay with me. I booked well in advance, paid for king size rooms and requested our friends be in the room next to ours. This was my first trip to Vegas, I was exhausted from all the travel (from Ohio) and delays and I wanted the room I paid for so we could clean up and go enjoy New Years Eve. The young lady immediately sprang into action and went to speak to a manager. It was only a few minutes and she returned to tell us they would take care of this by giving us side by side, upgraded, King size Suites at no extra charge. We had to make the long trek back to the other tower but it was well worth it. The rooms were gorgeous. White marble tiled bathroom, multiple flat screen tvs, Stainless steel appliances in the kitchenette, luxury king bed, contemporary living room and a balcony with a breathtaking view of the mountains from the 51st floor. So even though we had a rough start, The Palms did go above and beyond to salvage my first trip to Las Vegas. Everyone was amazing, and it was so fresh and clean. Just the escape Experience I needed. I highly recommend staying here. It's off strip but well worth it.

allReviews.title: Lots of Other Hotels to Chose From
allReviews.text: My sister and I have stayed several times at the Palms Place.  We liked it because its close to the food fair and slots, has a nice pool that's not too busy and large, apartment style rooms.  The last time we went was in September 2015 and sadly, I believe it will be our last.  Check in took hours - our room wasn't ready.  The large apartment style rooms are looking run down and in need of some TLC. One plus, our balcony door opened so we could enjoy sitting outside)....I'm not sure if this was a mistake, or not as not many balcony doors are unlocked in LV.  It was fun watching police chases with helicopters from our balcony).  The staff at the pools are like gestapo wardens.  If you move your lounge chair an inch, they will be at your side, telling you to move it back.  There were actual arguments between staff and guests at the pool where the Manager had to be called in.  Ridiculous..oh well, got a few free drinks out of the stress of having to listen to loud, angry voices.  I also noticed this time a lot of "undesireables' hovering around the front of the hotel.  Women with not much on and questionable men.  Scoot them away Palms Place!!  Makes your hotel look like a brothel.  So, all in all, there are tons of other hotels in LV.  May be giving this one the miss next time, unless they had some unbelievable rate and the CDN dollar goes up!!

allReviews.title: Only average, lots of other places to stay
allReviews.text: The other reviews hit it on the head.  Palms Place could be really great, but it's just average.  The views are good.  The rooms probably were terrific once.  It is not well maintained, the little things are pretty poor (e.g., bedspread was visibly stained after housekeeping made the bed.  Why didn't you change it?  And after I called at 9 p.m., they never came to change it until the next day or housekeeping.  There is an option to get dishes, which we did.  But housekeeping took them away, and didn't replace.  Etc.  One night roomservice rang the doorbell, we had the privacy light on and didn't order anything.  it was the wrong room)  This would be more than acceptable at a 3 star extended stay hotel (not trying to slam the courtyards of the world, just giving a comp).  But for a purported 4 star/diamond place it is pretty weak.I could go on, but it's really just like the others say.  For a really cheap price, I might consider staying again, but frankly I like so many other places in Las Vegas more -- even off strip -- that it is tough to advocate for another visit to Palms Place.

allReviews.title: Desert Oasis with Phenomenal staff!
allReviews.text: The Palms Place remains my favorite property in all of Las Vegas. We just checked-in tonight, and plan to stay another couple nights. Standards remain stellar, from Valet ("Tom") to the Front desk ("Brendan") and even the PBX (operator "Janet"). The Bellman was exceptional, and went out of his way to provide us with a couple items we left at home. Everyone on staff here is fully invested and committed to making every guest's stay special. Brendan worked magic for us, even after we arrived much later than we expected. He found a beautiful suite overlooking the pool and lights of the city. Our suite has everything you can imagine, including a Cleopatra free-standing jacuzzi tub, full kitchen with dishwasher, sub-zero, two bathrooms a fireplace and even a washer & dryer! Cutlery and dinnerware, including pans, etc., are provided with one quick call to room service. There is even a Waring pro blender with a glass pitcher, Cuisinart toaster and tea pot, etc. The suite is more than roomy, and is actually a luxury apartment (there are full-time tenants residing in several units in this beautiful location). The palms place is incredibly understated and quiet, providing a zen-like environment from the central lobby to the suite. No stale odors, no cigarette smoke, or ringing chaotic casino sounds to greet you upon entering. The entrance to the palms casino is accessed via the skywalk, and everything from nightclubs, restaurants, and even a movie theater is just across the connecting corridor. The palms place has it's own amazing restaurants and spa, private pool with cabanas, etc. The management team is unparalleled and always eager to help make your stay memorable and enjoyable. I am overwhelmed by the reception and hospitality we have received so far, and exceedingly grateful that such a resort still exists in Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: Too Many Hassles
allReviews.text: There is only one elevator in service, it's taking almost 10 minutes for it to arrive at your floor or the lobby. Actually had to skip a show as I hadn't allowed for this 20 minute round trip. The rooms are large and nice, but there is sewer smell in the shower stall. Also it's a tough place to self park, and the valet doesn't seem to be covered by the 38 dollar fee they charge as a hotel fee. They have wood floors that are "floating", so they aren't glued to the floor. So they make noise, at least the one above me is.

allReviews.title: My new favorite place in Vegas
allReviews.text: Vegas is the nearest "big city" to where we live in Utah so we visit frequently to travel or visit specialty doctors. This weekend our dog needed surgery so I searched travel sites for somewhere reasonable to stay for a night. I chose the Palms Place based on price ($79/night for 600 sq ft. studio). I wasn't expecting to be WOWED but let me say that I really thought this was by far the nicest place I've stayed in Vegas. The room was huge, clean, impressive! Our view from the 12th floor had a great view of the strip -- we could see all the way from Luxor to Stratosphere and everything in between. The bathroom totally rocked! The soaking tub was huge and the jets were powerful. nice floors throughout and the bed was SO comfortable!! The room was also really quiet. I appreciated that. We ate at Cafe 6 which was next to the pool. It was really great food! I am pretty hard to impress, but overall this was one of our best trips to Vegas. I'll def stay here again.

allReviews.title: Penthouse Condo overlooking Las Vegas Strip
allReviews.text: We arrived at this hotel at 12am after a long flight.. Purchased our room via Expedia and was already paid for. Come to find out our room had been taken BUT we got upgraded to a fabulous 1200 sqft  penthouse suite that was amazing!This hotel books very quickly and is well worth it because you're less than 7min away from the strip and close the express way and the airport.Our suite had a FULL stainless steel kitchen! The only thing I would suggest is for the rooms to come equipped with cutlery for its guest. Other than that our stay was perfect to celebrate 5 year wedding anniversary. I would stay here again!

allReviews.title: Superb Room-wish I could stay longer
allReviews.text: Arrived at 11pm en route from Riverside to Salt Lake. Room was spectacular corner suite on 20th floor with views from two glass walls and two balconies, even through fireplace which had glass front and back. Suite had two bathrooms plus jacuzzi in bedroom, king sized bed, 42inch TV in living room and bedroom, plus smaller TV in bathroom. Huge shower with three shower heads. It also had full kitchen and wonderful furniture throughout. I would have liked to stay longer but had to leave at 10am.The room was exceptionally quiet.

allReviews.title: Staycation
allReviews.text: The 29th flr. has a great view.  Excellent Vallet.  Not so friendly and informative Front Desk. The room had a stale smell in it but roomy and the bed was comfy.  Excellent Lighting and enough elec. sockets.

allReviews.title: Facilities were first class, customer service nonexistent, spa was a ripoff!
allReviews.text: The living/sleeping accomodations were excellent, it is too bad that there was no customer service and the spa was a total absolute ripoff, I was charged double what I was qouted, did not get the service I requested and after contacting management 4 times - 0 response.Plus the advertised rates did not include hidden fees! So buyer beware!

allReviews.title: Poor Palms Place
allReviews.text: We were excited to stay here for our staycation to celebrate our anniversary as we do in several hotels here in Las Vegas.  Looking at the photos we expected a beautiful, clean and modern environment.  The front desk girl was great so nothing regarding the staff.....but upon entrance to the unit we were hit with the reality of huge disappointment.  We step onto severely scratched, creaky wooden floors that seem to almost break when you step on them.  The stainless steal was something we thought not possible...stained.  The carpet is heavily worn and dingy with stains resembling bodily fluids we would rather not speak of.  The view is something we were really looking forward to and our eyes quickly led to the eaten shrimp tails on the deck.  My boyfriend then comes out of the bathroom to tell me there is a false eyelash next to his foot by the toilet....really?!  On top of it all there is a $500 locals deposit.  Enter at your own risk.....not worth the money....hopefully I get my $500 deposit back.....

allReviews.title: Not What it Appears to be!
allReviews.text: From what we could tell Palms Place is part of Palms Casino which is closer to the strip. Palms Place is in no way a hotel as it consists of units which are privately owned in which they are then rented out to the visitor. They do have a front desk for check in and internet which we found difficult to get on even with their help. There are no restaurants in the hotel and if you order room service it comes in take out boxes with plastic utensils. The units themselves are quite nice with comfortable beds but don't count on someone to clean your room and make your bed as we had to beg them to do this and eventually it was done. If you want a nice room as a reasonable price this may be the place but it's not a hotel. Last it took us a half an hour to get a cab to the strip and should you want to gamble you have to go through a tunnel to Palms Casio next door.. Would we stay there again, the answer is no!

allReviews.title: Nice place but poor housekeeping
allReviews.text: The hotel has a gorgeous view but the housekeeping was non-existent.  For the four nights we stayed the room was only cleaned and linens changed once and then we had to ask.  The first night we stayed the room looked very nice but when we came back the next day after being out all day the room was the same as when we left.  We rescued some towels off the floor and then went to down to the lobby to enquire if we had to do our own.  They advised that they would look into it immediately and everything looked great that day.  We expected everything would be good after that but our room wasn't cleaned again the next day so we phoned down and asked for clean towels.  Staff were helpful but won't stay again. Definitely not a 5 star.

allReviews.title: We Will Return
allReviews.text: My wife and I stayed here for a few hours, and we really enjoyed for the small amount of time we were here. The room is completely functional with all the amenities needed. Our only issue was the dirty ice bucket. But the room had a Strip view, stove, microwave and a shower that you could see through (romantic) from your bed. Makes for a great night!

allReviews.title: Nice place to make you feel at home
allReviews.text: Beautiful rooms beautiful views, good food we felt safe And actually roamed the hotel to see what we could see everything was exceptional. nice staff with good attitudes easy access to the strip. Amazing rooms I consider this hotel low key spot clean rooms and bathrooms

allReviews.title: Daily Deposit
allReviews.text: We called ahead of time to check on whether of not the pool is open , we were told we could use the heated pool at the Palms Resort and Spa. So we booked through Expedia and we also requested not to get a handicap room . When we arrive we were then told of a $50 daily deposit so that was $300 right off the bat and then of course the resort fee of $28 a day . When we got to the room at 2am it was a handicap room so the next day we had to change rooms . When we went to the "heated pool" it was not heated ,so that was a bust . We will not be staying at the Palms again .Off the strip and no pool and a daily deposit on top of the resort fee .

allReviews.title: Worst hotel experience ever
allReviews.text: I have never had to write a negative review online, but for Palms Place, I believe I need to. (YES Even after 4-months!) The experience at Palms Place was AWFUL. To top it off I wrote a letter to them on their website and they never responded.  The letter said: "My boyfriend and I booked 3-nights, August 2015.We arrived excited but when we checked into our room, it was terrible. There was a piece of metal hanging in the walkway from the kitchen counter, stains all over the walls (looked like vomit), the bathroom wasn't clean etc. We snapped a few photos to show downstairs. "David from Columbia" was the rudest employee we've ever encountered! He insisted this was "normal wear and tear," and said we could wait to have our room cleaned. When we got upset about the inconvenience he told us, "You can leave if you want to, just let me know." We were so applaud we cancelled our entire stay, and had to book another hotel, last minute. This put a negative damper on our trip."In short, we left the hotel and had an excellent experience at Vdara, but we spent way more money than we intended to! DON'T BOOK AT PALMS PLACE, STAY AWAY!!!

allReviews.title: Disappointing! Another big LV hotel with no personal touch!
allReviews.text: I stayed here one night while passing through Las Vegas on business. I was disappointed. The Palms brand is one I heard of and thought this would be a nice treat to stay here. I would have preferred a chain hotel catering to business travelers any day over this hotel! This hotel is not 4.5 stars. The latest scam by Las Vegas hotels is the "Resort Fee". A mandatory $28 charge giving you stuff you won't use and don't have time for. The only thing that made me OK with the resort fee was free internet. But NO, not so fast. The free internet was so slow you can't hardly send an email. If you want average Internet it's another $10 per day. For $28 a day resort fee, they should provide lightning fast internet. Why would it be an option to pay more for faster speed capable of sending an email when the resort fee is to include "free" internet?!?! Just charge a flat room rate, include basic quality services you would expect of a 4 or 5 star hotel and leave it at that. To top it off, I simply asked for a wine bottle opener. They charged $2.50 plus a $1.00 service charge to deliver a cheap plastic bottle opener that probably cost $0.05 and was virtually impossible to use to open a wine bottle. Hardly 4-5 star service!!! Avoid all mega large Las Vegas hotels charging "Resort Fees"!!! Service is horrible and the hotels are scamming people with "Resort Fees"!!!

allReviews.title: Yuck!
allReviews.text: Challenging to get in.  Valet parking was full, so parking was quite a schlep.  Room was kind of interesting, but you could see someone in the shower from anywhere in the bedroom.  Most disturbing, when we moved the sliding table over a bit (as it is designed to do), it was absolutely filthy!!!  We talked to the front desk about this, and frankly, she just didn't care!!!!  What a disappointment.  I don't prefer to be faced with inch deep filth in a place where I stay.

allReviews.title: Amazing experience!
allReviews.text: I stayed at Palms Place a while ago and I'm only getting around to reviewing it now, but Palms Place is an amazing hotel! The rooms were gorgeous with great views of the strip and even the base room has a ton of space. The bathroom was amazing. It was all-marble with a Jacuzzi and a separate rain shower, and a TV over the sink/vanity area. The rest of the room had 2 big TVs, one in front of the bed and one in the living room area. There was also a full kitchen with a giant minibar, dishwasher, fridge...everything. The staff was also very nice. It's not on the strip but it's very close, and since it's just off the strip it has amazing views of the whole strip, which was beautiful to look at. The Palms Place was great!

allReviews.title: my stay at the palms
allReviews.text: i recently stayed at the palms while i was on holiday.its a fantastic hotel with stunning mountain views over las vegas.very comfortable rooms.nothing to fault.was incredible opening the curtains every morning to that amazing view.the staff were all very courteous and polite and respectful.id previously said i was unaware of the resort fee and security deposit you have to pay on arrival..id like to make it clear this was an error on my part and i unreservedly apologise to joseph and the staff at the palms.this information was indeed on the site id booked through and it was my fault for not reading the booking properly...half hour walk into the strip or you can get the shuttle i didnt mind the walk was super weather.wouldnt hesitate to return and stay at the palms when im in las vegas again.

allReviews.title: Modern condos off the strip
allReviews.text: This is a great location if you have a car. Parking was easy, and it was easy to drive to hotels on the strip and park there. All parking was free.These are more like condos with a small kitchen and big bathrooms. The room was modern, comfortable and clean. The bed was a dream to sleep in. Note, that although there are balconies, they are locked off unless you are an owner.Only suggestions I would make to the hotel is that 1) There is some wear and tear (Ex. tub needs recaulking) that should be taken care of.2) When you pay 28 per night for a resort fee, that should include the "fast wifi". Only the slow wifi is included. (It was, however, just fast enough to stream netflix or youtube)We have stayed a lot of places in Vegas, but really loved the comfort and style of these rooms. We will definitely stay here again!

allReviews.title: Disappointing
allReviews.text: When arriving in the room we found one tv not working, the shower door wouldn't open and the safe was locked. This was fixed on the spot but should have been fixed before we checked in.Service is poor, room cleaning and restocking of mini bar seems not be a daily routine, so beware if you stay longer than 1 night.Location is good, if you have a rental car it only takes minutes to get to the strip.

allReviews.title: Best time EVER!!!
allReviews.text: e Palms Place Spa amd Resort was a wonderful place to spend our honeymoon.   It's located just off the strip, it has so much to do you really don't ever have to leave the property.   We stayed in the 1 bedroom suite. ..AMAZING!! Could stay forever! The best views of the mountains and the Strip!!  Room is equipped with full kitchen/washer/dryer, fireplace,  1.5 baths and beautiful soaking jacuzzi in the bedroom overlooking the Strip. The only problem was that the pots, pans, plates etc were not in the room and had to be specially requested, several times before being delivered.   We had a little bit of difficulty with the front desk. ..only 1 person to check a long line of people in and kept us waiting all day for an upgrade to the 1 BR suite,  meanwhile they had us check out of the first room so by 6pm we were trying to get management to place us in a new room. We will definitely be back. ..we will be sure to request that the kitchen be equipped with dishes etc prior to our arrival.  Great buffet,  many restaurants,  great casino.  Housekeeping was awesome!!

allReviews.title: Wauw what an experience
allReviews.text: We booked a suite in this hotel for one night. Wauw this was great; The suite at least 200m2 with a livingroom, bedroom, kitchen, big bathroom and a spa in the livingroom ! The whole suite was full of windows so we had a great view over Las Vegas. On top of that the price was absolutely not expensive! In NYC we had a very tiny room for this price.Takes 10 minutes to go to the Strip by taxi, they are in front of the entry of the hotel. Very friendly staff,Take note that Palms has two buildings, the "chique" resort and the "regular" Palms Casino hotel; We slept in the regular.

allReviews.title: Excellent stay. 5 stars all the way.
allReviews.text: The place more than meets expectations. Over the top style, very comfortable. These are suites, not hotel rooms; streamline design. Bathroom is big, room is big, bathroom has a whirl pool bath with a ceiling shower and a glass door...TV in bathroom, two TVs in space; one if front of bed, and the other in front of couch and living area. Over the top amenities and easy access to the strip. Free parking. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay there. Pillow top bed, really comfortable. Beautiful view, we were on the 25th floor. Balcony, but no access, all balconies are locked. Classy and elegant. It's such a good deal just a 5 minute drive to Strip, easy access...couldn't recommend more.

allReviews.title: What an amazing stay!
allReviews.text: I was a little concerned given some of the reviews. This is a new building, built or rather opened within the past decade. The entrance is not busy, drop off is available or valet. We just parked and walked in, or I would drop my wife off at the door due to the wind during our trip. We were very happy with our room. We wanted the kitchen and really wanted the Jacuzzi. The kitchen is nice it has an extra fridge, which isn't stocked, so you have room for some of your own groceries or drinks. We asked for some glasses and other kitchen items. The room was clean having some minor damage to one of the televisions, which I only saw when the morning sun hit the screen. The bed I was concerned wasn't going to be comfortable when I first saw it, but we both slept great on it. The Jacuzzi tub is a great size for 2 people, plenty of room to be comfortable and able to move around a little. We had the strip side view and enjoyed the quiet smoke free environment. We loved the Brenden Imax theater, at The Palms Casino, which has a Monday 5 dollar movies all day. A great deal that you can use the sky walk to access from the 2nd floor. Didn't use the spa like we wanted to, but if we stay again we will try next time. It would be nice if the spa was a little more affordable for guests. They charge $25 per guest to use the Hammam at Drift Spa, this isn't included in the resort fee which is $28.00 per night with tax. Parking never was an issue. We were able to park on the ground floor of the garage or out in the open parking just a little way from the entrance to the hotel. I would recommend this to couples, the room is very accommodating. If you were with a friend, or family member it would not offer enough privacy to make the room comfortable to shower, use bathroom and dress in. If someone is wondering why only 4 stars... I've stayed at better places and don't want to overrate a place solely due to it being very good in all categories. If I could I would give The Palms Place a 4 1/2 star rating.

allReviews.title: Wonderful but not perfect
allReviews.text: My husband and I stayed here as a last minute vacation. We prefer not staying on the strip because we always rent a car and its more quiet and laid back than the strip. We chose the Palms Place because our last minute trip gave us limited choices for our price range. We originally had reservations at the Palms hotel in a standard room. After I booked it, I started reading all the negative reviews of the shabby looking standard rooms and how the superior rooms were renovated. I called the Palms and asked about upgrading. The rep I spoke to said for the same $20 a night it cost to upgrade to the superior room at the hotel, I could upgrade to a studio in the Palms Place condo next door. That was the best money I ever spent! We not only had a panoramic view of the strip, we had a mini kitchen, a humongous room with 2 flat screen TVs and a king sized bed, a 3rd TV in the marble bathroom, and a jetted bathtub. A million times better than a standard room with two queen beds! The only minor things were some of the furniture was worn and needed replacing. The WiFi wasn't strong and we had trouble connecting. I was also hoping for a washer/dryer but not in this room. Also, when we arrived, we asked the concierge for a good place to get a burger. He said McDonalds. Not funny, Jerk.  A concierge is supposed to be helpful and answer your questions, give you suggestions when you ask for places to eat, and offer to make reservations-not be a Smart Mouth. I would tell management to transfer him to housekeeping so he can be Mr Funnyman to a toilet brush. Otherwise our stay was terrific. My other highlight was my trip the Spa! I got a Massage/Facial Package for $99 and it was lovely. The ladies who worked on me gave me a terrific recommendation to get my hair cut at the Palms Salon by Tory. Best haircut I ever got!!  We're so coming back to Palms Place.

allReviews.title: Great weekend stay
allReviews.text: Stood here this week and this place was amazing. Beautiful studio suite but was offered a 1 bedroom suite for $50 more a night. Although I didn't upgrade that's a lot cheaper than their listed rates. Had an issue with the safe in the room but security showed up in 5 minutes to open the safe for me. Love this hotel.

allReviews.title: Ahhhhmmaaazzziiinnggg!
allReviews.text: This is probably my favorite hotel I have stayed in Las Vegas. I love the proximity to everything without all of the crazy strip traffic. Upon Check-In, Chris T. was extremely helpful and ensured that we would have a pleasant stay. Be sure to find out everything that is covered by your resort fees (i.e. gym, transportation to the strip, etc.)This is one hotel you will not leave smelling like smoke-there is no casino in the actual resort. However, if you want to gamble, you can just walk through the sky tube and you will be in the Palm casino.The rooms were fantastic. They have everything you would need- refrigerator, microwave, teapot, toaster, etc. The restrooms were beautiful with a huge jetted bathtub. This is a place that you can spend a week and never feel crowded or that something was lacking. I cannot wait to return, this is going to be the first place I check availability when I am traveling to Las Vegas.

allReviews.title: disappointing
allReviews.text: when we arrived, there was a long check in line, and with only one person at reception, it did not get better.  Finally we were able to check in after about 30 minutes.  The room itself was nice and we were happy with the accommodations themselves

allReviews.title: Changes are occurring. Some good, some...
allReviews.text: This has been one of my favorite hotels since it opened. Just make sure you are booking Palms "Place" or you may end up at The Palms which is OK if you are a 24/7 Party Animal. Nine Steak House is really good. Not among the Top 5 but definitely in the Top 10. They have ruined Simon's restaurant. It is basically "Johnny Rockets" with a luxurious surrounding. Can't say if I will go back or not. P.S. Certain staff Members are absolutely wonderful.

allReviews.title: Nice but not really a hotel
allReviews.text: This is a service apartment, so don't expect the level of service of a hotel. The rooms are modern and comfortable. Check-in took 45 mins as there was only 1 staff working. It was good valve for money

allReviews.title: Not to far away but far enough
allReviews.text: we loved the palms place. Rooms were clean and well kept. We absolutely loved the beds and the waterfall shower head. The full stove and kitchen was also a nice addition. Would definitely stay again. Enclosed walkway/access to palms for gambling is also very useful.

allReviews.title: 1 week visit
allReviews.text: spent a week for work.  600 sq foot suite. 2 large screens; nice kitchen set-up. quiet room.  great cocktail bar in lobby.  have to take 2 people movers to get to casino; no biggy.  large sports bar. very good staff.  close to strip

allReviews.title: Palms Place: Sanctuary Among Vegas Madness!
allReviews.text: Loved staying at Palms Place. The studio/condo I rented through AirBNB was perfect for my week long stay during a busy trade show. The staff and check-in process was seamless with a nice option to valet park or self park not too far away. Since I rented through AirBNB, I didn't pay a resort fee, so that was nice as well. The room was wonderful with a stainless kitchenette stocked with a toaster, blender, utensils and coffee machine. The bathroom was all marble with a delightful rain shower overhead. The only reason I didn't give the stay a full five stars was due to the fact that the second TV and other showerhead didn't work. Other than that, it was awesome! Oh, and if you want to hang out in the casino and eat a quick meal, it's a short walk through the Sky Tube to Palms Casino. Easy breezy!

allReviews.title: Pleasure trip
allReviews.text: Family vacation. Room, spacious, kitchen usage...3rd stay at this locatin...loving it every time....will stay here again.  Hotel should offer some special discount for us regulars. It s great that we re just minutes away from the strip.

allReviews.title: Great stay at Palms Place Hotel
allReviews.text: To be honest I was a bit worried due to some of the reviews on here but we booked it as it looked great.It is off the strip - which is why we chose it, but to be aware of this, if you want to be in the centre of the action. Also note, that Las Vegas isn't really designed for walking! We hired a car and there was loads of free parking right at the hotel, which was great.Had nothing to worry about - all the staff were really friendly, the hotel was spotless, room was massive, the bed was super comfortable, the bathroom was amazing, with a drench shower and normal shower and whirl pool bath, the water was always hot. It had the most extensively stocked mini bar I've ever seen in a hotel - you could do some damage with that collection! It was just a great stay. We also had a great view, despite not managing to get a room on a higher floor. It was also very quiet (despite being very busy!), which in sin city, is amazing. There is a shuttle bus that goes from the Palms hotel to Caesars Palace - I would say, this could go on a bit later than 8PM? Seems a bit early to finish. The breakfast is through in the Buffet Bistro bit near the casino, the selection was fabulous, and the food was really nice. I liked the fact there wasn't a casino directly in the hotel but should you wish, it's right next door. The only downside, was the hotel trying to charge me for breakfast - when it was included in what I'd booked with Booking.com. So check your bill on leaving the hotel!! I would definitely recommend staying here. We also stayed at the Trump hotel, and I'd stay at Palms Place again over the Trump hotel....

allReviews.title: Rather Disappointing 4.5 Star Hotel
allReviews.text: We booked this hotel through Priceline.com so we didn't know the hotel name, but it was listed as a 4.5 star property. This property is actually a residence tower associated with the Palms Hotel, but apparently they rent out some of the studios and one-bedroom apartments on a nightly basis to hotel guests. As such, and considering the 4.5 star rating, I expected a very nice property. Unfortunately, it missed the mark in a number of areas to be rated this high.  At most it is a 4, perhaps a 3.5.This hotel, like many these days, charges a resort fee on top of the nightly rate.  For this, you get the use of the pool, "free" valet parking, and "free" wi-fi. The vehicle approach to the hotel is rather odd, almost as a second thought through the parking lot of the Palms. The entry is also small and tight and unable to handle the arrival/departure of more than just a few guests at one time. This is probably due to the fact it was designed primarily as a residence, and not a hotel. Despite the wait, the valet parking and bell staff where excellent once we reached the front of the line.Check-in staff were swift and courteous. We were given a studio, which compared to a hotel room was very generous in size and included a small kitchen. I'm not a fan of the ultra-contemporary interior design, but that is a personal preference. However, the furniture and flooring have seen much wear and are in need of replacement: Scratched wood flooring; scratched and chipped laminate and wood veneer furnishing. Ignoring those issues, the view from our room on the 35th floor toward the Strip was fantastic, especially at night.We visited the pool, which is of a nice design. However, there are three cabanas near the entry to the pool area that seem to have been (for the lack of a better word) abandoned or turned into storage space for old pool furniture.  A very odd greeting to the pool area.  In addition, the cushions on the lounge chairs were simply filthy!  This was remedied by covering them with towels, but this is simply unacceptable for a hotel of the stated star rating. The pool waitress was attentive in serving us outrageously priced drinks. ($14 for a beer? Really?)We stopped by the cafe just off the pool for a late afternoon snack.  We were never greeted, leading us to believe it wasn't open, although we saw two tables at which people were eating.  We waited a sufficient period of time, but left and moved on to a restaurant outside the hotel.Check-out was painfully long, with only two staffers at the front desk. Not sufficient for the number of guests checking out.It is hard to complain considering what we paid via Priceline.com.  However, this hotel is over-rated at 4.5 stars and I wouldn't deliberately select to stay at this hotel again.

allReviews.title: Rooms great, lobby ?
allReviews.text: The room was five stars, the check in area and corridor to the casino we encounter a few shady characters. Because it is not a true hotel, but a individual own condominium there is a somewhat bare bones staff in the lobby area.

allReviews.title: Great experience
allReviews.text: Really enjoyed staying at palms place. One of the best places I have ever been to! The room is amazing, and we got great view as well. Fairly cheap, and the food at the bistro buffet was good. Couldn't believe the beer and wine was included with the food!

allReviews.title: Disappointed
allReviews.text: Upon arrival at 12:00am, we could not pull our car upfront because of a bunch of limousines and huge monster looking trucks. We parked in self park and had to carry our luggage to check in. Then at check in there was a long line with only 2 people working. I complained and was given an upgraded suite. Our reservation had been in the hotel but the so called upgrade was next door. We had to carry our luggage all the way over to Palms place. The room at first glance seemed nice, had a great view of the strip. First of all the balcany was locked so you cant use it. The pillows were feather instead of down and very uncomfortable.  The marble tile floor had years of filth built up in the grout and corners. The spa tub was nice if you dont mind looking at molding caulking around the rim. I have no idea how this hotel is rated a 4 star resort. The casino and hotel over all has lots of differed maintenance.

allReviews.title: Not impressed
allReviews.text: I've stayed at Best Westerns nicer than the Palms Place. When I checked into my room, the overall cleanliness of the space was dismal. The remote for the tv was covered in something sticky... There were false eyelashes on the night stand... The glass on the balcony which you can't even used was completely smudged. For a "4.5 star" hotel this one did not make the cut. While the public areas of the Palms were lovely, the room itself is not one I will pay to stay in again.

allReviews.title: Oh palms... What happened to you?! :(
allReviews.text: Having lived in Southern California, I am a frequent visitor at Vegas.  Over the past 2 years, the Palms Place had become our favourite.  They have updated and pristine rooms, and the drive to the strip is very short as well.  They late night view of the city from their 37th floor elevator window is both comforting (beats the windy streets) and mesmerizing.  This time like many others, we traveled over the Halloween weekend.  We booked 2 neighboring rooms on the 39th floor with a king bed and a pull-out sofa bed (dreaded sleeping on this! :-/ ).  Following are the issues we found with 1 of our rooms on entering:1. Bathroom door did not lock (someone came in to fix it, but was back to square one the next day)2. The ice maker in the refrigerator did not work (No ice machine on the floor, however housekeeping sent us a bucket on request)3. There was a pair of used socks!!! (ewww!!) in the shelf below the tv!!!On mentioning these issues to the manager/front desk we were not given another room (Halloween weekend, all rooms were apparently full within 5min of us checking in (when checking in we were given the option of other rooms)!!)  While they did send in someone to fix the lock, given multiple issues in the room I think (sadly) the hotel's standards are degrading.... It's not old enough to have so many issues and if they continue with this kind of housekeeping, the day is becomes comparable to all the substandard hotels on the the strip wont be far.Please make things right, you aren't far off yet!P.S: The wifi doesn't reach the rooms either :(

allReviews.title: Do not waste your money on an upgrade
allReviews.text: I would recomend that you stay at one of the strip hotels.  We stayed at the Palms Place one bedroom suite and even though we paid for an upgrade to a higher floor we were not allowed to use the balcony, when asked they said it was not part of the deal and balcony use is owners only.  After complaining to the manager Nathan he said he would allow it but they did not do it and when the did come up after several calls we were told that due to keys broken in the lock they cannot accommodate the request, he gave us $50 food credit really? Stay at the strip hotels!

allReviews.title: Expected much more
allReviews.text: To far of the main strip, to much transportation expenses.Hotel clean! But very stale, deserted, depressing.No coffee shop attached. Need to walk to casino to get all you need. But even the casino was empty. Hooters food horrible.

allReviews.title: An honest review- Nice room, horrible check-in, bad service
allReviews.text: This is probably the only bad experience I've had with a resort in my 10 or so trips to Vegas.I called ahead and notified I would be arriving past midnight. They said it was fine. Arrived around 1:15am to the lobby, there was only 1 person at the desk and 2 guest ahead of me. Took exactly 51  minutes to check in. The man at the front desk helped a girl that had barely arrived to check in ahead of me when he saw I was there first and I had been waiting for nearly 30 minutes. He then tried to give me another room at the Palms casino because they were out of rooms and the one reserved for me had a "crack" on a window. He told me I wouldn't have to pay the difference for the other room at the Palms Casino. While he showed me pictures of the other room on a Ipad, I looked at the reservation prices on my phone at hotel.com.The room he was offering was a lot smaller and about $20 less than the one I had booked. Hmmmm yea I wouldn't have to pay a difference because the room was less.  I told him no and I'd take my room as is.When I finally got to my room (around 2:25am), I inspected all the windows and glass panes with a flashlight. I found no crack. I like to give credit where credit is due so I will say that the room itself was really nice, bed was comfortable , restroom was nice.Wifi is limited to only 1 device per day.Room had 2 TV's on of the remotes batteries was dead and the balcony door was locked. My girlfriend took a $3 Snicker's from the mini bar. She told me it was hard as a rock when she bit it. I thought maybe it was cold from the refrigerator but when we checked the expatriation date, it had expired almost 2 years ago!I called room service and explained them the situation. The lady who answered was very apologetic and removed the charge from my bill.I tried to fill the tub only to find out the Hot tap wasn't working, I had to fill the tub with the shower head which took over an hour.At night there was 1 closet light that wouldn't turn off when the door was shut. The light would illuminate the room through the middle crack. The second night I folded a piece of paper and placed it between the door and the switch and that did the trick. Overall the room was nice and modern, very roomy, but I've never stayed at a place where I could count the number of things wrong with a room with my fingers. I'm usually not one to ask for special services and I didn't even complain for the things wrong with the room (minus the candy bar). But the service at the check in left a lot to be desired. Perhaps if I had checked in during "regular" hours the service might of been different. But the way the man at the front desk tried to "solve" my scenario was not the best. Would I recommend it to a friend. Probably not. Would I stay here again. No.

allReviews.title: Great rate off the strip
allReviews.text: I had a one night stay in Vegas so I wasn't going to have time to enjoy the strip so I decided to stay at the Palms Hotel and Spa because it was significantly cheaper. I got a full kitchen, fridge and a large premium bathroom for pennies on the dollar. Overall a nice stay and the extra savings was a bonus.

allReviews.title: Hidden Gem in Las Vegas
allReviews.text: Having stayed there close to 200 nights, it's still the hidden gem!  From Tony at the Bell Desk, to Casandra @ the front desk, Henry in Valet, they are always incredible with greetings and asking if I need any help!  The rooms are Excellent for the value.

allReviews.title: Palms
allReviews.text: Overall the hotel and casino was pretty good. The room was clean and quite large, with a good view over the strip. The bathroom was luxurious for the amount we spent. The strip was a distance away, but there was a shuttle that takes you straight to Caesars Palace which was great. My main gripe is the 'resort fee' that was not disclosed at time of booking and came as a shock at the end of the stay. At $28p/n for use of the pool/gym and WIFI, I thought this was excessive and came as a shock. Another thing was that the door to the room balcony was locked, so we couldn't fully enjoy the view.

allReviews.title: Large and Comfortable
allReviews.text: We stayed at Palms Place for a few days whilst in LV. Palms Place offers you humongous clean and comfortable serviced apartment rooms. The views from the room is magnificent. Coming back to the room at nights and seeing the lights on the strip is excellent way to finish the day. It is located off the strip. Having a rental car helps solve the location issue. There is no parking fee for self parking. Price is reasonable for such a large room off the strip.

allReviews.title: Big rooms, beat up facility
allReviews.text: Palms Place is really a condo building offered as a hotel. So if you like big rooms, this is a good place.  Buying a package on Expedia, we stayed 5 nights (Sunday thru Thursday) in a 1 bedroom condo with great views of the strip for $158/night plus $28 resort fee.  And a big one-bedroom, with 2 bathrooms.  That is something you'll find hard to match.The location is actually pretty good.  The attached Palms Casino was overhauled in the last year, and is pretty nice for gambling.  You can easily walk to Gold Coast Casino for breakfast or lunch, or next door there is the Rio with nice gambling, food and the Penn & Teller Show.  Walk the opposite direction and it's a short stroll to the Orleans for other gambling and food.  Or, if the weather is nice it's a pleasant 2 mile walk to the strip and all it offers.  There also is a shuttle available to the strip from the Palms at no charge.  Like everywhere in Las Vegas, parking is free.  There is self park or valet, your option.But, this place is beat up.  We've stayed here 3 times in the last couple of years, primarily for the big room at a good price.  But wear and tear is obvious.  Don't expect an Aria room at this price.  Also, service is spotty.  We arrived at 5:00pm and the room was not available.  Surprising.  Most housekeeping seems to happen between noon and 5:00.  There are no ice makers, since you are expected to have ice from fridge in your room - but whether the ice maker works is spotty.This place is spotty, but it is a good value.

allReviews.title: A Great Room, But There Are Issues
allReviews.text: We stayed here because of the price - I got a deal on hotwire, and it was a Friday night, and my usual hotel of choice was fully booked.  For what we paid, (about $100 plus the dreaded $28 resort fee), it was a bargain.  For some reason though, the way they are running the place succeeds in minimizing the assets they have.Check-in was slow.  Although there were only a handful of people in front of us in line, and three people were working the desk, it took a long time (20 minutes) before we were attended to.  Once we reached the counter, though, the staff was polite and friendly, and gave us a room key quickly, on the 34th floor.  When we went to the room, we were immediately impressed.  It was huge, with a king-size bed and a pull-out sofa, a full kitchen, a jacuzzi bath, enormous windows that looked out on a balcony, and a great view of the strip.Then we started to notice things.  Many of the lights didn't work.  There were no sheets for the pull-out sofa, either on the bed or in the closet.  The door to the balcony was locked.  There were no plates or silverware for the kitchen.    We called for plates and silverware, and they were quickly brought up.  We called for sheets for the sofa bed, and we were told, pretty abruptly, to look in the closet.  When I said the closet did not have any sheets, they said they would bring them up.  40 minutes later, still no sheets.  I called again.  They said they would bring them up.  Then housekeeping called back and told me, in an exasperated manner, to look in the closet.  I assured them I was looking in the closet, and there were no sheets.  They said they would deliver them. I don't know when they did, because I went out, but when I returned the sheets were there.  Even then, though, the sofa bed was not made with the sheets, but they were tossed carelessly on the main bed.I called about the balcony, and was told it could not be opened for security reasons.  I have no idea what that means.  Whose security?The internet is limited to one device, works at a relatively slow speed, and is capped, unless you want to pay extra.To top things off, when I went to check out, there was a minibar charge on the bill although nothing inside the minibar had been touched.  When I called, they removed it, but told me that if housekeeping found anything missing, it would be added back on.There is so much right about this place - the facilities are terrific, parking was easy very closer to the entrance, you don't have to walk for miles to get to your room, the location is great both for the Strip and for the amazing Chinatown area.  It is a shame that there are so many challenges for the staff to overcome in running the place.

allReviews.title: Nice hotel, off the stip, very quiet
allReviews.text: This hotel is off the strip and not as close as I'd like it to be, but I guess that costs extra. It's one of the three hotels on the Palms property. We didn't really explore it much since it just seemed to have a lobby with one bar (it was very nice though). It has a modern feel to it and the room was very nice; it had a lot of storage space and extremely spacious. I just wish the bathroom had better lighting.

allReviews.title: A week at Palms Place
allReviews.text: The room was LARGE....actually 2 room, 1 1/2 bath suite.Living room and bedroom completely separate with sliding doors.  View was great with walls of windows. Very modern room, mirrors, shower big enounh for 4 people, Jetted soaking tub.Gas fireplace.   However, it is away from strip, but a shuttle takes you to Ceasers-but only until 8PM(cab back $10) The casino is nothing special-will want to go to strip, but coming back to nice big room relaxing  It is like a codo apartment rather than hotel room.

allReviews.title: Nice hotel.  Great room.
allReviews.text: Big room for the price.  Had a room on the 52nd floor with a great view.   Would have been nice if the door to the balcony opened but understand this could be a liability so no big deal.   The room had 2 TV's but the one in front of the sofa had a poor picture so just used the one in front of the bed.  Bathroom was nice but lighting was a little dark.   Would be better if the wall between the bathroom and the rest of the room was darker.  If someone turned the bathroom light on in the middle of the night or early morning, it lit up the whole room.   I found the room to be very quiet.  An advantage to not staying on the strip.  They did offer a free shuttle to the strip which runs every 1/2 hour from 11-8.  Would be nice if it ran later.  They were putting in new carpeting and wallpaper on our floor but by the 2nd day it was finished and never did hear the workers.   Staff was polite and helpful.   We didn't use the either pool but checked out both of them.  I did see dirty cushions on the chairs and the cabanas were small and didn't look clean.  Wouldn't pay extra to use one.  The food was great.  Would definitely stay here again and would recommend staying here.

allReviews.title: Great Value for Price
allReviews.text: We returned to the Palms Place because of the quality experience we enjoyed on our previous visit. I had requested a high, west facing floor both times, and was given rooms on the 52nd and 53rd floors. We enjoy the spaciousness of the studio units (600 square feet) and the fabulous bathroom with its rain shower head and individual sprayer, and the deep and roomy soaking jacuzzi tub. We have enjoyed the multiplex movie theater, food court, and Nove (the Italian restaurant) in the adjacent Palms towers. The price for our midweek stay was one of the best in the entire city.

allReviews.title: Do Not Stay Here. It's Awful. !!!
allReviews.text: I come to Vegas few times a year and I will NEVER stay here again. The people that work here have zero customer service skills. Internet and TV ISSUES: As we got to the room the sound on the TV was not working, neither was the free internet. I had to sit on the phone for 45 minutes with the internet provider to get the internet to work. When it finally did it was very slow. The next day I paid for the higher speed internet and it was still very slow. The TV sound got fixed by a technician but the channel line up is pretty lame.On the second night we decided to order a movie. The screen was blocked and said it was not available for my room.  When I called guest services they wanted me to get dressed, go downstairs and give them a credit card. This is after they charged me resort fees and took a rather large security deposit. In addition to that the cell signals have been knocked out so my LTE only had one bar. Balcony ISSUE: Balconies do not open, you are stuck in a room without ventilation. When I called and asked they gave me 6 different excuses why.DIRTY POOL CHAIRS: The chairs by the pool are disgusting. Full of gross stains and cigarette burns. Black Out Curtains ISSUE: Badly designed curtains that let a lot of sunlight in, especially on the bottom. Expect to be woken up with sunrise.

allReviews.title: Nice stay, but a few issues
allReviews.text: Stayed here for two nights mid-week, mid-October in a studio suite. I was very impressed by the size of the suite. The sofa was way bigger than expected and fairly comfortable. The bathroom was a really nice size, too, bright and spacious. The whirlpool tub, which my friend said was heavenly, was a bit odd because you had to walk though the shower. The kitchen had a nice fridge, a minibar, a dishwasher, and an automatic ice maker - which was a lifesaver. But don't expect any soap or glasses or dishes unless you call down - and you probably won't get enough.Like other reviewers, I noticed that the place is kinda getting rough around the edges. Dirty cushion here, peeling wallpaper there, gross corners, etc. A good deep cleaning would make the place sparkle. Yes, the entire building is a bit dark by design; I didn't mind it much. My biggest problem was with checkin. I specifically reserved a studio suite in the Palms Place building. But without saying a word, they assigned me a room in the regular Palms towers. I actually had to pull out the Rocketmiles reservation email to show her and then I was given the correct room. It's aggravating because I've read others that had the same issue, and I dislike the bait and switch tactics. Would I stay here again? Yes, but I know what to expect.

allReviews.title: Key card did not work... Not a 4 star hotel.
allReviews.text: I booked this hotel through hotels.com because it was rated 4.2 stars and the price was  decent.  We booked two rooms for four adults for two nights.  We couldn't get the key card to work for one of the rooms.  We were on the 27th floor and we had to go back to the reception area 4 times before they finally decided that they had to call a technician.  I asked to have our rooms changed and the receptionist offered a room on the 30th floor.  I was traveling with family so I wanted us to be on the same floor.  She tells me that there are no vacant rooms available at all, which was hard to believe.  She gave us two tickets for complimentary drinks and that was it.  No free upgrade, no waiving of the resort fee, which was $28 PER room PER night for the amenities we never had the time to use.  The hotel was not completely outdated but it wasn't managed well.  I could see it wasn't cleaned properly, bathroom wasn't very clean either.  The worst part of the room were the old mattresses on all four of our beds which gave us back pain the morning after.  We booked this hotel because we had a rental car, but if you don't plan on renting a car, this hotel is completely off the strip and it's not walking distance unless you plan on walking for 30 + minutes under the scorching sun.

allReviews.title: Would not stay here again. Not a 4 star hotel.
allReviews.text: Spent a couple of nights at this hotel but it  was truly disappointing.1. The lobby area is dark and very unwelcoming. 2. Our initial room reeked of cigarettes which I'm very sensitive to. After repeatedly reporting this to front desk, we were reluctantly given a different room. 3. Front desk staff are very unpleasant and lack people skills. 4. Rooms have a stale funky smell, like a drain or sewage smell .5 . There is no ventilation as balcony doors are locked. 6. Even though the room itself is modern it feels cold and non 'hotel -like'.Rooms lack attention to detail and seem to be neglected.  7. Wifi is limited to one device per room with a limit. 8. There are no kitchen utensils, if you'd like to use some you have to request it. 9. In all honesty the bell man,engineer and housekeeping lady were the only pleasant staff around.

allReviews.title: Pleasantly surprised!
allReviews.text: We were extremely happy with our room and stay at the Palms Place Hotel.  No question we would stay there whenever we are in Las Vegas again.  The bathroom was especially beautiful and unique.  We were there with friends and I know they loved the accommodations too.

allReviews.title: Nice stay at Las Vegas !
allReviews.text: We stayed 2 nights at Palms Place Hotel & Spa.Front desk staff were very efficient & kind,  and we had a lovely studio facing the Strip on the 51st floor !  ( what an incredible view !) Our Studio was extremely comfortable, spacious, and clean ! The incredible view was definitely a plus ! We enjoyed the pool at the Palms Casino, as we had access to both swimming pool: Palms Place & Palms Casino.Breakfast was ok (buffet style breakfast), but it's not very convenient to go all the way to the Palms Casino to enjoy it. Other than breakfast, the hotel is nice and clean & location is fine We were able to explore Las Vegas & Downtown very easily.

allReviews.title: Could be great, but....
allReviews.text: Palms Place has wonderful rooms with great views of the strip or the mountains. The rooms are spacious with stainless steel kitchenette and wet bar. The bedding was great and clean with duvet. Rooms needed urgent maintenance. Floors were clean but because of cheap material choices looked scuffed up and dirty. Internet experience was awful slow and capped. It also seemed like they blocked cell signals to sell their internet cap update. After all it could be great, but....

allReviews.title: Stay
allReviews.text: Awesome place. We had the view. Of the city      Great place to stay..they just have to upgrade the cleanlinrss of theirvroom. The desk receptionist are accommodating. Their night club is free when you stay. A lot of restaurants to choose from.

allReviews.title: 2 Fatal Flaws...
allReviews.text: Palms Place COULD near perfect if they could just fix two critical flaws.First, the good. I got a stellar deal of only $77 per night for two October weeknights. The location is close enough to the strip for a quick taxi over, but too far to walk (remember, Las Vegas blocks are looooong).Also good, not being attached to a smokey casino. The rooms were spacious with a kitchenette that would be perfect for families. Facilities were relatively new and modern. The studio had 2 TVs, with thoughtful plugs on the lamps by the bedside. The restaurant on the 6th floor gives a nice view of the small pool area. The salmon with veggies dish I ordered was better than expected. Now for the bad.1. Not only does Palms Place charge $28 per day resort fee, it doesn't include unlimited Wi-Fi Internet access. The Internet included is some sort of slow, capped package. You can upgrade to 2MB per day for something like $14 per day. What?! Either that was a typo or I misunderstood it. Any file these days is larger than 2MB. And to make things worse, that was PER DEVICE. Yes, you paid $28 resort fee for 1998 Internet, then another $7 to $14 for "upgraded" Internet that was just a tad faster, capped with a low ridiculous limit, and for only one device.This alone would make me consider boycotting Palms Place out of principle. If enough people complain, hopefully management will wake up and change this stupid policy.2. As described in other reviews, there's a sort of funky odor in the bathroom emanating from the drains. Anyone familiar with Vegas knows what I mean. It's that sewage stench in the streets and in certain restrooms. It's faint but obvious. For someone used to Asian countries like Taiwan, it's not a big deal. For others, I can see how it would be. I simply kept the bathroom door closed so it didn't leak out. But considering the nice facilities, the funky smell was offputting and out of place.So there you have it. Expensive, crappy Internet and a funky smell. Two fatal flaws in my opinion. If they fixed these two issues, this would be a no-brainer 4 star.Hello management?

allReviews.title: Not what we paid for! Staff has zero customer service skills or empathy.
allReviews.text: So we originally was booked with The Palms and this was the last 3 days of my honeymoon. While at the Palms I saw the pools hanging out of the hotel and told my wife we needed to splurge on the last night and get a pool suite. I called the operator (Billy) who told me those suites were $35,000! Okay not splurging that much but he did have a pool suite at Palms Place. He said as soon as you are ready we could check in to Palms Place. We packed went over checked in at the front desk, got our keys and headed up to the Penthouse suites. When we got near our room there was a ladder next to our door with part of the ceiling ripped off. We went in to our suite and was over whelmed by a sewer smell, it gets better! We went to look at the pool and the glass wall surrounding the pool was covered in blood. (no joke looked like CSI scene) At about the time when I was telling my wife their is no way I am staying here, 3 housekeepers came in and asked us what we where doing in the suite. I told the ladies they checked us in. She said the room wasn't ready and they shouldnt have checked us in. So back down to the front desk, gave us new keys and up to the 58th floor where are keys wouldnt work! back down to the desk and new keys. We got into the room and it looked great but the pool (jacuzzi) was cold. Called down and had engineering up to fix it because this is the reason we booked the room in the first place. So to make this short we had engineering up to that suite on 3 more occasions trying to fix our TV. Our engineer was a really nice guy and I wish I could remember his name but he was the only employee of this establishment that cared or even apologized for what we dealt with on our last day here. So to make matters worse by the time we where finally ready to get into the pool. (jacuzzi) it was so hot we couldnt get in. I had enough of people coming into our suite on our last night so we called it a night. When I checked out in the morning, I explained the situation to the guy at the front desk and I kid you not it was oh well you owe $$$. Not even sorry for your inconvenience. This would have been amazing if they could have sold us what we paid for. On a positive note, the views from the 58th floor are breathtaking and I was with my wife who always seems to make bad situations great. The Palms Place needs a lot of customer service training because I have had better at a Motel 6.

allReviews.title: Off the strip - rooms need some attention
allReviews.text: Our first visit to Vegas we did not realize that choosing a hotel on the other side of the highway would make visiting complicated. The hotel offers a free shuttle service that ends at 8pm. Rooms are large and modern but show signs of wear. I did enjoy the large windows and mountain view. The casino is a bit depressing compared to the ones on the strip.

allReviews.title: Out of the way
allReviews.text: Rooms are supposed to be modern, but instead feel cold.  Loose wiring on shelves and lights hung uneven.  Hallways smell bad.  It is really a condo that has been converted to a hotel.  Long walk to Palms next door

allReviews.title: Construction!! Yikes!! No warning!!
allReviews.text: Woke up to construction in the hallway, construction workers ripping up the wall paper and carpet.  Fumes, dust everywhere! Otherwise the room was awesome.  Great layout, clean, beautiful. Need better service at the front desk.

allReviews.title: Luxurious and Roomy
allReviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised to find the suite was quite large. Free wifi is available. The bathroom was also very nice and large, designed with floor to ceiling marble and a jetted tub. The customer service however was not as polished as the hotel itself. Several calls to concierge and valet went unanswered.

allReviews.title: Very nice hotel with many small problems
allReviews.text: The hotel in overall is great. If this was a 2/3* Days Inn, I would be happy to give it 100% rating. But from a hotel like this one, you are awaiting to be perfect and it was not.What was our biggest disappointment was that the pool was closed for a private party. As the pool was one of the main reasons to choose this hotel, it was a great disappointment. I think that it would be fair if the hotel gave a notice in advance so that you can rebook or gave some kind of compensation (e.g. discount from the resort fee, drink voucher or something). However, that didn't happen even when I complained at the reception.Second, the WiFi is poor. They call it high-speed internet, but once you log in, you see that you are limited by 1mbps. I think that was high-speed like 10 years ago. Also, there is only 1 device per room! In present, when everybody has a smartphone and the room is usually occupied by more than 1 person, it's definitely not enough.Thirdly, the service. As there is a kitchen in the apartment, we wanted to cook dinner (finally, after 2 weeks of staying in hotels and eating fastfood/restaurant food). There are no kitchenware in the place and you have to call for it. It took my 3 calls to finally get the kitchenware after more than an hour from my first call.And many other small gabs.On the bright side, the room was very nice and spacious, the hotel looked luxurious and there is a pretty good casino downstairs. It was about 5-10mins of taxi ride to the Strip and the hotel also provide a shuttle each 30mins (not working in the evening).

allReviews.title: Good Stay @ The Palms!
allReviews.text: Great deal on Travelzoo, was hoping they would've honored the second breakfast buffet deal for us with a lunch as we were leaving early, but the front desk said 'no' and wouldn't allow me to speak to management. Also check in took forever~they might need more than 2 clerks when there's a line-up 12 people deep!! Room was great and the pool was refreshing. We like the location away from the crazy strip. Would stay again.

allReviews.title: Rude People
allReviews.text: Hello, we stayed here from October 5-9, 2015. Hotel staff are rude and give bad service. We called front desk because the jacuzzi wasn't working, never got fixed. At the end we were overcharged for things we didn't even used and to top it off my husband got one candy bar and one coke from the mini fridge and were expecting to be charged for two candy bars and two drinks. I guess since we were two persons they just decided to charge us double. Very unsatisfied with everything. Will never stay here again. Thank you

allReviews.title: One of my new favourites!
allReviews.text: Super impresssed!!  We got a great deal on this hotel so wasn't too sure what to expect.  And some of the reivews weren't good, I really don't know why?!  The rooms were massive with fridge, sink, dishwasher, microwave, sitting area etc.  Bathrooms included a glass shower as well as a soaker tub and lots of mirrors. We had a great mountain-view room as well. Everything was clean and the staff were awesome.We had never stayed off the Strip before but the free shuttle is super handy and even taking a cab wasn't as expensive as we thought it would be.  Its also a non-gaming hotel so felt like a retreat coming home to. If we were in the mood for gambling or wanted different restuarants, the walk over to The Palms is really quick.Definitely recommend :)

allReviews.title: A less expensive alternative but don't expect much
allReviews.text: Located about a 30 minute walk from the strip,  the hotel is relatively inexpensive compared to the ones that are on the main drag.  The hotel staff is quite inexperienced and not very helpful.  Example would be upon checking I was given a room on the 38 th floor.  When the elevators opened up I was treated to a floor that had no wall paper,  carpet broken sheet rock and lighting provided by portable lights.  Returned to the front desk and after showing them a picture I took of the area,  they realized the floor was being renovated.  They had never seen what the area looked like.   Asked the concierge for directions and advise for dinner.  Had no clue.  So basically you are on your own.  Sometimes not a bad thing but be prepared.The room is a bit dated but you have a couch, bed, kitchen area and bathroom.  Hot water takes a while so start the shower and relax til the water gets to temp.  Had a view of the strip from the balcony but as many have said before the balcony is locked so you have no access.The gym closes at 7pm and when I asked if they had a sauna,  they do however it is a 25 dollar surcharge per use.   I asked if the resort fee of 25 dollars per day covers this and they said the resort fee covers the ability to get a newspaper in the morning at the front desk,  the ability to print a boarding pass and wifi.   Wifi,  well access is available in the room,  but at close to dial up speeds.  They do offer two other plans but at a substantial surcharge.  And remember it's only one asset per room.The Palm casino is close,  about a 5 minute walk and you have a moderate casino and some dining choices.  Tried Hooters for a quick bite and it's the first one I went to where the staff really made you feel like they didn't want to be there.  Maybe they didn't realize you don't go there for their great food choices.All in all,  it was an uneventful stay once I got to a room on a different floor,  but don't expect the services and flair that you find at some of the better known places along the strip.  You basically get what you pay for.

allReviews.title: Brilliant hotel off the strip
allReviews.text: After reading mixed reviews about this hotel was a little apprehensive to say the least.However our stay and room were brilloantCheck in was smooth and easy. Our room on the 9th floor had a brilliant strip view (shame about the locked balcony but safety first i presume).The room is self is huge and mosern. Very comfy king sized bed, seating area, two huge flat screens and the kitchenette area was a bonus- fridge especially.  The bathroom is fantastic!! Huge marble jacuzzi bath and rainforest shower Superb. AC was spot on too.Pool was calm and quiet if a bit small (palms itself has a bigger, more party orientated pool).All in all a brilliant hotel off the strip (half hourly shuttle to the strip provided til 8pm) and only about $7-8 for a uber into the centre of the action!! Ace!!

allReviews.title: Really disappointed.
allReviews.text: The hotel looks great on the Internet, however in reality it is dirty and in need of updating. We arrived after a long day, on entering our room it was clear it had not been cleaned, and there were random pills on the floor. We have a baby and a toddler so we were very concerned, and we didn't want to spend our holiday worrying what the kids might or might not find on the floor. We spoke to the management who were not bothered about this. Fortunately our Bellboy witnessed how bad the room was and got up moved to another room, which was very adequate, but no more.

allReviews.title: Superficial Style Lacking Attention To Detail
allReviews.text: I was hopeful this was going to be a great stay after looking at all of the reviews.  I did not  rely only on TripAdvisor as I booked this stay on 10/5/2015 via Expedia.com.  The staff were more than friendly and I thought this would be just as nice as my last three stays in The Cosmopolitan.  I checked in and walked through the "sky tube" to the tower and up to 29308.  There was an odor in the room I couldn't identify but it wasn't enough to ruin the stay.  It is a very nice room. Large and it has a view of the strip and the valley.  The balcony is inaccessible to those lodging but it was raining so nothing to miss there.  I actually booked the room because I was attending a party in the Paradise Tower (25201) and didn't want to worry about traversing Vegas once the party shut down.  When I got back to my room and it was time to wash and sleep I began to focus on the details.  There appeared to be significant water damage to the unit above (30208?) and the damage spread to this unit.  The odor could have been mildew.  The tub was a bit dirty and so was the shower.  I opted to forgo the tub.  The bedding was ripped in sections and the carpet was soiled.  Still, it was quiet, and well appointed for the lack of care in maintenance.  This property is on the bubble.  I hope they keep things going nicely as it has plenty of potential and I can see where it was once a great gem.  Do not pay >300\night for this room.  You will be disappointed you didn't grab a room on the strip.

allReviews.title: Nice contemporary hotel.
allReviews.text: Great place to stay if you like an European contemporary style. It is spacious, has all the amenities and doesn't have a casino in the lobby. Free self parking, wifi and a nice gym. Unfortunately the balcony has been locked at all times. The marble tiled floor in a shower stall is slippery. The kitchen cabinets, by design are lacking the door knobs. The $25 a day resort fee was unexpected surprise. I would still come back to this hotel and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to my friends.

allReviews.title: Vacation
allReviews.text: Really nice place to go. Hallway had a little smell, really good place to stay. Really clean place, friendly people. I definitely recommend this place, wifi had a 12 hour limit for free. Not too far from the strip and not too busy in the surrounding area like the strip, best of both world.

allReviews.title: Hidden Gem
allReviews.text: This hotel/ condo was ideal! The room was huge, the pool was great, entire spot was very modern. There is a shuttle to the strip as well as reasonable price for taxis. Its nice to see the view of the strip from the room! Amazing view!

allReviews.title: Great stay, huge room!
allReviews.text: The (off-strip) Palms Place Hotel is a condo style setup- don't expect 5 star hotel service.The studio suite room was large and well appointed with a big bathroom and plenty of room for the family, one king bed plus sofa bed, and useful kitchenette.  Great view of the (nearby) strip. The pool area at the Palms Place is lovely and relaxing, but if you want action head to the adjoining Palms Casino hotel pool for a more vibrant scene. The hammam is a great space, very relaxing.Join Club Palms even if you are not much of a gambler- great buffet food offers for members. Great stay!

allReviews.title: Feelings just like home!
allReviews.text: I stayed here three nights, for the Electric Daisy Carnival.The room was beautiful and it included and full kitchen. The staff was very friendly. Just know that they don't have bell boys, so enjoy carrying all of your bags.

allReviews.title: It started off on the wrong noteand ended on a worse one.
allReviews.text: Where to start. I wish I could show video that would really drive this review home. So we got married on 9-12-15 in Boston, ma. We decided to do something different and go to Las Vegas for our honeymoon. Thinking that we would have so much fun and enjoy our time. When we arrived it was around 1 am. The person at the desk handed us a note saying that we were being placed on a floor with construction. I questioned if there was any other location that they could put us in because I was worried about the way the floor would smell and noise. He told me he would put us in a strip view because of the fact that there was construction. I questioned him again because i had called earlier in the week to confirm everything and we were never told about construction happening. To be honest we would have gone to their other property instead. I have asthma and dust is a huge trigger. We get to the 9th floor and there are no signs as to where to go, no carpet, the floor smelled like glue and it was so overly dusty that honestly no one should have been on the floor. We get into our room finally and the floor was dirty. Because our suitcase is a rolling one we brought even more dirt in with us.  I told my husband that I would call in the morning but I was so sleepy from the long travel. We get up in the morning and I call the phone number on the sheet. I ask for a manager. A lady said the manger was busy but she could help. I explained to her that we work up to the noise of construction workers spakling the walls and talking very loud and it was only 8am. She told us that she had another room she could be moved into but it would take 1 -2 hours. I said no problem and said thank you. Well we waited. Three hours later I called because and the lady said oh yea it will be ready in an hour to 2 hours. We decided to go out to the pool since we made a reservations months before for the cabana. We get there and the bar tender (which was so nice and sweet) told us that the first three were the best ones. We took the second one from the bar and there was stains on every pillow in there. The walls were dirty and it just didn't look clean. I went and got towels (again they were really nice) and I placed them down so we could sit down. We got drinks  and something to eat but I couldn't finish my food in there. We left and closed out our account because it was so bad and had no plans on coming back. We ended up giving the bartender a 60 dollar tip because of the minimum amount that you had to spend. By that time I was sure that they room was ready. We went back up and I called and they lady told us again it would 1-2 hours. (if you are keeping count this is the 3rd time) So we decided to take a nap.
