When we work up to the noise of something being mixed and out room smelling like Paint. I went and opened the door and I couldn't get out because the door had been covered in full plastic. I called down again to the manager that told us this time she had a room she could move us into and someone would be right up to hep move us. Well, No one ever came. 30 mins later my husband packed everything and said we are going down stairs. One of the works on the floor cut us out so we could leave and we had to wait out there until the elevator came the workers outside asked if we wanted masks (because they were painting and they had them). So, I thought you are telling me that they thought it was ok to put people on these floors, breathing this stuff in when they workers had things because it isn't stuff that you should be. So, we get down stairs the guy at the desk was a jerk that i was in tears. I explained that this was ok and they whole issues that I had. He said we because we upgraded you that should make you happy. I told him the point is that this should have never happened in the first place. I would have never stayed here if i had known and further more I didn't appreciate the tone that he was making it sound like I asked to be on that floor in the first place. We get to the new room and while it was nice I was so upset about everything that happened. So our first day was completely ruined and the customer service was horrible. On Thursday of our stay I called to speak to a manager because I was in a elevator and someone that had the same problem was telling us that they didn't have to pay for the day and was moved into the same kind of room we were. So I called downstairs and I was told they couldn't do anything plus they put the complaint in as just a noise complaint not as what it was. I didn't appreciate the customer service, the fact that they thought that this was ok to do and then the fact that they treated people differently. I will never stay there again and I will make sure that my friends and family doesn't either. Just a side funny note, the floor was done two days later. So I would say that maybe they just shouldn't have put people on the floor until they were done. If you want to see the video I did post on their facebook site.

allReviews.title: Lipstick on a Pig plus Extreme Resort fees!
allReviews.text: Stayed here Monday through Wednesday, you walk in and it's fairly modern stylistically, but as the old saying goes you cant just slap lipstick on a pig. Staff was fine, courteous and nice. The experience however was awful! We went up to our room on the 35th floor and from the moment we stepped off the elevator you can just kind of tell that the stay wasnt going to go well. From the peeling wall paper, to the scratches on the walls down the hallway, to the missing arrows on which way the rooms were counting up/down this is hardly the 4 and a half stars priceline rated it at and 4 stars that trip advisor rates it as. The room, again, just like with the hotel lobby, you walk in and are relatively impressed by the ambiance, the modern look, and the view.. or lack there of. Well lets start simply by saying if you're not a shorter person the functionality of this room is completely lost on you. Unfortunately i'm taller so everything is a strain and a pain in order to use. Then you get to actually using the room for it's functionality and that again is where the problems arise. The floors were dusty and could use a cleaning, the decor has seen better days and looked to be beat up (chips, scratches, dirt everywhere), the furniture looked to be purchased second hand with the amount of fabric rips and upholstery missing. There are 3 tv's in the room.. 1 didnt work/had no remote to the second tv was a standard old lcd tv and the third was right in your face in the bathroom. The rain fall shower however was nice, but it wasnt designed properly so unless you messed with the shower head you were going to have a pool escaping your shower into the main room. The kitchenette was fine.. standard amenities there.. the dual fridge was ridiculous.. The top of which being the mini bar with extremely dated products inside of it. The bottom being a college style dorm fridge which clearly hasnt been properly cleaned in some time because it smelled of something fierce. Now onto the resort fee.. I'm sure everyone and their mother has complained about this evil of Las Vegas so i will not waste my time other than to say. $25/day plus tax for wifi that was ridiculously slow for only 1 device per room?! took this bit of Vegas thievery to unprecedented heights!!!.  Long and the short of it, I fell into the allure of the star rating on websites and wanted to stay in a nicer place this is one that I will not be attempting to stay at ever again. No, thank you! Keep it!

allReviews.title: Nice hotel but bad management
allReviews.text: This place could easily get better ratings if not for the following reasons:- the rooms are nice but already showing signs of wear - the chairs all have scratches and marks on them, the floor has scratches all over it, and the furniture is definitely looking a bit sad. - the room hasn't been cleaned very well, the toilet smells pretty bad (as if it hasn't been properly washed in quite a while), and the everything has minor smears or stains on it.- took a very long time to check in - definitely more than 2 attendants needed at key check in times- the wifi sucks!! Only one device per room allowed?? And it's quite slow. Considering you pay a $25 resort fee which includes "complimentary wifi". So basically $25 for slow wifi on one device.- WORST OF ALL: the pool was closed all three days due to a "private event". I've paid good money for this hotel and the facilities that come with it, especially the pool, and it's unacceptable that I can't use it on any of the days that I stay here. Not cool.Like I say - nice hotel, but a lot of things wrong with how it's being run.

allReviews.title: Quiet Reprieve From The Strip
allReviews.text: Since I do not gamble, I wanted to be in a non-casino atmosphere and not right on the strip. After reading some of the negative reviews, I was a little concerned about what I'd find upon arrival. My room was a studio suite on the 36th floor and happened to be a nice view of the strip and mountains to the east. The room was plenty big for one person. The bathroom was immaculate, although I'd have to say the lighting was poor. It was hard to see to shave even with the lighted magnified mirror. The only other negative aspects about the place were that some of the furniture was a little worn, which was no problem and there was thick dust on the shelf of at least one of the closets. The wood part of the floor could stand to be refinished. Also, the feather pillows had an unpleasant odor. At first, I was afraid this might be body odor, but the more I thought about it, I think it was actually the feathers that stunk. It has been many years since I've slept with feather pillows and it might be that they get foul with age. I did not bother to complain because I could position myself to not pick up on the odor. The more I think about it, I probably should have requested new pillows. The room was quiet at night which is what is very important to me in order to sleep. I tried to relax in the mornings at the pool area. The second day the weather was bad so that put an end to that. The third and last day there were shards of glass found around the pool so the decision was made to drain the pool, sweep or vacuum it out and refill. This would be at least a 36-hour project, so there went that relaxing morning. You could get in the hot tub, but I didn't want to do that in the middle of the desert!! I did not rent a car. The company that I booked the trip with sold me a roundtrip shuttle ticket from the airport to the hotel. You can go to The Palms and catch their shuttle to the strip which leaves every half hour between 11 AM -8 PM. They drop you off at the Forum Shops at Caesars. I would catch the city bus at night on Flamingo between Caesars and Bellagio to return to The Palms. I'm sure you could do the reverse route if you wanted to go to the strip before 11:00 AM. You will encounter the casinos and smoke when you go over to The Palms. Most of the eating places near Palms Place are actually at The Palms. I ate breakfast over there every morning and would sometimes get a late night snack. You have a covered area between the towers where part of the walkway has moving sidewalks, but not all of it. Walking does not bother me. I would recommend Palms Place, especially if you want to get away from the casino atmosphere for the most part and the madness of the strip.

allReviews.title: I loved my king suite!
allReviews.text: Not sure why there is such a mixed bag of reviews on the Palms Place but for my 1 night stay it was awesome! I walked into my room & was floored by the huge bed, sunken jetted tub & shower that had a rain shower head as well as a regular one... Kitchen was great, it was more of a time share type of room with a stove, and dishwasher along with a toaster/microwave and coffee coffee maker. Had a large king bed & sleeper couch, 2 flat screen TVs and a big desk area along with lots of closet space. Had a nice balcony but it just overlooked the parking garage. This place has a walkway to the Palms Casino for any gambling... I also went to their theater to catch an afternoon movie, very comfy. They have an IMAX theater but my movie was y showing in there. Lots of choices to eat at their "food court" and several different restaurants to choose from on the property. They have a spa & pool although I didn't use them I could see them from the pool area. Pool has cabanas you can use too... I would recommend this place and will try to come back for a longer stay to try out all the amenities.

allReviews.title: Never again
allReviews.text: Was recommended to try palms place for our stay in Vegas. We spent the money and booked a one bedroom suite for a 7 night stay - our stay lasted less than 24 hours. Checked in and immediately noticed the suite had an unpleasant odour. Before making a call we had knocks on our door on 2 occasions offering a deodorizer due to complaints about an odour (1st alarm bell went off realizing this wasn't just us being picky). After 2 hours and a 14 hour flight no improvement. Call made to the front desk and suspicions were confirmed when we were asked if it was a sewage smell - rather than being offered an alternative maintenance was sent up to pour something down the drains.  Went for dinner and returned back to the odour worse than when we left. A call to the front desk and we asked to be moved - we were told to hang tight and expect a call back immediately. 30 minutes later and being put through to 3 different people at 10.30pm we were told that we could move to one room for the night and would have to again be moved after the first night or stay until another suite became available - during this unhelpful phone call I was able to book a similar room in a much better hotel on the strip. Due to the complete lack of customer service we advised we were leaving and that someone from the bell desk would be up to assist. Another 30 minutes and phone call later someone finally came to the door. The bell hop was lovely and complained about the smell the minute he walked in and asked why we weren't offered another room after our first complaint - completely understood that there was no way my husband, son and I should have to tolerate the odour. Prior to leaving we were advised that a refund would be made for pre payments that had been made. One week later after checking the credit card statement I was quite shocked to see that we hadn't need refunded but charged again for another night and a resort fee. Several phone calls later and having to explain the situation this was eventually rectified. Am pleased to say that despite the rocky start we thoroughly enjoyed the rest of our stay in Vegas at our usual hotel on the strip. As for palms place - it will always be known by the name given to it by my son "the stinky palms" It's a shame as a frequent traveller to Vegas had the experience been better we would have returned once a year. Unfortunately for an establishment that is supposed to pride itself on it service and presentation our experience was quite the opposite.

allReviews.title: I wouldn't recommend it to my friends
allReviews.text: We were disappointed with our suite as it was very dirty (dusty furniture and the floor, dirty windows, dirty mirrors and walls in the bathroom), some of the lamps didn't work. Pool area wasn't clean either. Though the management tried to solve these problems for us, we wouldn't stay at this hotel again. Besides, you have to pay for the internet and amenities when checking out, even if you don't use them..As for the good points, it is quiet, you can relax at the spa salon and the pool. The pool area could be much better though. We liked the dining places and bars in the neighbor Palms Casino Resort. I should also mention that the buffet was good and it's staff was super friendly and helpful.Overall, it's ok, but not 4,5*.

allReviews.title: Great Experience
allReviews.text: We got a studio suite. We spent a day at the pool, the staff there was wonderful with great poolside food and of course drinks. All the hotel staff as well as casino staff that we encountered was great. The housekeeping was wonderful, always managed to get to our room no matter how late we slept in or any odd hours we kept. Off the strip, if thats a factor for you.

allReviews.title: Lovely Suite but lacks amenities and service
allReviews.text: Stayed here recently and the suite was phenomenal, however, this didn't seem quite like a hotel but more of an apartment. Housekeeping was wonderful to interact with but when it came to the front desk staff or the concierge, it truly lacked any feeling of staying in a hotel. The front desk couldn't recommend a place that would deliver dinner, any restaurants were a good 10 minute walk through the casino and once there limited in food.  Tried to order a plain grilled cheese at a place in the casino, however, no one would take my order. It's pretty bad when the front desk recommends papa john's as a pizza place. The location is a bit away from everything and was around a $15 cab ride to anywhere down the strip.

allReviews.title: Nice Modern Place!
allReviews.text: Very large and comfortable suite, loved the idea of having a kitchenette! Clean, modern and with class. The only thing I'd ask from them is to keep the pool hours of operation longer as it closes super early at 6 pm. The rest was great!

allReviews.title: Better every visit
allReviews.text: I have stayed here 3/4 times in the past year. can't say enough great things about the property. rooms are Huge and beautiful. If you appreciate a beautiful room and bathroom. This is the place. Pool scene is relaxed and chill. Casino is a short walk over . Food on fl 6 is epic ( burgers are choice). Helpful staff. Easy parking.  It's my favorite suite hotel so far.

allReviews.title: Past reviews are true, slowly going down
allReviews.text: All the recent past reviews are pretty spot on when it comes to this place declining slowly. The rooms are OK and getting to be very dated. It's all the little things that are not being maintained. Rusted, grimy shower head, dated IPad radio port, non fictional balconies and stains on the furniture. If you find a good deal online for this place, book it, but if there's anything on the step around the same price range, look elsewhere.

allReviews.title: What a ghetto pool area....
allReviews.text: Was here at the end of August 2015. The pool area is terrible. If you want run down cabanas with missing seat cushions that look like they haven't been cleaned in a year, pool lounge chairs with disgusting stains and cigarette burns then stay here.....very very disappointing. I will not be back.

allReviews.title: Nice amenities, poor management
allReviews.text: The room was fabulous and the amenities were amazing; however, our trip took a turn for the worse when we went to bed and it smelled like a farm.  Turns out they were new feather pillows and the hotel hadn't taken the time to air them out before putting them on a bed.  The smell was so bad that my hair even retained the smell after a shower.  We soon found more issues when room service calls were not completed.  One request took 5 attempts and 2 days to complete.  (we just asked for a frying pan for the kitchen in our suite).  Another issue is that the wifi never worked in the room. But the absolute worst thing that happened was on the day we checked out, we were told that we could still use the spa after checkout (same day).  So we checked out early and headed to the spa; however, when we got there they told us that because we checked out we were not able to use the facilities.  We had specifically asked before we checked out and were very disappointed by the whole thing.  Overall, I would not recommend.

allReviews.title: Seen Better Days
allReviews.text: It's sad to see how this hotel is not being maintained like it used to. New owners took over the hotel and letting it get run down. Rooms are ok but furniture is showing wear and tear and the hotel is not what it once was. Pool is nice but chair cushions are stained and need to be replaced and cabanas look they need an overhaul. You can get good rates on rooms and it is a quiet hotel

allReviews.title: Very disappointed!
allReviews.text: Wow, Harrahs took this place over a few years ago and has let it go. This use to be my "go to place" but not anymore. I love the location, room/balcony views and pool area. But i have noticed over the past three years that no money is being invested in this place and the condition of the rooms i have stayed in are dilapidated. I think they are waiting for the next investor to come along and re-do everything.The pics being shown on Yelp appear to be 3-7 years old. My suite has dirty/stained couches and draperies, no utensils or serving wear in the kitchen, a 7-8 year old coffee pot, chipped and dirty walls, doors and paint, outdated furnishings and decorations. The hotel itself has dirty carpets and the pool lounges cushions are gross; stained, weathered and many cigarette hotels. I feel sorry for the staff, mainly the housekeepers, who probably hear the majority of the complaints and the desk staff, who have no control over the management who probably dont care. Sad for me, going to try a hotel on the strip next, will let everyone know what I find.And Simons restaurant is now a cafe that does not serve breakfast and has limited hours.

allReviews.title: Sadly Steadily Declining
allReviews.text: I have stayed here several times  I really enjoyed previous stays, but I have noticed that the decor and service has slipped a little with each visit.  This last visit however it was definitely noticeable.  The wifi, included in the resort fee, is always a challenge.  It is difficult to sign in and keeps expiring at odd times.  In the room i had the furniture was dated and worn,  Even a cigarette burn in the leather chair.  How you you get a cigarette burn in a non-smoking hotel?  The shower controls only allowed for one temperature of water.  Probably the most irritating thing was the lack of service from housekeeping.  On my second day there I left my room and was gone all day.  I had turned on the housekeeping light and yet when I returned that night my room had not been touched nor was any effort made to do so.  I will have to think long and hard before I return.

allReviews.title: Past its prime?
allReviews.text: I did not have a enjoyable experience when i visited the hotel.I have been to Vegas countless times and i have allways wanted to stay at this hotel.The checiking in process went smooth enough. But from the start i reacted to the LONG waiting time to get an elevator. The room we had was nice and had a decent view (if you look away from the parkingfacility two floors down). But the room itself was not cleaned properly. Leftover clothes from the previous visitors. The shower was just plain dirty and the floor in the living room had several nail clippings from the previous guests. I called downstairs and asked if they could offer me an upgrade. Instead of asking why i wanted to change rooms the guy answering plainly said "where fully booked" and gave me the impression that he wanted to hang up.We then ordered in room dining which arrives in a brown paper bag. That does not give the luxury feeling that the resort wants you to have. The order was wrong and we had to wait an additional 15mins for the rest of our food.I the decided that i would change hotels. I called downstairs and asked if i could cancel the rest of my stay. "call expedia" was the short response i got (i had booked via hotels.com). He hung up on me without saying goodbye in a proper way. I cancelled my reservation and left for another resort.When i got back home i sent an email woicing my concerns and my dissatisfaction. It has now been three weeks and no reply.A disapointng stay.

allReviews.title: Upscale modern,great value (but a long walk from the Strip)
allReviews.text: The good: we had a nice view of the Strip from our room.  Room was upscale modern, very spacious.  Weird little kitchen area.   Fancy bathroom fixtures.  Very clean.  Front desk service was warm and personal.   The meh: your parking options are valet (and a long wait to pick your car up), or a seriously long walk to the Palms casino parking garage.  It is also a long and not very pedestrian-friendly walk to the Strip.Great value for the money at the rate we got.

allReviews.title: No longer a loyal customer
allReviews.text: Around 2 years ago, when I first stayed at the Palms Place, it was great. I liked its location and modern design.I've been back several times after that and without fail, each experience has been worse than the last.There is always something that does not work. Some pieces of furniture (bedside lamp, desk lamp, even a coffee table) will just be missing sometimes. Several light fixtures will not work, some of the already few outlets don't work, forcing me to connect my devices in awkward locations.During my last stay, I noticed several things in the room either be missing or broken. (missing bedside lamp, desk lamp, and some of the few lamps that were there did not work. make-up mirror did not work.)I was fine with it. I knew that's how Palms Place is now, and I booked anyway. (though I do always hope.)But the bathtub did not work. No water at all. I called about it, they sent up a guy quick enough. He quickly diagnosed the problem as something that can't be fixed easily and offered me room change. Fine. Now how I wanted to spend the night, but I do want a working bathtub for the remaining three nights.I pack all my stuff back up. Later, another guy came up to give me keys to my new room.I grab all my stuff and went to my new room. The room had other peoples' stuff in it. The room was occupied! I was given KEYS TO A PREOCCUPIED ROOM. That is scary for me, and even scarier for those people.Unbelievable. I went back down to my old room, put my stuff down and went to the front desk. They apologized and gave me the correct room keys and comp coupons for the drift spa. I told them I won't have a use for it, but I was told they have absolutely no food comps.Fine. But did you know my new room doesn't have a coffee table?She said she will either bring me a coffee table, or at least call me if none is available.No table, no call.Oh, and the pillows reeked of dried up saliva upon my arrival. Had to ask for new ones. They were quick enough to arrive, but I shouldn't have to check if my bed and linens are fresh upon arrival. New pillows were very uncomfortable, with the feathers poking through and poking my face while I tried to sleep.So, once nice, but now poorly maintained rooms with plenty of missing/non-working furniture/lights.Quick and friendly staff, but mistakes and broken promises.Came with my wife for a little vacation. Left with less money and more headaches.

allReviews.title: Poor Customer Service
allReviews.text: I have stayed in this hotel on 2 other occasions and had an excellent time and even raved to friends about how it was such a great place to stay.  This last trip was extremely disappointing.  First the wait to check-in was less than ideal since they only had one person working the front desk.  Soon another staff member came, so i'll give them credit for realizing an issue and addressing it.  The next issue was that the room we were assigned to smelled like wet dog, very strongly.  The bell man even came into the room and noticed the smell and said he would hold onto our bags until we got a new room.  I called the front desk to request a room change, which didn't seem like it would be an issue as we arrived early enough in the day.  They said they would call us back and it took about 20min for them to call back and state that they had no other rooms they could possibly move us to, but they would send housekeeping to freshen up the room.  So we wait for housekeeping to come and work a miracle.  After about 20minutes we call to inquire when they would be arriving, they say right away and we wait another 15min for someone to arrive.  When housekeeping arrived they had a watered down bottle of febreeze that they sprayed around the room.  This is what housekeeping told us it was, "a watered down bottle of febreeze."  Needless to say this did not fix the issue.  The housekeeping guy even said it smelled and we should ask for a new room.  I call down again to the front desk and share that the room still smells and that housekeeping even said that it did after he used the febreeze.  The woman from the front desk then put me on hold for about 10 minutes, when she returned she said that she checked what i said with housekeeping and now they would move us to another room.  I am sorry i found this so insulting. So basically they did have a room to move us to initially but instead lied and said they didn't.  I would have been less upset if they initially said hey let us try to fix the problem first before we move you to another room, the fact that they lied and then felt the need to fact check what I was saying was absurd.  So then we wait another 45minutes to actually get moved to a new room.  This was because they didn't seem to know who was doing what, we had to call the front desk again to follow-up, then wait for another call from the front desk in which they said that the bell man would bring up our new key and our bags.  So we continue waiting and finally the bell man arrives with our keys...but no bags.  I share with him that we were told he would have our bags too and he said he didn't know anything about that, so we call again and finally our bags arrive.  The next thing that was not ideal was the ability to get a taxi.  We soon learned that we needed to plan to leave an hour to an hour and a half early to go anywhere on the strip.  I even attempted to call valet before we got down there to see if we could ensure a taxi was down there when we came down, but no one ever answered the phone.We wanted to use the tub, but it had no stopper so we had to wait about 30minutes and call housekeeping twice to get one.  We also noticed that the furniture in the room had become dated and worn.  Everything from chairs peeling to chairs missing a foot, to actual pieces of furniture in the room missing.  When we got our new room we could tell that there used to be a coffee table in the room (all of the other rooms appeared to have them) but it wasn't there.  The coffee table wasn't a big deal, changes the aesthetic, but I  can't say I had intentions of using it.  Lastly, housekeeping seems to have the oddest schedule for cleaning the rooms.  The next day we went to the pool, both my friends and i made sure our light was on to request that our rooms were cleaned.  We get back around 4pm and only one of the rooms had been cleaned and housekeeping was not even in the other room to clean it. They seemed to be very disorganized for a luxury/boutique hotel.  They also seemed to be unapologetic for their shortcomings.  I think with all of the issues we had to deal with we received one "sorry about that".  The waiting was ridiculous all the way around.  I am understanding to the fact that a hotel may encounter an issue or two, but the way that they address it and with what sense of urgency is what makes a difference.  If they had been more attentive and somewhat apologetic I would not have left so disappointed.  We were there for a short trip and wanted to jump into having fun at the casino or pool when we first arrived, but all of the issues, and poor customer service precluded us from doing so.  I will say that I enjoyed their pool and I like that palms place is a respite from the crazy of vegas, it provides the opportunity to indulge in both relaxation and quiet but still venture out into the lively vegas strip when you choose.

allReviews.title: What a Nightmare.
allReviews.text: I intended to buy a property in the building and decided to first stay for a long weekend to test out the service and noise level. The building appears to be attractive and convenient  but it becomes quickly clear that it is one endless disaster of cheap decor, awful and abusive service and horrible attitudes. I would have imagined given my level of interest and desire to invest in the property - a minimum standard if service would have been met. I imagined incorrectly. Included in my stay was a visit from EMT/Security after I slipped on the marble floor in kitchenette that flooded after poor workmanship /wear and tear on grout causing a leak from bathtub in bathroom through the wall. I was billed (via my room charge) for several charges which I didn't authorize nor was the front desk able to produce receipts for (my guess is that another guest was allowed to abuse my account.) Throughout my 4 days at PalmsPlace, I requested my room be cleaned every day. I literally did not have my wishes honored once. In fact, I asked 4 times for towels on the third day and then arrived at 6 PM. At the end of my stay, I asked that my $476 billing be adjusted (after all, I also gambled here and patronized/tipped well at each of the restaurants.) Given my frustration over the dilapidated and unclean room, the lack of concern and my loyalty, I was told I would get follow up from Viktoria, the manager. Not surprisingly at all, this was also untrue - DAYS LATER. This is just the tip of the iceberg. Please consider my experience when staying here - if this is how the property treats someone who is willing to become a tenant, I can't imagine how awful a short term guest is treated. See photographs of filth/unkempt property for yourself.

allReviews.title: Off the strip, a nice getaway from the madness.
allReviews.text: In town with my lady for EDCLV, which should let you know that I came in town to sleep and rave.Nice hotel close enough to walk to the strip while still being away from the rowdy drunkards.The room was nice and comfy for two people. The only thing I would change is the fact that the shower didn't have a door. Other than that we got beautiful views of the mountains in the background. The pool is nice and the gym is there if needed.

allReviews.title: horrible hotel - unless you are below 25 years
allReviews.text: i stayed here for a trade show and i have stayed in hostels much better than this hotel. it is simply horrible and noisy with drunk girls and boys running around in the hallwaysunless you are friends on party vacation or for bachelor parties stay awaythoams

allReviews.title: Perfect place to relax
allReviews.text: I was a bit skeptical after reading some of the reviews but I am glad we gave it a try.The location is perfect if u want to be near but not on the strip. The have a shuttle that runs every half hour and if u can't wait a cab is under $10 depending on where you want to go. Check in was easy,I was expecting a hard time since it was 10am but there were no issues. The studio has plenty of space the only downside is the balconies on the higher levels are locked. The pool is very relaxing at Palms place and you will also have access to the larger pool at the Palms. The Concierge helped us get tickets to shows. There is a movie theatre on site along with several dining options so it really was the perfect place to get away from the strip!

allReviews.title: Good stay but not 5 star
allReviews.text: We were looking for a cheap stay in Vegas but that still had a pool etc and for that purpose this hotel met our needs. However I would be disappointed if I was expecting a 5 star hotel. It just wasn't quite that good. Rooms were really nice but had to request any cooking utensils and kitchenware from different places. We had a balcony butte weren't allowed to use it. The hotel is just about walking distance to the strip (1.5 miles ish) if you don't mind a walk but it's down a very busy road. There are shuttle buses every half an hour however they stop running after 8pm which is not much use to get back.  A taxi is around $10-15 depending on the traffic. We stayed in the palms place building, the staff were really helpful and the pool was really good however got a little busy in the afternoon and you might have to wait for a sunbed. The other pool at palms casino was much bigger and really nice but very strict on what you can take in (my partner wasn't allowed his go pro and had to walk all the way back to the room to take it back). Only problem is drinks are really expensive. If I was going to Vegas again then would stay closer to the strip. Oh and one more annoying thing - you only got wifi for one device per room!!! Very frustrating.

allReviews.title: Honeymoon road trip
allReviews.text: Great stay, modern, clean and lots of facilities at the hotel. The Hotel staff at the front desk are really helpful and sought to get together anything that would make our stay even better. They offered us some great options for upgrades and really made our last few nights in the USA fantastic.

allReviews.title: Stayed at Palms Place Suite and loved it!
allReviews.text: Loved my Suite at the Palms Place Hotel. Stayed on the 53rd floor facing the Strip so we had GREAT views. Didn't need to go to the Stratosphere or High Roller cause we could see everything from our room. It's off the strip and def not close enough to walk but the shuttle from 11am-8pm that dropped off at the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace was convenient. After 8pm, cab is the easiest way to get back unless you figure out the RTC Bus System.The hotel/hallway is very dark/low lighting but it goes with the modern secluded theme. The room looked exactly like the photos. Very sleek and modern. The cable TV could def go for an upgrade but I liked having 2 TVs (one by the bed, the other in the living room area.) Bathroom was very nice, loved the overhead and handheld shower head with the tub. Felt SO refreshed after my showers! TV in the bathroom didn't have a remote but I used it maybe once.The cleaning staff was very ice. We overslept one night and missed the housekeeping but we caught them in the hall and they came back and refreshed our room for us. Drift Spa had a 85$ special for a 50 minute massage and I'm SO glad I went! Loved their spa.Restaurants were okay. We ate at the buffet for breakfast (we weren't hungry enough to enjoy it but the food was just okay.) And had breakfast at the 24/7 Cafe which was pretty good and not too overly priced. We also ate at the Hooters in the hotel..(I know....) but service and drinks were pretty good. Casino was pretty big and service was nice. Overall it was worth the price and it was definitely a lot cheaper than the other hotels on the Strip with rooms that weren't half as ice as Palms Place.

allReviews.title: New Favorite Vegas Hotel
allReviews.text: Best hotel I have stayed in Vegas. Other 5 star hotels I've tried are Trump and Vdara, but I'd say Palms Place exceeds them both. Although the location is a bit off from the strip the hotel is cheaper than other suites. The lady who booked our stay was amazing. Didn't even know she upgraded us to a complementary one bedroom suite! Upon opening our room, I was surprised and amazed at the place! The room was very modern with contemporary furnishings. Includes a king size bed and a queen size sofa bed. The shower was also huge (3 shower heads total)! And the view, which surrounds the living room with a floor to ceiling window was breathtaking! The neighboring Palms casino (which has a food court and movie theatre) was very convenient. The cleaning staffs were friendly and helpful. Overall love the place and hope to experience another great stay in the future.

allReviews.title: Barbara
allReviews.text: We were put here  when our reservation were not available at the Palms Hotel. What a surprise, it was huge with kitchen, bath and 1/2, washer/dryer.  Beautiful panoramic view, breathtaking.  Clean and very luxurious. We had a sectional in living room.

allReviews.title: Quick Return to Vegas
allReviews.text: Decided to stay at a different hotel away from Strip to avoid crowds/& noise.  We were impressed w/room size & spacious bathroom.  But just as others have expressed, they're out to get any amount of money anyway they can.  We arrived early before 3:00pm check-in time & although the 1st desk clerk to help us was professional & did offer advice, she was very fast to charge an "early" check-in fee of $33! Reservation was prepaid,so the $33 was just extra they made. I was to tired to argue. (I had already had that argument w/the airport Hertz car rental person who attempred to take liberty of "upgrading MY car choice into a safer vehicle "!  3 main issues w/the place, a/c can't handle cooling suites floors 37 up. Ceiling fans are much needed!!- Entire place to include suites is in "dire need" of much better lighting. - Hotel staff is also in "very dire" need of Positive Customer Service "- No Matter Who Owns the Place!!  Check - out desk clerk reacts to requests "as a bother" vs "a privilege to have U stay ".  Don't expect much for  $25 a day resort fee. And as far as even a slight suggestion for a room w/a view, not if Ur common working people...

allReviews.title: Great spot
allReviews.text: Overall great spot my suites with tons of room and a great kitchenette with the modern styling very sleek and hip. It is a bit off strip but they do have a shuttle that will take you to Caesar's Palace I think. Also tons of cabs come by so you can usually hitch a ride. Definitely a recommendation if you're going with friends family partying whatever.

allReviews.title: Awesome Customer Service
allReviews.text: My wife and I stayed at Palms Place for a "staycation". The rooms were the same as any other room on the strip with the bonus of a kitchenette. When we went to our room there was a light out in one of the nightstands, no big deal, but i did call to report it. the Engineer showed up to our room in less than fifteen minutes, which was great, but what happened after that was something I hadn't experienced before. About two hours later the director of facilities called to check on the call we had placed, and to make sure we were happy with the service. Of course we were and plan to stay again, and recommend this property for all visiting friends and relatives. Absolutely the best value in Vegas. I can't finish without saying something about the bed, the matresses are amazing. It was like sleeping on a cloud.

allReviews.title: worst service experience at Palms Place
allReviews.text: People say what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, well I must say not in my situation. My bachelorette party with three (3) of my girlfriends turned out to be the worst experience ever at the Palms Place upon check out certainly leaving an after taste of poor service and undesirable experience to return to this hotel. The bellman on shift Monday morning 7/20, ken, who gently detailed my luggage upon check out on the luggage ticket before heading to the strip was very nice and friendly. Upon my return to the hotel to retrieve my luggage to head to the airport, I was assisted by Christian, the afternoon bellman, who assisted us placing all of our luggage in the trunk of the taxi, while getting in it.  To my surprise Christian forgot to place my Louis Vuitton personal bag with the rest of the luggage, which contained my ID in it and my personal belongings in the trunk of the taxi. Once I arrived at the airport, I just couldn't believe I had around 50 minutes to go back and forth to retrieve my bag at the Palms Place, go through airport security and catch a flight to NY.  I hopped back in the same cab from the airport to hear the unfortunate words of the bellman Christian once back at the hotel   " You can either take your bag and catch your flight or wait for someone to contact you as the manager is really busy right now " Seriously? Well, I certainly told Christian I had to leave and catch my flight to NY and left my business card with him at the bell desk. Once I Ieft I just couldn't believe the words I heard from him a few moments ago. No sympathy or apologetic tone towards my situation. No ownership of the situation, no hospitality service and no desire to turn the unfortunate situation around  as a guest who was just there for few days trying to create a memorable experience with my bridesmaids at this property. While back to the hotel, one of my friends  was also trying to get in touch with the manager to find out more about my personal bag and there was a completely run around on behalf of the guest services staff. She had to call multiple times. There was also another gentlemen next to Christian without proper uniform or name tag who seemed not to care about my situation at all as well. I went ahead and told both of them this is unacceptable, especially for someone who also works in the same hospitality industry as you do. Perhaps I should of stayed at one of my hotel  chain properties to really experience the service I was really looking for in Vegas for my first trip. I missed my flight to NY with Delta for a later time at night, missed the return trip with my girlfriends, and spend around extra money on the taxi trip back and forth to the hotel.  Should I end this email with Viva Las Vegas? This is certainly not the service I wanted to experience at the Palms Place. If anyone is interested to mend this situation, feel free to contact me via email or on my phone noted on the reservation.  I would like to personally hear from your hotel leader, GM, on my situation. Please forward me his contact information as well. On the other hand, I  also have to mention some great highlights of my trip ; I really enjoyed the Friday party pool, the pool staff were really approachable, the Ghostbar has the view of the Las Vegas Trip and the security guard was very attentive to all of us once at the rooftop bar on Friday night.  Furthermore, I was really impressed with the impeccable and well maintained facilities of the Palms overall.  As they say it is not about quantity but quality, there is still  room for improvement and it reflects poorly on some of your team members. until this date, 7/30 I have not receive any phone calls nor follow up despite writing emails to the guest service manager; andrea.robertson@palms.com, definitely not a property that prioritize in guest service experiences for their guests.

allReviews.title: Bad Service - Stolen Property
allReviews.text: I thought visitor's to this Hotel should be aware of this...I had personal items stolen from my room and this is hotel's response...buyer beware!Palms Response...Please be advised under Nevada Revised Statute 651.010, an owner or keeper of any hotel, inn, motel, motor court, boardinghouse or lodging house in this State is not civilly liable for the theft, loss, damage or destruction of any property brought by a patron upon the premises or left in a hotel guest room because of theft, burglary, fire or otherwise, in the absence of gross neglect by the owner or keeper.   Consequently, with the evidence we have in hand, we must respectfully deny any and all liability and any requests for consideration.How do you prove an employee of hotel stole your items while you were away...think carefully about this!

allReviews.title: Good value for price & everything Vegas trip needs
allReviews.text: This is my 5th trip to Vegas & I have always stayed at big hotels on the Strip.  In Aug 2014 I stayed at Cosmopolitan.  It was a 24 hour party hotel.  I wanted something quieter for a few days.  Palms Place was $90 and even with resort fee, still a steal.  It was a 600 sq FT apt that gave plenty of space.  Separate pool which small was accommodating.  There were a lot of families given having kitchens and no casino on Site.  It is quiet here and easy walk to Palms hotel with all the bustle.  It seemed like it was pretty low on occupancy between both hotels but we still had great service everywhere.  For our needs, this was a good choice.

allReviews.title: Heaven off the strip
allReviews.text: My wife and I make an effort to stay in a different hotel every time we go to Vegas. This stay may change my mind. You just can't beat the price on a place like this. It was absolutely beautiful. It is off the strip, but since we drive to Vegas, we can drive to anywhere on the strip. Checking in was super easy and everyone was nice. They offered an upgrade to the top level for an extra 25 per night, but we just stayed with the strip view that was offered to us. The view was just amazing! On the 20th floor we could see the entire strip from the stratosphere to Mandalay bay. The room was massive and had everything you would need for a long stay. We were really impressed by how clean everything was. It was interesting having hardwood floors with carpeted area and marble. It felt very modern. The rainfall shower was awesome and so was the giant jetted tub. Easily fits two people. I'm 6 foot and could completely stretch out in it. The lighting of the whole hotel was perfect for whatever the mood. My only knock was that there wasn't a bottle opener. We brought our own drink, but with a mini bar, you'd think they'd have a bottle opener. I called to see if I could have one brought to our room but they just said they'd bring one up if they had one, and I never heard anything back. Oh well... But everything else was just beautiful. The pool area was also nice and quiet. Since it is smaller, I don't think many people want to use it. But it is perfect for us. Totally recommend this place if you want something quieter without a casino .

allReviews.title: Not bad
allReviews.text: I love the location, the fact that it's not on the strip. It's convenient to drive on to Spring Mountain, where all the Asian eateries located. Also traffic is not as bad as the strip and you are just a few minutes drive away from it.After reading all the reviews, I was prepared to paid the resort fee and we didn't use the wifi period! If I'm an international traveller I would not prefer this hotel because I would heavy rely on wifi service. There's a 24 Hour Fitness 6 minutes away or you can wake up early to run on the strip.In terms of the room, spacious enough for a family of four. Bed is pretty comfortable, a lil on the soft side. Nice living area to watch TV. Bathroom was big enough. Our room was pretty clean, didn't have any issues with dirty rooms like others mentioned. Probably came here during midweek so not too busy.My issue with the hotel is the housekeeping service. The first day we were at the hotel, we had to leave really early in the morning, so I didn't put some tip on the table. The next day when we left the hotel around 10 and had the housekeeper light on. We returned around noon and the room still wasn't cleaned, called and they said they'll let them know. Around 2pmish, still no one in sight. we called again and this time someone apologized. We return late night and the room was clean. However, I find this very unprofessional and unacceptable.Overall, this is a decent hotel probably undergoing a lot of managing issues. I would only stay here is I get a good deal. I suggest all the international travelers to stay on the strip or pick a hotel that has unlimited and free wifi.

allReviews.title: An ok place
allReviews.text: Stayed here in their one bedroom suite and the hotel room was fine, but not what I expected it to be and definitely not worth the price. The room service cleaned, but not very well and their pools close at 6pm... Why on earth would a hotel in VEGAS close their pool so early?? And their pools are small. Maybe enough for 50 people or so. We were not impressed. They also do not offer a complimentary breakfast, not even to those who purchased a suite. We will definitely be staying in a different hotel next time we visit.

allReviews.title: Just add champagne
allReviews.text: I love staying at Palms Place.  They are all complete apartments, with kitchen and dining areas.  Off the strip so there is easy access to your car without having to walk through some massive casino.  A shuttle runs to Caesar's if you want the strip activity.  I always stay here.  High count linens, great double shower and sink,  and a bubble tub in the 1 bedroom units...just add the champagne.

allReviews.title: Palms Place, an outlier to the Casino, is a spacious, luxurious, peaceful property, but just steps from the action.
allReviews.text: Palms Place, an outlier to the Casino, is a spacious, luxurious, peaceful property, but just steps from the action.

allReviews.title: Ok hotel but far from everything.
allReviews.text: The only good thing about this hotel is the view of Las Vegas Strip from the bar and club in hotel.This property is not family friendly and only good for young couples that just want to dance and party.We would not stay again because very noisy property away from the strip and no good restaurants nearby.

allReviews.title: Average stay in a dark, dark hotel
allReviews.text: We booked a room at the Palms, but even though we called in and told them we'd be checking in late (around 9 pm), when we got there they said they only had smoking rooms left, but offered us a complementary upgrade to the Palms Place.   The room we ended up getting was basically a studio apartment, with a king sized bed and a pull out queen sleeper sofa.  The room was modern, with a kitchen of stainless steel cabinets, a refrigerator and a small heating plate.  The bathroom was very modern as well, and included a TV.  Overall, the room was a little cold feeling and dark, and the halls of the hotel we're really dark and, honestly, kind of depressing.  I gave the hotel an average rating because, well, it was average.  And the whole thing about only having smoking rooms left?  Not cool.

allReviews.title: I love staying here
allReviews.text: We always receive the best service every time that we stay here.  Everything is always five star, and I have stayed EVERYWHERE on the strip.  Palms is definitely a top 5 fave along with Wynn, Encore, Venetian, and Cosmo.   We stayed at Palms Place in April, and our Penthouse D suite had a Jacuzzi on the balcony overlooking the strip.  It was incredible.  Highly recommend staying at this hotel.  They have everything that you need.   Even the restaurants are outstanding.

allReviews.title: Sweet Suite!
allReviews.text: After 5 nights at The Hard Rock Hotel Las Vegas it was nice to move a bit further away from The Strip to Palms Place Hotel, for a further 4 nights. As far as I believe all the rooms at Palms Place are "suites". Our room was great with a view looking out to The Strip. Small kitchenette with fridge and ice drawer, massive king size bed, sofa area, large shower and massive whirlpool bath. The suite had 3 TVs, including one in the toilet! Room was a short 10 minute trip over to the main part of the Palms complex where the food court, buffet, casino and cinema are. Buffet was great, snow crab legs, seafood, steak, pizza and much more. You can upgrade to include beer and wines too. Cinema is great when you want to escape Vegas madness for a little while. There's quite a lot of kids at this resort, which did surprise me as I'd always considered Vegas as the adults playground.Although the Palms is a little way from the strip, there's a shuttle service (I think 30mins or hourly) that takes you direct to Ceasars Palace.Didn't try any of the hotel's speciality restaurants but Ghost Bar is worth a visit. The views at night over The Strip are spectacular!

allReviews.title: Great Price, Good Location
allReviews.text: This is the 2nd time that we have stayed at Palms Place and have really enjoyed it. It has easy access to the Palms hotel which has many places to eat and their casino. The room that we had was lovely with a little kitchenette and dining area. The room was lovely and spacious, lovely comfortable bed. There is a free shuttle that goes from the Palms to the Strip ( not as often as I would like) but the Rio has a free shuttle service which is close by enough to walk there. I would recommend buying a few groceries off the Strip and keeping them in your room, the restaurants and even coffee shop was expensive ($5.99 for a juice that should be at most $2.50!)I visited the spa and loved the treatments I received. The spa is lovely and very relaxingGreat stay overall, would come back here again.

allReviews.title: Great hotel off the strip
allReviews.text: This place only costs a little more than what the main Palms Hotel charges, but its miles better in quality. The same kind of room on the strip would cost ten times as much for sure. We had a studio but it was plenty big enough for what we needed. Loved the pool here also.

allReviews.title: Good hotel, clean spacious, comfy, but fails on location for me
allReviews.text: Will keep it brief, as i know what its like reading these things:Good points: Clean, large, comfy studio suite, kettle, coffee machine, fridge, safe in room.  stayed in Palms Place floor 51 (very quite).  Lovely jacuzzi bath and rain shower.  Free Shuttle to the strip.  Nice buffet restaurant.Bad points:'Free' Wifi is limited, and payable once you have used your limit.  Expensive drinks around pool = $16 vodka lemonade.Not on the strip - too far to walk. Not much going on outside of resort apart from garage/shop.

allReviews.title: Great Price for What You Get!
allReviews.text: We decided to go to Vegas during Memorial Day weekend but the hotels were expensive that weekend. We can across Palms Place and it was a good price for a suite.  I wasn't expecting much so I was in pleasantly surprised.  The suites are big and decorated very modern.  We asked for high floor with a view and they fulfilled our request. The bathroom was my favorite with a marble jacuzzi tub and a rain shower.  It was easy to access the Casino at the Palms. Plus you don't get the traffic or the amount of people you get when you stay at a resort with a casino or on the strip. We would definitely stay there again.

allReviews.title: Great Stay
allReviews.text: First time stay here was amazing. One big suite to myself? Sure why not!! Everything was great here. Customer service, the spa, house keeping, you name it. I thought it was really cool how they have a bathtub in the bedroom. Kind of different, you know? By the way, the internet sucks on the 12th floor...What I like about this hotel is that this hotel is not located on the strip. It's quieter and not as packed. Even at the Palms, it's not too hectic like all these other new hotels. Overall, hotel is great. Sunset of the strip and mountains looks amazing too.

allReviews.title: Stunning View, but Off Strip
allReviews.text: I know that choosing our stay meant being off strip, but it felt even further off strip than I would have liked. Taking a cab everywhere isn't the cheapest of options...but taking a shuttle is something you have to really plan for. The room was quite amazing. The tub was brilliant and so decadent for me. The kitchen was perfect for making anything I'd want, the couch huge, the bed was so comfortable!!!! The view was spectacular, and the shower was just perfect for waking up. The 2 bathrooms was a nice touch. The fireplace? That was weird to see, but that was only because while we were there it was during a heat wave and was 105 degrees every day. It is quite the walk to the casino through the Sky Tube but...well, that is also something that made it a quieter place to stay, away from the action. The elevators seemed to be quite slow even though it didn't seem busy at the time. Of course, there is a resort fee, which I have come to be quite used to but it is still annoying. Like...what are you really getting out of it? Complimentary wi-fi? No thanks, I'll use my own data since it works a million times better than this "complimentary" wi-fi. Not very complimentary if you are paying for it. But, like I said, it's a staple nowadays to have these lovely resort fees. I did not use the shuttles or the pool, so I am not able to comment on such. I believe I'll most likely stay at the Rio in the future.

allReviews.title: Big lies about complimentary AND paid internet
allReviews.text: We were excited to treat ourselves a bit with the 4.5 star hotel, and while the room was good, there were some major disappointments, the biggest being the Internet.To start with the positives, it was so nice to have a large room. It had a large couch which was nice to look at, but not too comfortable.The shower was amazing, and the tub was huge, and it was nice to have a good deep tub to relax in.Our view was beautiful, as we could see pretty much the whole strip.For the downsides, both of out TV's and our tub weren't working when we checked in. They fixed the TV's, but were unable to fix the constant dripping leak in the tub while we were occupying the room. They said we would need to switch rooms to have a quiet tub, I had already unpacked, so we just strategically placed a towel over the faucet to mute the drips. There was also a cabinet with old food from a previous guest inside. The biggest shocker was the Internet.When you check in, they inform you of the $25 resort fee (which is fine if they provide the value).Below, at the end of this review is what their FAQ's on their website say about the resort fee, specifically saying that the resort fee includes "Complimentary In-Room High speed internet service (faster rates available for additional fee)"Attached is the snapshot of the Internet log-in page when I went to use this so-called free internet.The complimentary internet they speak of is 1 mb of internet, for one device, good only for 12 hours.If you don't know what 1 mb will give you, that will allow you to surf Facebook for 10 minutes, if that. Not exaggerating.The paid option is $15 for two days, but only gives you 10mb.There are roughly 1000 MB's in 1 GB, and the average person uses 2 GB a month.Divide 2000 MB's by 30 days, that is 66 MB's a day. Even if you are the kind of person to only use 1 GB a month, that's over 30 MB's in a day. These crooks are charging you $15 for 10mb to use in 2 days.At first we thought it was a typo on their end, and asked if they meant to say GB's instead of MB's, but nope, they meant MB.High speed internet doesn't mean anything if you use all of your internet in 10 minutes!! It doesn't even cost them anything more to open it up to more data.Why say you offer complimentary Internet if you really don't? And especially when it's not complimentary as it costs $25/day!And at least offer enough internet for us to get some work done if we are willing to pay for it! So what else are they charging you for with the mandatory $25 resort fee? Access to the gym, pools (which close at 5pm), and a shuttle to Caesars Palace.Call me crazy, but most hotels that charge a premium price for your room allow access to the gym and pools for free. And with a big fat lie about complimentary internet, this fee is practically theft.If it weren't for this deception, I would have given a 4-star review, but these crooks just crossed a line in my books. FAQ from the website:The resort fee is a daily fee of $25.00 (plus applicable tax) that is charged at the end of your stay. This is a standard practice at the majority of the hotels in Las Vegas, we promise.The resort fee includes:Complimentary In-Room High speed internet service (faster rates available for additional fee)Complimentary access to Palms Cardio Center & Palms Place Fitness CenterShuttle Service to and from the Forum Shops 11AM-8PM Daily [please note hours may adjust some]Daily Newspaper (available at select locations)Unlimited local and toll-free callsAirline Boarding Pass printingCopies and faxes at the Front Desk and Concierge (does not include color and large print jobs)

allReviews.title: As always
allReviews.text: Me and my bf stayed here for 3rd timeAnd first time at Palms PalceGreatest experience! They gave us one bedroom suite with panoramic view and jetbuth in the bedroom! Loved it!Also environment and stuff were super friendly! We went to the pool,had drinks and some food.

allReviews.title: Leaking.....
allReviews.text: We have arrived there really late and they told us that they were overbooked! Even though we had a reservation already! We had to wait for more than an hour for them to get us any room (not the one we had booked).  Next day they changed us room to a proper one like it was reserved ages ago... The room looked huge and modern. Although the TV in the living room,  and most of the lights weren't turning on... When we needed plates for breakfast it took them more than an hour to bring them and I had to ring them again. View from the room was beautiful. Food in the casino area was okay. Staff was friendly. Valet was fine. But I wouldn't stay here again.

allReviews.title: Great Suite
allReviews.text: We stayed in suite 39321, which was amazing. It had one guest bathroom, with toilet and sink. A washer and dryer. Kitchen with a fridge, two freezers, sink, stove and dishwasher. There was a gas fireplace. A tv in the living room, and a tv in the bedroom. The bedroom also had a bathtub and three large closets. The main bathroom had a double shower, two sinks, a toilet and hairdryer. Throughout the suite there are two large balconies, the bummer is that they are locked with no access. The suite is amazing but it did feel like it wasn't cleaned well. There were fingerprints on the closets, dust and a general sense that things were surface cleaned only.

allReviews.title: Palm Place VS Palm Resort
allReviews.text: At first I did not realize I booked the Palm Place and not the hotel. So the walk to the Palm Place was a bit of a challenge at midnight with my luggage. However when I got to my room I was really pleased. It was big, nice bathroom, plenty of room to work and use my laptop. Next time I will look into booking Palm Place. Jocelyne Toronto Canada

allReviews.title: Palms place
allReviews.text: Best room in vegas!!! We stayed here one night to start our honeymoon off and we wished we booked our entire trip at the palms place. They upgraded  our room to the one bedroom  suite and I fell in love. Absolutely  beautiful!

allReviews.title: It's nice to have the Palms and the Palms Place
allReviews.text: My college friend and I stayed at the Palms Place when we visited Vegas for the Rock n Rio Festival.  The Palms Place is the condo side with a nice pool and dark, quiet lobby.  It was great for us to stay there...room was great...we're not super young anymore but it was also nice to be able to visit the Ghost Bar and Palms Pool for a little rowdiness/fun.  Really enjoyed our stay

allReviews.title: First time "off" strip
allReviews.text: When we first arrived the Palms Place we were a little freaked out.  Being used to large expansive, bright lobbies, this was small and dark.  After a say or so, it was not so displeasing.  The room was very nice, large with a nice view of the strip.  We were a little disappointed we were not allowed to out on the balcony...it was one reason we chose the room.  The staff was helpful when needed but otherwise left you alone.  Pool are was OK, getting run down, we had booked a cabana then cancelled when they seemed dingy.  Overall, it really grew on us and by the end we loved it.

allReviews.title: In need of a makeover
allReviews.text: We stayed here because it was the designated hotel for my sons lacrosse tournament. The hotel reminds me of the 1970's. It's in need of a serious renovation. We stayed in a one bedroom suite. The size of the rooms are awesome. The layout not bad either. It's just that everything looks worn. The carpet, couches, bathrooms etc. We ordered room service which was ok. All in all I wouldn't stay again. There's too many better options in vegas. If they renovated I'd consider staying again.

allReviews.title: Clean, Convenient, and Comfy
allReviews.text: My overall experience was quite pleasant, considering I wasn't there entirely for a vacation. I loved the humongous bed, all three TVs, cushion-covered sofa, clean bath tub, and the chic kitchen table.  It was the apartment experience I hoped to get when I booked the place (despite the lofty "resort" fee imposed on the property) and more. I felt like a wealthy local sipping wine covered in cushions while watching the sunset. Getting your dishes washed everyday was also a big luxury! That being said, there are definite downsides. The hotel only provides wifi on ONE electronic and as a person traveling with a laptop and a smart phone, it was quite frustrating. Also, I couldn't get most of the living room lamps and lights in the bathroom to work properly, and it took a considerable time to get it fixed. How poorly managed is this place? Anytime I asked for anything, should it be a bowl or something trivial, it would take ages, providing the ultimate apartment manager experience as well. You wouldn't think an actual "resort" management team would be like your apartment manager! Checking-in took eons as well not because the process was long, but because I had to wait in line with only one working receptionist and a handful of rowdy travelers. This place could really use some service training! Clearly, the Palms isn't on the strip and if walking around the strip is something you've been dreaming about, this isn't your hotel. Shuttles don't run too often, taxis are a rip-off, and driving would be lame because what's Vegas without alcohol? On the other hand, due to the location it was rather quiet and relatively more affordable for what it offered. I would go back just to relax like a local.

allReviews.title: Memorial Day Weekend
allReviews.text: Arrived from the airport Friday Around 9pm got a taxi to the hotel and from the Moment of arrival til departure I had a wonderrful experience..... the Suite was spectacular the decour was very upbeat and worth waking up to for the next four days the marble to tile to carpet combo was breath taking the bathroom was well worth the money I spent the three types of baths you could take was my kinda deal......I had a great time at the pools enjoyed the casino and had a great time in Vegas thanx to the palms place and it's awesome staff ...... A very satisfied Miami Native

allReviews.title: Great Place to stay
allReviews.text: Stayed at Palms Place for Memorial Day Weekend. A great Place to stay!  Everything is upscale.  I felt like the stay was money well spent.  I stayed on the 39th Floor, the elevators were kind of confusing.  I had a friend staying on the 32nd floor, I had to take elevator to 36th floor, then use stairs to get to 39th floor. Besides that, Everything else was great.

allReviews.title: Worse Vegas Hotel experience ever in 15 years
allReviews.text: I had one of there suites for a biz trip, amazing view from my room but the crappiest service ever. Was there for biz after a long day with my crew, hungry, tired. Contacted room service so I could eat and they never picked up. I contacted the Hotel lobby and they claimed could not get through to room service either lol whatever. Plus they charged me $20 dollars just for a cart fee to bring my luggage to my room to add insult to injury. If you want premium service go to the TRUMP, or for the NO.1 vegas hotel experience the Mandarin bar none.P.S. the jacuzzi tub would just start automatically in the night and wake me up.

name: Hilton Grand Vacations Club Paradise Las Vegas

allReviews.title: Excellent property
allReviews.text: All around great property, clean, helpful courteous staff, I would definitly visit again and recommend to friends

allReviews.title: Large room, and clean!
allReviews.text: This hotel was very clean and quiet. The room was large and updated. The bed was very comfortable. Easy access to the Monorail. We practically had the pool to ourselves one morning! Overall, a great stay, and I would definitely stay here again!

allReviews.title: Better Hilton’s in the area at a lower cost
allReviews.text: I stayed at the Hilton at resorts world which I enjoyed a lot but we transferred to this hotel which didn’t have any Hilton benefits as a HHONORS gold member. That is quite a disappointment and the hotel charges a resort fee for what? A pool that looks like a prison with a view on a car park. I guess I didn’t get the concept. We didn’t have breakfast at the hotel but it didn’t look that fantastic.The price was higher than the other better Hilton so that’s what I will opt for next time as the hotel could use a refresh too.

allReviews.title: Hilton Grand Vacations Club Paradise Las Vegas
allReviews.text: Stay was excellent- the 2 bedroom apartment was very comfortable, very well maintained & well equipped. Hotel is a little far from the Strip so the easiest way there  is to take a cab. Not much of amenities - so Resort fee not justified. But as an RCI resort it is very good value for money.Also, the Grocery store at the Resort rather expensive so better to order online.

allReviews.title: Great stay!
allReviews.text: Loved our resort!!  Beds very comfortable, staff friendly and helpful, added bonus was free bottles of water!!  Only downside was the hot tub's heater was broken, so we didn't get to enjoy that, but the pool was wonderful!  Was within a 4 minute walk to a Monorail station!!  Will definitely stay here again!

allReviews.title: Convenient for conventions held at the Las Vegas Convention Center.
allReviews.text: It was very convenient for us since I was in town for an Expo held at the LV Convention Center. I stay there every 3 years.

allReviews.title: Vegas Oct, 2025
allReviews.text: Had an excellent time staying at the HGV Paradise. Resort was clean and provided everything we needed for a great stay. Going in October was a great move because the weather was perfect. Highly recommend this resort.

allReviews.title: Very Nice Hotel
allReviews.text: I had originally left a negative review because of improper fines I received from parking garage. However, after receiving call from Executive Ambassador Donna B, I have changed my review to a more accurate review. As for the parking issue Donna handled it without decency, respect, and most importantly, professionalism. Tho hotel was clean, quiet, and our suite was excellent. Staff was friendly, helpful. They are very close to the monorail. All in all I would stay here again.

allReviews.title: Clean Hotel, No Frills
allReviews.text: This venue is new to the Hilton Grand Vacation Club.  They are still making modifications.  It is not a large property. Although, there is a closed unused outdoor parking lot I'm guessing they will use that to expand the space.  The hotel is very clean. It is suited for families and larger guest parties. It's away from the strip (near the Stratosphere), so consider that when making your travel plans. There is a 24 hour gym. The pool is not that large, but big enough and there is a jacuzzi. There is a lifeguard on duty. Lots of lounge chairs for sunbathing. There's a grill and outdoor couches with a flat screen television for everyone to use. Like most of the Hilton vacation venues there is the Marketplace that sells cold and hot food, breakfast and lunch, even Starbucks coffee. Complementary free parking in a parking structure. No need for tickets. It scans your license plate. You can catch the monorail at The Westgate. It's a little bit of a walk, but doable. I received complimentary bottled water and 3 additional water vouchers.  I had a 1 bedroom suite. All the vacation venues include a washer/dryer, full kitchen (fridge, microwave, dishwasher, oven, cutlery, pots, pans, etc), living/dining area. It was very spacious, & again, clean. The television guide wasn't working to show you what was on, but the hotel said they were working on that function. You can call if you had any concerns & also communicate via text. They were very punctual in response time. Check out is fast and easy. There are no casinos, restaurants or bars at this venue. Again, they are still making modifications to this venue. I don't know if that is in the plans for a future date. There are 2 lounge areas. One of them, has billard and foosball table, and a small arcade.

allReviews.title: Fees
allReviews.text: Watch out for daily resort fees and taxes!  Nothing special here that would justify the fees and taxes.

allReviews.title: Enjoyed our stay.
allReviews.text: Lovely, spacious and comfortable two-bedroom suite included a full kitchen and dining area, spacious living room and three great beds.

allReviews.title: Great Weekend Stay
allReviews.text: Stayed here for the weekend and upgraded to the king suite. Was surprised how spacious it was with big living room space and kitchen. Love the fact that it has washer and dryer. It's really close to Westgate, and convention center. The pool was never too crowded and always has chairs available. The only complaint would be if you are light sleeper, installation is not that good. You can hear toilet flashing, people turning on the sink and footsteps from above. Check in was a breeze and overall would def. return for the convenience of the kitchen and other amenities.

allReviews.title: Great Place - Short Walk From Monorail
allReviews.text: Didn’t really want to stay north of the strip, but I gave it a short.Room was big (had a one bedroom suite with adjoining two bedroom room) and clean. They have a marketplace downstairs if you are missing anything.They didn’t offer me a timeshare meeting because my wife wasn’t with me, I honestly was just interested in pricing.I would stay here again.

allReviews.title: Greatest Place to stay
allReviews.text: So laid back and easy to vacation here. My wife and I are having a very nice time simply doing a Staycation at The Hilton on Paradise

allReviews.title: Nice resort
allReviews.text: Close to the strip. On the edge of the safe area to walk. Close to 2 monorail stations. Garage could use cameras. A guy was peeing at the third floor elevator entrance one morning when I went to the car. Luckily I was taking the stairs.

allReviews.title: No communication
allReviews.text: I booked a seven day vacation since Dec 2024. Checked in May 2025. The resort was under construction, which no one notified me. There was no pool, amenities were missing/lacking. This was Las Vegas 90+degrees weather. They insisted on charging a resort fee even though I am an Owner. It was far away from the strip and cost a lot of money for Uber.

allReviews.title: Pool is closed for renovation
allReviews.text: The staff at this resort was friendly and helpful. Check in took a while, There are a maximum of 3 clerks and we arrived around 6pm on a Friday and there was a wait. When we arrived we found out that the entire pool area was closed for renovation. No pool and no hot tub in May in Vegas. Not good. The rooms have been refreshed, but there is very little drawer space in the large one bedroom. The closet is small because they put in a bench and mirror. (?) No dressers, there are shelves. The outlets in the nightstand are great, until you knock over your water in the middle of the night, then they are a fire hazard. The outlets should be on the wall like they were at the refreshed MGM Grand rooms.

allReviews.title: Vegas Girls TRip
allReviews.text: Hilton Grand is a very nice property.  five minute walk to the tram that takes you along the whole strip. For a decent fee you can ride the tram 24 hrs.  easy like a hop on hop off.  The condo is great two bedrooms and privacy for both.  WIll definitely go back

allReviews.title: Off the strip quiet
allReviews.text: Clean and quiet.  Monorail station nearby.  Uber friendly. BBQ grills were nice and clean. Key card to use the elevator.  Pool under construction.

allReviews.title: Charged for demolished pool
allReviews.text: We were charged a resort fee for the privilege of watching workers demolish the pool.  We had a late airline departure and had planned to laze by the pool before leaving. Not to be.  They said we could traipse down to the Westgate and use their pool.  Lame.

allReviews.title: Charged for demolished pool
allReviews.text: We were charged a resort fee for the privilege of watching workers demolish the pool.  We had a late airline departure and had planned to laze by the pool before leaving. Not to be.  They said we could traipse down to the Westgate and use their pool.  Lame.

allReviews.title: Hilton doesn’t disappoint
allReviews.text: We stayed here April 27- May 1 of 2025 the location is nice and parking is free for guests. Checking in, we got greeted and the staff were attentive and sweet. We stayed in the one bedroom suite. It has a washer and dryer, bathtub, walk in shower, double vanity, a tv in the bedroom and one in the living area, pull out couch, & a kitchen etc. The king size bed is comfortable and clean and the pillows are fluffy and comfortable. The room itself was clean. The AC worked great. They have a store down stairs with all the essentials you need. They also have a game room down stairs. I  always try to stay with Hilton and I have to say, they never disappoint. Thank you Hilton, Pabla J M

allReviews.title: we weren't that impressed
allReviews.text: We never felt unsafe at this hotel, as some recent reviews have said.However we were really peed off that the pool was closed when it stated on our booking that it would be open start of April. BS, it looks like its going to be closed for the forceable future.When we complained they really couldn't care less. pointing out that you can use another resort pool, some 15 minutes walk away.. yea right!Hotel is in need of renovating, it looks tired and worn.Resort charge of $25 per day + tax is a complete rip off. you get nothing except 2 small bottles of water a day, which they use to justify charging you.The only thing 'Hilton' about this hotel is its name, not the standard you would expect.

allReviews.title: Not a Gold Crown - Choose another Property
allReviews.text: There are several issues with this Time Share -1. It needs renovation - it is not a Gold Crown2. There is not enough security as street people have access to the property.3. The pool is undergoing renovation and it is not noted on their website.4. The parking garage is dirty.5. The plumbing has issues.

allReviews.title: Clean hotel but felt unsafe
allReviews.text: My daughter and I recently stayed at this hotel while on vacation visiting from Hawaii.  The first night we checked in our hotel room was robbed while we were out at a show.
